This paper takes the treatment of antonymy in Collins COBUILD Advanced Learner’s English Dictionary (2003) as the point of departure for a discussion about the principles of antonym inclusion in dictionaries and corpus methodologies in lexicology. Ccaled includes canonical antonyms such as good/bad and dead/alive, as well as more contextually restricted pairings such as hot/mild and flat/fizzy. The vast majority of the antonymic pairings in the dictionary are adjectives. Most of the antonyms are morphologically different from the headwords they define and typically do not involve antonymic affixes such as non–, un– or –less. Only just over one-third of the total number of pairs is given in both directions. The principles for when antonyms are included in ccaled are not transparent. We propose an initial top-down corpus-driven method to support decisions about antonym selection and inclusion. http://www.doi.org10.1111/j.1467-9582.2007.00136.x Carita Paradis, Caroline Willners (2007) Antonyms in dictionary entries: Methodological aspects* Studia Linguistica 61 (3), 261–277. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9582.2007.00136.x --[[User:Brett|Brett]] 13:44, 17 November 2007 (UTC) == Blocking 65.25.105.176 == I got temporary sysop permission on this wiki, to block [[User:65.25.105.176|65.25.105.176]] and revert its vandalism. === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/peɪs/}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈpɑːtʃe/|/ˈpɑːke/}} * {{audio|en-us-pace.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} {{usually singular}} The '''pace''' of something is how fast it moves. #: ''The pace of '''change''' has been very, very slow.'' #: ''Today, the pace of '''life''' is so much faster than it used to be.'' #: ''They were frustrated at the '''pace''' of development that was taking place there.'' # {{countable}} {{usually singular}} Somebody's '''pace''' is their speed, usually walking. #: ''He quickened his '''pace''', almost running.'' #: ''The man's long legs forced Kev to pick up his '''pace'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''pace''' is the distance between your feet when you walk. #: ''She stopped three '''paces''' from the table.''
== Verb == {{verb|pac|e}} # Walk back and forth in a small space. #: ''Groups of men, in all imaginable attitudes, were lying, standing, sitting, or '''pacing''' up and down.'' # Set the speed in a race. # Measure by walking.
== Preposition == {{preposition}} # Contrary to the opinion of; Used to express polite disagreement #: ''Nor, '''pace''' Bush, must all countries be with America or against it.''
=== Usage === * This is usually considered to be a foreign word (Latin) and is often written in italics to indicate this: *: Nor, ''pace'' Bush, must all countries be with America or against it.

{{BNC1HW}} === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ɔːlˈrɛdi/}} * {{SAMPA|/O:l"rEdi/}} * {{audio|en-us-already.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|al|ready}}
== Adverb == {{adv}} # [[before]] a [[certain]] time (often now) #: ''When we met, his first wife was '''already''' dead.'' #: ''He was '''already''' well known, but now he's a superstar.'' #: ''Would you like some coffee." "No, thank you. I've '''already''' had two cups.'' #: ''Oh! You're here '''already'''. I didn't think you'd be here until 2:00.''
=== Synonyms === * [[now]] * [[previously]]
=== Antonyms === * [[yet]]
=== Related words === * [[all]] * [[ready]]

*Common block reasons ** [[Wiktionary:Vandalism|Vandalism]] ** Abusing multiple accounts ** Being unkind or rude ** Inserting false information ** Inserting nonsense/gibberish into pages ** Intimidating behaviour/harassment ** Removing content from pages ** Creating bad pages ** Spamming links to external sites ** Unacceptable username ** [[w:Open proxy|Open proxy]] or [[w:Zombie computer|zombie]] (see [[Meta:No open proxies]]) ** Spambot/Malbot *For global purposes ** [[m:Global sysops|Global sysop action]]: to prevent further abuse ** [[m:Global sysops|Global sysop action]]: crosswiki spambot ** [[m:Global sysops|Global sysop action]]: crosswiki abuse

== Noun == {{noun}} # An [[adjective]] that has [[comparative]] and [[superlative]] [[form]]s. #: ''"happy" and intelligent are '''comparable adjectives'''.''
===Usage=== Most adjectives are [[comparable]], meaning that they have a [[comparative]] form and a [[superlative]] form. For example, [[happy]] has the comparative form [[happier]] and the superlative form [[happiest]], while [[intelligent]] has the comparative form [[more intelligent]] and the superlative form [[most intelligent]].
In contrast, [[extra]] is a [[non-comparable adjective]]. You can say "I have an extra pen" but not "I have a more extra pen."
=== Related words === * [[comparable]] * [[comparison]] * [[comparative]] * [[non-comparable adjective]] * [[superlative]]

{{BNC1HW}} === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ʌˈpɔɪnt/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-appoint.wav|UK}} * {{hyph|ap|point}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''appoint''' someone to a [[job]] or [[position]], you give the job to them. #: ''The president '''appointed''' her to [[investigate]] the problems.'' #: ''He has been '''appointed''' to the Supreme Court of Canada.'' #: ''They '''appointed''' him team [[captain]].'' # {{transitive}} If you '''appoint''' a time for something, you choose that time. #: ''They met at the '''appointed''' time.''
=== Synonyms === * [[agree]] * [[pick]] * [[choose]]
=== Related words === * [[appointed]] * [[appointee]] * [[appointment]] * [[point]] * [[reappoint]] * [[self-appointed]] * [[well-appointed]]

{{BNC1000HW}}
=== Pronunciation === ;verb * {{enPR|əsō'shiāt|əsō'siāt}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/əˈsəʊʃieɪt/|/əˈsəʊsieɪt/}}, {{SAMPA|/@"s@USieIt/|/@"s@UsieIt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/əˈsoʊʃieɪt/|/əˈsoʊsieɪt/}}, {{SAMPA|/@"soUSieIt/|/@"soUsieIt/}} * {{audio|en-us-associate.ogg|US}} ;noun (may also apply to the verb) * {{enPR|əsō'shiət|əsō'siət}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/əˈsəʊʃiət/|/əˈsəʊsiət/}}, {{SAMPA|/@"s@USi@t/|/@"s@Usi@t/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/əˈsoʊʃiət/|/əˈsoʊsiət/}}, {{SAMPA|/@"soUSi@t/|/@"soUsi@t/}} * {{audio|en-us-associate-2.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-us-associate-3.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb|associat|e}} {{AVL}} # {{transitive}} If you '''associate''' two things, you think of them as being [[connect]]ed in some way. #: ''People often '''associate''' Einstein with science, but he was also a man of peace.'' #: ''I '''associate''' Thailand with spicy food and beautiful beaches.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''associate''' with someone else, you spend time with them. #: ''Parents are often afraid of their children '''associating''' with the wrong group of friends.''
=== Synonyms === * [[see]] * [[join]] * [[combine]] * [[mix]] * [[relate]] * [[connect]] * [[link]]
=== Related words === * [[associative]] * [[associatively]] * [[association]] * [[disassociate]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} An '''associate''' is somebody that you do business or work with. {{syn|friend|partner|fellow|companion|colleague|ally}} #: ''I have an '''associate''' who might be interested in your product.'' # An '''associate''' member, professor, producer, etc. is one who is connected but at a lower level. #: ''She spent years as an '''associate''' professor before becoming a full professor in 1997.''
=== Related words === * [[associative]] * [[associatively]] * [[association]] * [[disassociate]] * [[society]]

== Verb == {{verb|commit|t}} # {{transitive}} If you '''commit''' something [[illegal]] or bad, you do it. #: ''We have '''committed''' no offense and ask to be freed at once.'' #: ''The people who have '''committed''' this dreadful act should be punished.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''commit''' to something, you agree or say that you will do or participate in something. #: ''The president has '''committed''' the government to improving schools.'' #: ''We must '''commit''' ourselves to the job at hand.'' #: ''After '''committing''' to the project last year, they are now trying to pull out.'' #: ''She wants to get married, but he's not ready to '''commit'''.'' #: ''The government has '''committed''' $10 million towards solving the problem.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''commit''' someone to a place or a process, you send them there, often against their will. #: ''He was '''committed''' to a mental hospital after he tried to kill himself.'' #: ''The judge '''committed''' him to twelve years for the murder.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''commit''' words or idea to something, you record them there. #: ''He '''committed''' the whole speech to memory.'' #: ''She '''committed''' her life's story to paper.''
=== Synonyms === * [[promise]] * [[pledge]] * [[bind]]
=== Antonyms === * [[withdraw]] * [[refuse]] * [[renege]]

[[File:Wiktionary Bots.png|230px|right]] {{shortcut|[[WT:BOT]]}} '''Bots''' are automated scripts or processes which perform jobs on Wiktionary. Usually, they do jobs which would take a long time to do without the bot.
Bots perform their jobs under a different user name than the owner, so that it is easy to tell them apart. Also, bot edits are hidden from pages like [[Special:RecentChanges]] to keep them from flooding the list. To see the bot edits, [{{fullurl:Special:RecentChanges|hidebots=0}} manually add hidebots=0 to your query string], or click "Show bots" at the top of the [[Special:RecentChanges|New Changes]] feed.
The most popular type of bot is called the [http://sourceforge.net/projects/pywikipediabot/ Python Wikipedia Robot Framework] or "pywikipediabot" for short.
== Current bots == These users have been given a "bot flag" and are approved to perform tasks. See [[Special:ListUsers/bot]] for a current list of fully approved bots. This wiki uses the [[m:Bot policy|standard bot policy]], and allows [[m:Bot policy#Global bots|global bots]] and [[m:Bot policy#Automatic approval|automatic approval of certain types of bots]]. Otherwise, there is no formal bot approval process here; place your request on [[Wiktionary:Simple talk]] and a bureaucrat will flag your bot if there are no opposes raised.

revision.text:
{{wikipedia}} {{BNC1000HW}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{UK}} {{IPA|/kaʊnt/}} * {{audio|en-us-count.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-uk-to count.ogg|UK}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{ti verb}} If you '''count''' something, you [[find]] how many there are, usually by looking at them one by one. #: ''OK kids, first everyone get on the bus, and then we'll '''count''' to see that everyone's here.'' #: ''I '''counted''' 43. How many did you get?'' #: ''I '''counted''' up the mistakes and divided by the total.'' #: ''My daughter can '''count''' to twenty by twos.'' # {{ti verb}} If something '''counts''', it is accepted, allowed, or included. #: ''If you use your hands in soccer, the goal doesn't '''count'''.'' #: ''That's not the answer we were looking for, but it '''counts''' as correct.'' #: ''Do you '''count''' the pet as part of the family?'' #: ''Hey, '''count''' me in. I want to play too.'' # {{intransitive}} If something '''counts''', it's important or useful. #: ''If you're trying to lose weight, the kind of food you eat really does '''count'''.'' #: ''The way you dress can '''count''' for a lot when you're looking for a job.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''count''' on somebody or something, you [[depend]] on them. #: ''If you have any problems, you can '''count''' on me to help out.''
=== Synonyms === * [[matter]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''count''' is the [[number]] of something. #: ''Our new-student '''count''' is now up to 124, five more students than last time.'' # {{countable}} A '''count''' is an act of counting. #: ''The study will include a '''count''' of the number of birds on the island.'' #: ''We're going to jump on the '''count''' of three: one, two, three!'' # If you loose '''count''' of something, you can't count them all. #: ''I've lost '''count''' of the number of times she's said that.'' # {{countable}} In law a '''count''' is a [[crime]] that a [[court]] has charged you with. # {{countable}} {{nobility}} A '''count''' is European [[title]], similar to [[earl]].
=== Related words === * [[uncounted]] * [[counting]] * [[countless]] * [[countable]] * [[uncountable]] * [[count down]] * [[count noun]]
[[Category:Law]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/dɪˈrɛkt/|/ˌdaɪˈrɛkt/|/dɚˈɛkt/}} * {{SAMPA|/dI"rEkt/|/%daI"rEkt/|/d3`"Ekt/}} * {{audio|en-us-direct.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|di|rect}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} {{AVL}} # If something is '''direct''', it is [[straight]] and as short as possible with nothing extra in between. #: ''It's a '''direct''' flight from Tokyo to Toronto with no stop in Vancouver.'' #: ''These improvement are a '''direct''' result of the recent changes.'' #: ''In talking to the president, she was more '''direct''': "Your product is making me sick."'' #: ''There is growing contact, both '''direct''' and indirect, between the people.''
=== Related words === * [[directly]] * [[indirect]] * [[indirectly]] * [[directness]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}}; {{context|always with a goal}} If you '''direct''' something somewhere, you [[point]] it there. #: ''He '''directed''' his light to the corner where he heard the noise.'' #: ''Can you please '''direct''' your attention to the screen.'' #: ''Can you '''direct''' me to the station, please?'' # {{transitive}} If you '''direct''' something such as an organisation, you are in charge of if. #: ''She '''directed''' the investigation into the crash.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''direct''' a play or film, you tell the actors how to act. # {{transitive}} If you '''direct''' something, you tell people what to do. #: ''He '''directed''' that the money go to the church after he died.'' #: ''Please close your books where you are '''directed''' to do so.''
=== Related words === * [[direction]] * [[undirected]] * [[director]] * [[directorship]]
== Adverb == {{adverb}} # If you go somewhere or do something '''direct''', you do so by the shortest route without anything extra in between.
=== Synonyms === * [[directly]]

== Noun == {{noun}} # '''Divorce''' is the [[legal]] ending of a [[marriage]]. #: ''Did you know that Richard and Sarah got a '''divorce'''?'' # A [[separation]] of [[connected]] things. #: ''There is a [[geographic]] '''divorce''' between the United States and Mexico.''
== Verb == {{verb|divorc|e}} # {{transitive}} To '''divorce''' is to [[legally]] end a marriage between two people. #: ''The captain of a ship can marry couples, but cannot '''divorce''' them.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''divorce''' someone, you end your marriage to them. #: ''Lucy '''divorced''' Steve when she found that he had been [[unfaithful]].'' # {{transitive}} To [[separate]] something that was connected. #: ''The smaller group voted to '''divorce''' itself from the larger one.'' # {{intransitive}} To get a legal divorce. #: ''Edna and Simon '''divorced''' last year; he got the house, and she got the [[business]].''
[[Category:Marriage]]

{{BNC1000HW}}
===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|/ɛls/; sometimes /ɛlts/}} * {{audio|en-us-else.ogg|Audio (US)}}
==Preposition== {{preposition}} # You use '''else''' to show that something is not the same one as another thing. #: ''OK, he's cute, but what '''else''' has he got?'' #: ''I don't think this one fits me. Do you have anything '''else''' in the same colour?'' #: ''I've told you most of it. There's not much '''else''' I can think of.''
=== Usage notes === * The preposition '''else''' is used only after words beginning with ''some-, every-, any-,'' and ''no-'', after question words, and after ''much, little'', and ''all''.
===Synonyms=== *[[besides]] *[[other]]
===Related words=== *[[elsewhere]]
==Adverb== {{adverb}} # You use <math>x</math> or '''else''' <math>y</math> to say that if <math>x</math> doesn't happen or isn't true, <math>y</math> would happen or would be true. #: ''They don't want to be here or '''else''' they would have come.'' # You use or '''else''' to say that if something doesn't happen, it will be bad. #: ''You'd better clean your room, or '''else'''.''
[[Category:Intransitive prepositions]]

{{wikipedia|Figure}} {{wikipedia}} {{BNC1000HW}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈfɪgjɚ/}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈfɪgə/}} * {{CA}} {{IPA|/ˈfɪɡɚ/|/ˈfɪɡjɚ/}} * {{audio|en-us-figure.ogg|Audio (US)}} * {{hyph|fig|ure}}
== Noun == {{noun}} {{AVL}} # {{countable}} '''Figures''' are numbers showing the [[value]] or [[amount]] of something. #: ''The sales '''figures''' from the spring were down from last year.'' #: ''According to the official '''figures''', unemployment levels are about 6 per cent. '' #: ''You only have to look at the '''figures''' for fire deaths in hotels to see this is not a problem.'' # {{countable}} A '''figure''' is a person, often a well-known person. #: ''They have published articles about many leading '''figures''' including John Reed, J.A. Hobson, Tom Mann, and Daniel de Leon.'' #: ''The '''figure''' of Margaret Thatcher towers over the Falklands War.'' # {{countable}} A '''figure''' is a person, especially the person's [[shape]].{{synonym|silhouette}} #: ''She did not see the '''figure''' standing in the shadows of the kitchen doorway.'' #: ''Across the river is the '''figure''' of Lenin on top of an armored car carved of stone.'' #: ''Her girlish '''figure''' had disappeared as she aged, sat more, and ate more.'' #: ''The most popular boy's toy ever is the G.I. Joe action '''figure'''.'' #: ''He looked down at the wet '''figures''' of the boy and dog.'' # {{countable}} A '''figure''' is a [[geometric]] shape. # {{countable}} A '''figure''' is a picture in a textbook or scientific journal. (Often written [[fig.]])
<gallery> File:Mary Ball.jpg|four '''figures''' File:Geometria 02.svg|some 2-dimensional '''figures''' File:Hranol kosy.svg|a 3-dimensional '''figure''' </gallery>
=== Related words === *[[figural]] *[[fig]] *[[figure skate]] *[[figure of speech]]
== Verb == {{verb|figur|e}} # {{intransitive}} If <math>x</math> '''figures''' in something that happens, <math>x</math> is part of that happening. #: ''The weather '''figured''' prominently in their plans.'' #: ''The fact that he wouldn't be there didn't '''figure''' among her worries.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''figure''' that something is true, you think that it is true. #: ''Few people '''figured''' that he would win.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''figure''' something out, you think about it until you understand it. #: ''He '''figured''' out that she was speaking Italian.''
=== Synonyms === *[[count]] *[[think]] *[[calculate]]
=== Related words === *[[figuring]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/pɑːs/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/pæs/}} * {{audio|en-us-pass.ogg|US}} == Verb == {{verb|pass|es}} # {{ti verb}} If you '''pass''' something, it was ahead of you and you move so that it is now behind you. #: ''Please, step to the right and let faster people '''pass''' on your left.'' #: ''She was so close to the road that she could feel the wind from '''passing''' cars.'' #: ''He looked in as he '''passed''' the window.'' #: ''We '''passed''' through the tunnel and were back out into the light.'' #: ''She '''passed''' her hand across her face.'' #: ''He '''passed''' the belt through the loops in his pants.'' #: ''Did you see two people '''pass''' this way, a man and a woman, walking north? '' # {{law}} {{ti verb}} If a [[bill]], law, motion, etc. '''passes''', it is accepted, usually after a vote. #: ''The House '''passed''' a law that makes it a crime to have sex with anyone under age 16.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''pass''' a test, exam, etc., you get a score that is good enough, often over 50%. #: ''You '''passed''' the test. In fact, you got 7 out of 10 correct.'' # {{ti verb}} If time '''passes''', it moves from future to past. #: ''I'm bored here. The only thing that helps me '''pass''' the time is your letters.'' #: ''They '''passed''' the night in a hotel just outside town.'' # {{ti verb}} If a road, river, railway, etc. '''passes''' a place, it continues from one side of the place to the other side. #: ''They are building a 150-kilometer road that '''passes''' through Yasuni Park.'' #: ''The road from Karachi to Gadani '''passes''' the route once taken by {{w|Alexander the Great}}.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''pass''' something to someone, you give it to them, usually by hand. #: ''Could you '''pass''' me the salt, please?'' #: ''The book '''passed''' from hand to hand.'' #: ''I '''passed''' your name on to my manager.'' #: ''She '''passed''' the information on to the police.'' # {{intransitive}} If something '''passes''', it happens. #: ''What has '''passed''' today must remain a secret.'' # {{sport}} {{ti verb}} If you '''pass''' a ball, [[puck]], etc. you throw, kick, or hit it to another member of your team. #: ''He '''passed''' to Lafleur, who put the ball in for the goal.'' === Synonyms === * [[go by]] * [[move]] * [[give]] * [[approve]] * [[succeed]] * [[spend]] === Antonyms === * [[fail]] === Related words === * [[past]] * [[passable]] * passably * [[impassable]] * impassably * [[passer]] * [[pass the buck]] == Noun == {{noun|pass|passes}} # {{countable}} A '''pass''' is a piece of paper, plastic, etc. that allows somebody to enter a building, [[vehicle]], or area. #: ''We have a season's '''pass''' for the ski hill.'' # {{countable}} A '''pass''' is a score on a test, exam, etc. that is good enough, often over 50%. Also a person or paper that gets this score. #: ''On the last test there were only five '''passes'''; everyone else failed.'' #: ''We have one of the highest '''pass''' rates for the exam in the state!'' # {{sport}} {{countable}} A '''pass''' is a throw, kick, hit, etc. of a ball, puck, etc. to another member of your team. #: ''Robert's '''pass''' in front of the net is blocked by the goalie.'' # {{countable}} A '''pass''' is a place in a [[mountain]] that is easy to [[travel]]. #: ''The mountain '''pass''' was [[block]]ed, which made it [[difficult]] to get across.'' # {{countable}} A '''pass''' is one case of a repeated action or process. #: ''We caught some new mistakes on the third '''pass'''.'' === Antonyms === * [[fail]]

== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} {{AVL}} # A '''particular''' thing is the one that you mean and not any other. #: ''Usually it is not [[allow]]ed, but in this '''particular''' case, it's OK.'' #: ''I don't see any way to solve this '''particular''' problem.'' # A '''particular''' thing is a special or great one. #: ''She took no '''particular''' interest in what they were saying.'' # If somebody is '''particular''', they will accept only the best or only things that they like.
=== Related words === * [[particularly]] * [[particularity]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # If you talk about something in '''particular''', you mean that more than other; [[especially]]. #: ''It's true of many small cars, but the Honda in '''particular'''.'' #: ''In '''particular''', I'd like you to think about the first problem.'' # {{countable}} {{usually plural}} The '''particulars''' are the detailed information. #: ''The two stories are quite similar, though they differ in some '''particulars'''.'' #: ''We've spent a good deal of time considering the '''particulars''' of the situation.''
=== Synonyms === * [[detail]]
=== Antonyms === * [[generality]]

=== Other spellings === *{{informal}} [[oughta]] === Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ɔːt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ɔt/}} * {{audio|en-us-ought.ogg|Audio (US)}} == Verb == {{verb4|must|ought|oughtn't}} #{{Modal}} If you '''ought''' to do something, doing it is better than not doing it. {{syn|should|must|had better}} #:''I think perhaps we '''ought''' to help her.'' #:''It's dangerous and there '''ought''' not to be any children close by.'' #:''We really '''ought''' to go a bit early because of the snow.'' #: ''What time '''ought''' the school to open?'' #: ''I suppose I '''ought''' to write her an e-mail.'' #{{Modal}} If something '''ought''' to be true, you have reason to believe it, but you don't know, or it is not true. {{syn|should}} #: ''He '''ought''' to be here by now.'' #: ''You '''ought''' to be able to finish that in an hour.'' === Usage notes === '''Ought''' is different from other modal auxiliaries (e.g., ''may, will, could'') in that it takes ''to'' + [[bare infinitival clause]] instead of a bare infinitival clause. For example: : ''I will go.'' : ''I ought '''to''' go.'' There is, however, a trend to use '''ought''' with a bare infinitival clause in negatives and certain questions. For example: : ''You '''oughtn't''' (to) worry about it.'' : '''''Ought''' we (to) ask her about it?''

{{BNC1HW}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|rāz}}, {{IPA|/reɪz/}} * {{audio|en-us-raise.ogg|US}} * {{hmp|rase|rays|raze}} == Verb == {{verb|rais|e}} # {{transitive}} If you '''raise''' something you make it [[high]]er; that is you move it [[up]]. #: ''I need to '''raise''' the car off the ground to fix it from below.'' #: '' '''Raise''' your hand if you know the answer.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''raise''' [[child]]ren or [[animal]]s, you [[care]] for them until they have [[grow]]n up (become [[adult]]s). #: ''I '''raised''' the children after their mother died.'' #: ''I '''raised''' my [[dog]] from a [[puppy]].'' # {{transitive}} If you '''raise''' [[food]] ([[plant]]s or [[animal]]s) you [[grow]] it on a [[farm]]. This is also used for plants that are not food, like [[cotton]] or [[tobacco]]. #: ''My grandfather '''raised''' [[corn]] and [[chicken]]s.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''raise''' a [[number]], you make it bigger. # {{transitive}} If you '''raise''' an [[idea]] you start [[talk]]ing about it. #: ''Why did you have to '''raise''' the issue of abortion?'' # {{transitive}} If you '''raise''' somebody in {{r|gambl|ing}}, you make a bigger [[bet]]. # {{transitive}} If someone '''raises''' the [[dead]] they make dead people [[alive]] again. #: ''[[Jesus]] is said to have '''raised''' the dead.'' === Synonyms === * [[heighten]] * [[increase]] === Antonyms === * [[lower]] * [[depress]] * [[decrease]] === Related words === * [[rise]] == Noun == {{noun}} # A '''raise''' is an [[increase]] in [[pay]] at [[work]]. #: ''I have worked here long enough I should get a '''raise'''.'' # In [[gambling]], a '''raise''' is an increased [[bet]].

{{BNC1000HW}} {{wikipedia}} === Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈmætə/}}, {{SAMPA|/"m{t@/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈmætɚ/}}, {{SAMPA|/"m{t@`/}} * {{audio|en-us-matter.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|mat|ter}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''matter''' is something that you can talk about or do something about a [[topic]] or a [[situation]]. #: ''Government must make these changes as a '''matter''' of urgency.'' #: ''We can discuss the '''matter''' more fully at the meeting.'' #: ''Whether our people should be in the country or not is '''matter''' for debate.'' #: ''At the meeting we will have time to talk about new '''matters''' arising.'' #: ''They decided on a number of '''matters''' related to housing.'' #: ''Try not to do anything to make '''matters''' worse.'' #: ''As a '''matter''' of principle, we should try to help poor people.'' #: ''It is not a simple '''matter''' to stop using gasoline.'' #: ''Care Assistants help them with such '''matters''' as toileting, dressing, washing and so on.'' #: ''The truth of the '''matter''' is that we do not know how to do it.'' #: ''The questions about the new president are a '''matter''' of public concern.'' #: ''Cheating on a test is a serious '''matter'''.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Matter''' is the stuff that everything is made of. #: ''Cities are trying to separate organic '''matter''' and other garbage.'' #: ''Scientists now think that there is some kind of "dark '''matter'''" in space.'' # You use, "as a '''matter''' of fact" to add information that may be surprising. #: ''"Have you met anyone interesting over there?" "As a '''matter''' of fact, I met a whole bunch of people just this afternoon.'' # You use "what's the '''matter'''" to ask somebody why they are unhappy, or why there is a problem. # You use "for that '''matter'''" when you have just thought about something that you are comparing to something else. #: ''He wasn't very nice today. For that '''matter''', he's never nice.'' # If something is only a '''matter''' of time, it may not happen now, but it will happen after some time. #: ''It's only a '''matter''' of days now before I start the new job.'' # You use "no '''matter''' what" to say that even if other things change, a particular thing will not change. #: ''I'll be there no '''matter''' what. I promise.''
=== Synonyms === * [[issue]] * [[problem]]
=== Related words === * [[matter-of-fact]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} {{context|usually negative}} If something doesn't '''matter''', it is not [[important]]. #: ''"Should I put it up there?" "Oh, it doesn't '''matter'''. Put it anywhere."'' #: ''Anyone can play. It doesn't '''matter''' if you're seven or 70.'' #: ''It doesn't '''matter''' what you do as long as it's fun.'' #: ''Many people don't like me, but that doesn't really '''matter''' to me.'' #: ''This should help a lot of people and that's what '''matters'''.'' #: ''"Sorry about that!" "Oh, it doesn't '''matter'''."'' #: ''It's not your money, so what does it '''matter'''?''
=== Synonyms === * [[count]]
[[Category:Matter| ]]

=== Synonyms === * [[approve]] * [[permit]] * [[consent]]
=== Antonyms === * [[deny]] * [[disagree]] * [[refuse]]

{{BNC1000HW}} === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/pæk/|[pʰæk]}} * {{audio|en-au-pack.ogg|AU}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} When you '''pack''' something, you put it in a [[container]] to carry with you. #: ''Did you '''pack''' your swimming suit?'' # {{ti verb}} When you '''pack''' a container, you put things in it to carry with you. #: ''The students have all '''packed''' their bags and left for the summer.'' #: ''It's time to '''pack''' up and go.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''pack''' a place or a container with something (or '''pack''' something in a place or container), you put a lot inside. #: ''The hall was '''packed''' with visitors.'' # If you '''pack''' something like snow or earth, you press it to make it take up less space. #: ''All the runners had '''packed''' the earth hard.'' # If you '''pack''' a gun, you carry it with you. # If you '''pack''' something away, you put it away in a container. # If you '''pack''' it in, you [[give up]].
=== Synonyms === * [[crowd]] * [[stuff]] * [[jam]]
=== Related words === * [[packing]] * [[packed]] * [[package]] * [[packaging]] * [[packet]] * [[packer]] * [[unpack]] * [[unpacked]]
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:LeonWeber 3.jpg|thumb|A child wearing a pack on his back]] # {{countable}} A '''pack''' is a container that things are sold in. #: ''Cigarettes were selling for over $10 a '''pack'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''pack''' is a bag used to [[carry]] things, usually on your back. #: ''My spare clothes are in my '''pack'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''pack''' of [[card]]s is a set of 52 playing cards. # {{countable}} A '''pack''' is a group of animals, usually that [[hunt]] together. # {{countable}} A '''pack''' of people is a group, usually not a nice group. # {{countable}} A '''pack''' of [[lie]]s is something that is completely untrue. # {{countable}} An ice '''pack''' is something cold that you put on an [[injury]].
=== Synonyms === * [[package]] * [[packet]] * [[bag]]

{{BNC1000HW}}
===Pronunciation=== *{{IPA|/ˈpɑrdən/}} *{{audio|en-us-pardon.ogg|Audio (US)}}
==Interjection== {{interjection}} # You use '''pardon''' to show that you didn't hear or understand someone. #:''"Could you close the door, please?" "'''Pardon'''!" "Close the door, please."'' # You use '''pardon''' when you have made a [[rude]] sound like a [[burp]].
===Synonyms=== *[[sorry]]
==Verb== {{verb}} # If a government '''pardons''' somebody who is [[guilty]] of a [[crime]], it allows them to live as though they had not [[commit]]ted the crime. #: ''The Ethiopian government has '''pardoned''' twenty five prisoners who were found guilty in connection to the unrest that rocked the nation.'' # When you '''pardon''' someone, you [[forgive]] them. #: ''I hope he'll '''pardon''' me for what I did to him.''
===Synonyms=== *[[excuse]] *[[forgive]]
===Related words=== *[[pardonable]] *[[unpardonable]]
==Noun== {{noun}} # You say '''''pardon''' me'' or ''I beg your '''pardon''''' when you didn't hear someone, when you accidentally touch someone, when you want someone's attention, or when you'd like someone to move. # {{countable}} A '''pardon''' is given when someone is [[forgiven]]. #: ''The soldier was given a '''pardon''' for all the acts he had committed while fighting in the war.''

{{BNC1000HW|picture|photograph}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/pɪk/|[pʰɪk]}} * {{audio|en-us-pick.ogg|Audio (US)}} * {{audio|en-au-pick.ogg|Audio (AU)}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Nattes à chat-pick.wav|Audio}} * {{hmp|pic}}
== Verb == {{verb}} [[File:Tea plantation picking.JPG|thumb|'''picking''' tea]] # {{ti verb}} When you '''pick''' something, you [[choose]] it. #: ''I have '''picked''' the best people to work on this job.'' #: ''This was '''picked''' as the best new toy of the year.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''pick''' up something, you lift it. #: ''She '''picked''' up the glass and put it down again.'' #: '''''Pick''' your clothes up off the floor!'' #: ''The baby's crying. Can you '''pick''' him up?'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''pick''' up the phone, you answer it. # {{ti verb}} If you '''pick''' something up from somewhere, you go and get it. #: ''Mom, can you '''pick''' me up from Austin's at 8:00?'' #: ''I'll go an '''pick''' up a pizza.'' # {{ti verb}} If you try to '''pick''' up someone you have just met, you talk to them because you want to have sex with them. # {{transitive verb}} If you '''pick''' fruit, flowers, etc., you take them off the [[plant]]. #: ''We spent the morning '''picking''' apples in the forest.'' #: ''Please help me '''pick''' up the books that I've dropped.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''pick''' something from somewhere, you take it out of or away from that place. #: ''After dinner he '''picked''' the rice out of the children's hair.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''pick''' a [[musical instrument]] such as a guitar, you play it by pulling its [[string]]s and letting them go. # {{intransitive}} If you '''pick''' at something, you touch it many times without doing anything. #: ''He was too sick to eat and just '''picked''' at his food.'' #: ''She '''picked''' nervously at her dress.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''pick''' on someone, you are not nice to them in particular. #: ''He was '''picked''' on by his brothers for his small size.''
=== Synonyms === * [[choose]] * [[select]] * [[take]] * [[pluck]]
=== Antonyms === * [[replace]] * [[put]] * [[set]]
=== Related words === * [[picker]] * [[unpicked]] * [[handpicked]] * [[picky]]
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Guitar picks-KayEss-1.jpeg|right|thumb|A guitar '''pick'''.]] # {{countable}} A '''pick''' is a [[choice]]. #: ''His '''pick''' for Man of the Year was John Smith.'' #: ''You have your '''pick''' of the rooms. Which one do you want?'' # {{countable}} A '''pick''' is a [[tool]] used to [[dig]]. #: ''He dug that hole using a '''pick'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''pick''' is something used to play a [[guitar]] with. #: ''He forgot his guitar '''pick'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[choice]] * [[selection]] * [[plectrum]]
[[Category:Tools]]

=== Related words === * [[political]] * [[politics]] * [[politician]] * [[unpolitical]] * [[politically]] * [[nonpolitical]] * [[politicize]]/[[politicise]] * [[politicized]]/[[politicised]] * [[politicization]]/[[politicisation]]

{{BNC1000HW}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{US}} {{IPA|/prɛs/}} * {{audio|en-uk-press.ogg|UK}} * {{audio|en-us-press.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=presses}} [[File:President Ronald Reagan Meets with The Press After Signing The 1981 Tax Reconciliation Bill Rancho Del Cielo. - DPLA - 3b4f0119e2b08b0c050e82c2495cae12.jpg|thumb|{{w|Ronald Reagan}} speaking to the '''press''']] [[File:Power press animation.gif|thumb|a '''press''']] # {{uncountable}} {{context|sometimes with plural verb}} The '''press''' are the people and [[organisation]]s that [[report]] the news. #: ''The president gave an interview with members of the '''press'''.'' #: ''The company put out a '''press''' release about the new equipment.'' # {{uncountable}} The '''press''' is the news as it is reported. #: ''The next day, the fire was all over the '''press'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''press''' is a company that prints books. #: ''The book was published by {{w|University of California}} '''Press'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''press''' is a machine that [[print]]s books, newspapers, etc. #: ''Stop the '''presses'''! We've got a new story.'' # {{countable}} A '''press''' is a machine that pushes down on something to make it flat or to push out the water or juice. # {{countable}} A '''press''' is a time when you push something. #: ''She gave the button a quick '''press'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[media]]
== Verb == {{verb|press|es}} [[File:SmithMachineBenchPress.JPG|thumb|bench '''press''']] # {{transitive}} If you '''press''' something, you [[push]] it against something. #: ''She '''pressed''' her nose against the window.'' #: ''Please, '''press''' a button.'' #: ''He found the cut and '''pressed''' down firmly to stop the blood.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''press''' clothes, you use an [[iron]] to make them flat. # {{ti verb}} If you '''press''' someone to do something, you ask them strongly or many times. #: ''When she '''pressed''' him for an answer, he hung up the phone.'' #: ''The group has been '''pressing''' for new laws to reduce pollution.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''press''' on or forward, you keep going even though it's [[difficult]]. # {{transitive}} If you press a weight, you exercise by moving the weight up and away from your body. # {{transitive}} If you '''press''' a CD or record, you make a physical copy of it.
=== Synonyms === * [[push]] * [[squeeze]]
=== Related words === * [[unpressed]] * [[pressingly]]

===Pronunciation=== *{{UK}} {{IPA|/rɪˈgɑːd/}} *{{US}} {{IPA|/rɪˈgɑrd/}} *{{audio|en-us-regard.ogg|Audio (US)}}
==Noun== {{noun}} # {{uncountable}} If you have '''regard''' for something, you [[respect]] it. #: ''He has a high '''regard''' for his teacher.'' #: ''These people have no '''regard''' for other people's feelings.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Regard''' is how something is though about or [[look]]ed at. #: ''We do disagree, but only in '''regard''' to how much the government is spending.'' #: ''What has he said with '''regard''' to taxes?'' #: ''He's made a lot of money and is certainly a success in that '''regard'''.'' # {{usually plural}} You use '''Regards''' as a [[closing]] in a formal letter. # {{usually plural}} You ask somebody to give somebody else your '''regards''' as a formal way to show your concern for and interest in these people.
===Synonyms=== *[[attention]] *[[aspect]]
===Antonyms=== *[[disregard]]
===Related words=== *[[disregard]] *[[regarding]] *[[regardless]]
==Verb== {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''regard''' something, you think about it. #: ''How do you '''regard''' his actions?'' #: ''She's widely '''regarded''' as the best tennis player in history.'' # {{transitive}} When you '''regard''' something, you [[look]] at it. #: ''She '''regarded''' him with a smile.''
===Synonyms=== *[[look]] *[[consider]]
===Antonyms=== *[[disregard]]

{{BNC1000HW}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/rɪˈpɔrt/}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/rɪˈpɔːt/}} * {{AU}} {{IPA|/rəˈpoːt/}} * {{audio|en-us-report.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} {{AVL}} # {{countable}} A '''report''' is a [[description]] of something that has happened. {{syn|account|description}} #: ''There was a recent '''report''' on the election.'' # {{countable}} A '''report''' is a document that gives the [[result]]s of a study of a particular situation. {{syn|analysis|result}} # {{countable}} A '''report''' is a loud fast [[noise]]. {{syn|bang|explosion}} #: ''He could hear the '''report''' of the explosion.''
=== Related words === * [[unreported]] * [[reportedly]] * [[reporter]]
== Verb == {{verb}} {{AVL}} # {{ti verb}} If the [[news]] '''reports''' something, it tells us about it. #: ''The journalist '''reported''' that there were riots in the city.'' #: ''He's been '''reporting''' on the ongoing war in Iraq.'' # {{ti verb}} When you '''report''' something that has happened, you [[describe]] it. #: ''They '''reported''' to the police that their car had been stolen.'' #: ''She '''reported''' hearing loud noises at the time of the incident.'' #: ''He's '''reported''' to have been there at the time.'' #: ''So, you should '''report''' on your progress in three days.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''report''' somebody for something they've done wrong, you tell an official about the problem. #: ''The restaurant was '''reported''' to the city because of the dangerous kitchen.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''report''' somewhere, you go there and give your name. #: ''Visitors to the school should '''report''' to the office.''
=== Synonyms === * (''tell about'', ''describe'') [[describe]], [[inform]] * (''tell an official'') [[inform on]], [[rat on]], [[tell on]]
=== Related words === * [[report back]] * [[reporter]] * [[reportedly]] * [[unreported]]

{{BNC1000HW}} === Word parts === {{ety-suffix|supple|ly}} {{a|adverb only}}
=== Pronunciation === <!-- Hyphenation on the top, because it fits for both sections below! --> * {{hyph|sup|ply}} ;verb, noun * {{enPR|səplīʹ}}, {{IPA|/səˈplaɪ/}} * {{SAMPA|/s@"plaI/}} * {{audio|en-us-supply.ogg|US}} ;adverb * {{enPR|sŭpʹlē}}, {{IPA|/ˈsʌpli/}} * {{SAMPA|/"sVpli/}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=supplies}} # {{cu noun}} A '''supply''' is an amount of something that you can use when you need it. #: ''We will need a '''supply''' of water.'' #: ''During the war, the Americans destroyed their food '''supply'''.'' #: ''Sadly these books are in very short '''supply''' in Britain.'' #: ''The price of oil changes quickly to match '''supply''' and demand.'' # {{pluralonly}} '''Supplies''' are things like food, water, medicine, gasoline, etc. that people need when they are not near somewhere where they can get them easily. #: ''The Japanese government is finally planning to send medical '''supplies''' and financial support.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Supply''' is the act or system of supplying something. #: ''They plan to fix the Russian economy and improve the '''supply''' of food and consumer goods.'' #: ''The airplane's air '''supply''' wasn't working.''
=== Synonyms === * [[source]]
=== Related words === * [[supplier]]
== Verb == {{verb|suppl|y}} # {{transitive}} If you '''supply''' something, you make it [[available]], usually regularly. #: ''We were '''supplied''' with a few basic tools that we needed for the job.'' #: ''Our garden '''supplies''' us with all the food we need.'' #: ''The office was well '''supplied''' with chairs.''
=== Synonyms === * [[provide]]
=== Related words === * [[supplier]]
== Adverb == {{adv|more=true}} # In a [[supple]] way.
=== Other spellings === * [[supplely]]
[[Category:Adverbs suffixed with -ly]]

== Adjective == {{adj|slight|slighter|slightest}} # {{attrib}} A '''slight''' increase, difference, etc. is a small change. #: ''This year's 5.6% level is a '''slight''' increase from last year's 5.4%.'' #: ''Don't worry about me. It's just a '''slight''' pain'' #: ''I don't have the slightest idea what she meant.'' # If someone is '''slight''', they are thin. #: ''Out stepped a '''slight''', middle-aged woman who smiled kindly.''
=== Synonyms === * [[minor]] * [[insignificant]] * [[thin]] * [[slim]]
=== Antonyms === * [[big]] * [[major]] * [[significant]]
=== Related words === * [[slightly]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # If you '''slight''' someone, you [[treat]] them as if they were not [[important]]. #: ''Ever since that time, he's been '''slighted''' by his fellow workers.''
=== Synonyms === * [[disrespect]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # A '''slight''' is when you are not [[polite]] to someone. #: ''Has she forgiven him for his '''slight'''?''
=== Synonyms === * [[insult]]
[[Category:Size]]

{{BNC1000HW}} {{number box|en|1}} === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈsɪŋɡəl/}} * {{audio|en-us-single.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-au-single.ogg|AU}} {{-}} == Adjective == {{adj}} # {{attrib}} A '''single''' thing is the only [[one]]. #: ''In large baking dish, arrange chicken pieces in '''single''' layer.'' # You use '''single''' to stress how many or how few. #: ''I hate going to work every '''single''' day and listening to people yell at each other.'' #: ''I haven't heard a '''single''' word of thanks.'' #: ''Eastern Canada is the world's largest '''single''' source of newsprint.'' #: ''I don't think we should give them a '''single''' thing.'' # A '''single''' person is not married. #: ''The '''single''' mother of two spends weekends with her kids.'' #: ''I used to go out a lot when I was '''single'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[only]] * [[individual]] * [[unmarried]]
=== Antonyms === * [[multiple]]
=== Related words === * [[singly]] * [[singleness]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} {{music}} A '''single''' is a song that is sold or put out by itself (or with one other song), not on an [[album]]. #: ''Today she releases her live version of Birthday, the first '''single''' from an upcoming tour album.'' # {{countable}} {{sport}} In [[baseball]] and [[cricket]], a '''single''' is a hit that enables a runner to score a point. # {{countable}} {{sport}} In baseball a '''single''' is a hit that enables the player to move to first [[base]]. # {{uncountable}} {{sport}} '''Singles''' is a game where each side has only one player, especially in [[tennis]]. # {{pluralonly}} '''Singles''' are people who are not [[married]] or not in a romantic relationship. #: ''You'll pay no tax if your income falls below $50,000 for a married couple, $35,000 for '''singles'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''single''' is a hotel room for [[one]] [[person]]. #: ''I reserved a '''single''' in Montreal.''
== Verb == {{verb|singl|e}} # {{intransitive}} {{sport}} In baseball if you '''single''', you hit the ball and are able to run to first [[base]]. #: ''The batter '''singled''' to right field.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''single''' something out, you [[identify]] it, often to give it special attention. #: ''She was '''singled''' out as the best student in the class.''
[[Category:Tennis]] [[Category:One]]

{{BNC1000HW}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/sɜːv/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/sɝv/}} * {{audio|en-us-serve.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-au-serve.ogg|AU}}
== Verb == {{verb|serv|e}} # {{ti verb}} When you serve food or drink, you give it to somebody to eat or drink, especially as a [[host]]. #: ''Shall I '''serve''' your drinks first?'' #: ''Lunch is '''served''' from 11:00 until 3:00.'' # {{ti verb}} If something '''serves''' (as something), it [[use]]d or useful for a certain [[purpose]]. #: ''This cup can '''serve''' as a holder for my paintbrushes.'' #: ''This program has '''served''' as a model for smaller enterprises throughout the state.'' #: ''His experiences during the war '''served''' as the basis for his book.'' #: ''The area is '''served''' by a number of schools.'' #: ''The law no longer '''serves''' the function it once did.'' # {{ti verb}} When you '''serve''' (as something), you [[work]]. #: ''John '''served''' in the army.'' #: ''He '''served''' as the director of the company from 1992 until 2003.'' #: ''He '''serves''' the king.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''serve''' time in [[prison]], you stay there because you are a criminal. # {{ti verb}} {{sports}} If you '''serve''', in a game like tennis, you begin play by sending something like a ball over a net.
=== Related words === * [[servant]] * [[unserved]] * [[serving]] * [[server]] * [[servery]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{sports}} A '''serve''' in a game like tennis is the action beginning of play by sending something like a ball over a net. #: ''Whose '''serve''' is it?'' #: ''That was a great '''serve'''!''
=== Related words === * [[service]]
[[Category:Sports]]

{{BNC1000HW}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|trī}}, {{IPA|/traɪ/}} * {{SAMPA|/traI/}} * {{audio|en-us-try.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-uk-to try.ogg|UK}}
== Verb == {{verb|tr|y}} # {{ti verb}} If you '''try''' to do something, you make [[effort]] to do it. #: ''As much as I '''tried''', I couldn't understand it.'' #: ''I'm just '''trying''' to get things cleaned up before the kids get home.'' #: ''It's OK. We'll '''try''' again tomorrow.'' #: ''I really want to '''try''' and make a difference.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''try''' something, you [[taste]], do, or use it to see if it's good. #: '''''Try''' using the new shoes for a week and let me know if there any problems.'' #: ''He's never afraid to '''try''' something new.'' #: ''Did you '''try''' the fish in the fridge?'' # {{transitive}} If you '''try''' someone for a crime, you [[put]] them on [[trial]]. #: ''He was '''tried''' for robbery''.
=== Synonyms === * [[attempt]]
=== Related words === * [[untried]] * [[trying]] * [[trial]] * [[tryout]]
== Noun == {{noun|try|tries}} [[File:Caloundra try at Noosa.JPG|thumb|A player scores a '''try''' in a game of rugby.]] # {{countable}} A '''try''' is when you [[attempt]] to do something. #: ''I gave juggling a '''try''', but I just could not do it.'' # {{countable}} A '''try''' is when you taste, do, or use it to see if it's good. # {{countable}} {{sports}} A '''try''' is when you put the ball behind the other team's net in [[rugby]].
[[Category:Sports]]

'''Conjunctive adverbs''' are [[adverb]]s that can also be [[use]]d as [[conjunction]]s.
[[Category: Conjunctions]] [[Category: Adverbs]]

==Noun== {{noun}} # A '''loanword''' is a [[word]] in one [[language]] that comes from another language. #: ''"[[Tsunami]]" is a [[Japan]]ese word, but is a '''loan word''' in English.'' #: ''Most languages have some '''loanwords'''.'' #: ''There are many '''loanwords''' in English''.

== Noun == {{noun|politics|politics}} # {{uncountable}} '''Politics''' is the [[activity]] of [[control]]ling, affecting or studying an [[organisation]], especially a [[government]]. #: ''The Prime Minister entered '''politics''' when she was in university.'' #: ''It is very hard to keep the Church out of national '''politics'''.'' #: ''The decision about the war will be about both foreign policy and domestic '''politics'''.'' #: ''Office '''politics''' have stopped her from getting the job.''

==Pronoun== {{pronoun}} {{per pron}} # {{context|object}} You use '''them both''' to emphasize that you are talking about two things or people together. #: ''Can you give it to '''them both'''?'' #: ''I want '''them both''' to come.''
===Related words=== *[[them]] *[[both]]

== Pronoun == {{pronoun}} # {{per pron}} {{context|object}} When you use '''you both''', you emphasize that you are talking about two people together. #: ''I'll give it to '''you both'''?'' #: ''I want '''you both''' to come.''
=== Related words === * [[you]] * [[both]]

revision.comment: /* Pronoun */“..us both two emphasize…” is not gooder english. Instead of the noun “two”, indicating the number 2, the preposition “to” should be applied, which makes “… to emphasize…” an infinitive verb used as an affective of “…is both…”. See: https://www.grammarly.com/blog/infinitives/
revision.text:
==Pronoun== {{pronoun}} {{per pron}} # {{context|object}} You use '''us both''' to emphasize that you are talking about yourself and another person together. #: ''It would be better for '''us both''' to go?'' #: ''He wants '''us both''' to come.''
===Related words=== *[[us]] *[[both]]

==Pronoun== {{pronoun}} {{per pron}} # {{context|object}} You use '''you all''' when you emphasize that you are talking to or about more than just one person. #: ''I'd like to introduce our new manager to '''you all'''.'' #: ''I want to thank '''you all''' for coming.''
===Related words=== *[[you]] *[[all]] *[[y'all]]

== Pronoun == {{pronoun}} # {{per pron}} {{context|object}} You use '''them all''' to emphasize that you are talking to or about 100% of those being addressed. #: ''We have to make this better for '''them all'''.'' #: ''I want '''them all''' to be here early tomorrow.''
=== Related words === * [[them]] * [[all]]

==Pronoun== {{pronoun}} {{per pron}} # {{context|object}} You use '''us all''' two emphasize that you are talking to or about 100% of the people with you. #: ''We have to make this better for '''us all'''.'' #: ''I want '''us all''' to be here early tomorrow.''
===Related words=== *[[us]] *[[all]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈpəʊɪtri/|[ˈpəʊʷətrɪ]}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈpoʊətri/|[ˈpʰoʊ̯.ətˌri]}} * {{audio|en-us-poetry.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|po|et|ry}}
== Noun == {{noun4}} # {{uncountable}} The [[art]] of writing [[poem]]s. #: '' '''Poetry''' is much cheaper than [[painting]] since you don't need special supplies.'' # {{uncountable}} A group of poems. #: ''This is a book of '''poetry'''.'' # {{uncountable}} Poems in general. #: '' '''Poetry''' is found all over the world.'' # {{uncountable}} {{lc|Beautiful}} words or speech. #: ''To hear my child speak is '''poetry'''.''
=== Related words === * [[poet]] * [[poetic]] * [[poem]]
[[Category:Poetry| ]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-poetic justice.wav|Audio (UK)}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=none}} #{{uncountable}} '''Poetic justice''' is when a person has something happen to them that is like something bad they did to someone else. {{syn|payback}} #: ''After taking many peoples homes, he went broke and became homeless -- now that was '''poetic justice'''.''
=== Related words === *[[poetic]] *[[justice]]
=== See also === *[[irony]] *[[ironic]]

===Pronunciation=== *{{IPA|/ˈlir.ɪks/}}
==Noun== {{noun|lyric}} #{{countable}}; {{usually plural}} {{plural of|lyric}} #{{countable}}; {{usually plural}} '''Lyrics''' are the words that go to a [[song]]. Often, '''lyrics''' are like a [[poem]] set to [[music]]. #: ''I wish I knew the '''lyrics''' to ''Dreams'' by The Cranberries.'' #: ''The singer was trying to write '''lyrics''' for a new album.''
===Related words=== *[[lyrical]]
[[Category:Music]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{a|verb}} {{IPA|/rɪˈpiːt/}} * {{a|noun}} {{IPA|/rɪˈpiːt/|/ˈriːpiːt/}} * {{audio|en-us-repeat.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-uk-to repeat.ogg|UK}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''repeat''' something, you do it again.{{syn|redo}} #: ''I don't want to have to '''repeat''' typing this.'' #: ''If you fail the class you will have to '''repeat''' it.'' #: ''That song is not good because it just '''repeats''' the same words.'' # {{intransitive}} If something '''repeats''' or '''is repeated''' it is done more than once, or there is more than one of it. #: ''The flashing light just keeps '''repeating'''.'' #: ''The war was very bad, I hope history doesn't '''repeat''' with another like it.'' #: ''The words "No show hello" '''repeat''' through the whole song.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''repeat''' yourself, you say something you just said again. #: ''I already told you what to do, don't make me '''repeat myself'''.''
=== Related words === * [[repetition]] * [[repetitive]]
=== Synonyms === * [[re-do]] (also spelled "re do" or "redo") * [[do over]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} An instruction to repeat something. Usually this is used for [[music]] in part of a [[song]]. Sometimes it may be used for other things like part of a computer [[program]]. # {{colloquial}} Something this has been repeated; that is a [[repetition]].
=== Synonyms === * [[repetition]]

{{wikipedia}} == Noun == {{noun|duct tape|none}}
# {{uncountable}} '''Duct tape''' is a kind of [[strong]], [[waterproof]] [[tape]]. It used to be used to tape [[duct]]s, but is now used for many purposes. #: ''Please hand me the '''duct tape'''. I need to fix this box.''
===Usage notes=== ''Duct tape'' and ''[[duck tape]]'' are pronounced the same way so either word may be used. Note, however, that ''Duck® tape'' is a registered trademark.
== Verb == {{verb|duct tap|e}} [[File:Duct tape wall.jpg|thumb|A young man being duct taped to a wall]] # {{transitive}} To tape something by using '''duct tape'''. #: ''I '''duct taped''' it to the pole so it would stop falling.''
=== Related words === * [[duck tape]]
[[Category:Tools]] [[Category:Tapes]]

==Noun== {{noun|duck tape|none}}
# {{uncountable}} Duck® brand [[duct tape]]. # {{uncountable}}; {{informal}} Another word for [[duct tape]].
===Usage notes=== ''Duct tape'' and ''duck tape'' are pronounced the same way so either word may be used. Note, however, that ''Duck® tape'' is a registered trademark.
[[Category:Tapes]]

== Noun == {{noun|2=daddies}} [[File:My Father.jpg|thumb|a '''daddy''' and his girl]] # {{colloquial}} Another word for [[father]], a [[male]] [[parent]]. This is usually used by [[child]]ren. #: ''The girl was very [[happy]] to see her '''daddy'''.'' # {{slang}} Someone who is better than someone else. This is often used to say you are better than the person you are talking to, especially if you have [[beat]] them at something. #: ''You know I'm your '''daddy'''.'' #: ''Who's your '''daddy'''?'' (Same meaning as above) # {{slang}} Someone who is very [[great]]. #: ''He really thinks he's the '''daddy'''!''

== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:High school students.jpg|thumb|Adolescents]] # {{countable}} An '''adolescent''' is a [[person]] or [[animal]] that is [[old]]er than a [[child]] but [[young]]er than an [[adult]]. #: ''The [[teacher]] worked mostly with '''adolescents'''.'' # {{countable}} An '''adolescent''' is a [[person]] going through sexual maturation.
=== Synonyms === * [[teenager]] * [[teen]]
=== Related words === * [[baby]] * [[child]] * [[adult]]
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If something is '''adolescent''' it is [[typical]] of adolescents. #: ''The woman still had an '''adolescent''' appearance.''

===Pronunciation=== *{{audio|en-us-killer.ogg|Audio (US)}}
==Noun== {{noun}} #Someone who [[kill]]s. Usually this mean someone who kills other people, and does not have a good reason to kill. #: ''The police caught the '''killer''' today.'' #: ''She was happy that her brother's '''killer''' was caught.'' #Something that kills. #: ''Lighting can be a real '''killer'''.'' #Something that cause [[problem]]s. #: ''Failing the exam was a real '''killer'''.'' # {{slang}} Something that is very [[exciting]]. #: ''The show was [[great]], a real '''killer'''.''
===Synonyms=== *[[murderer]]
==Adjective== {{adjective|killer|none|none}} #If something is '''killer''' it kills. #: ''Watch out! There are '''killer''' bees!'' #: ''The family barely got away from the '''killer''' storm.'' # {{slang}} If something is '''killer''' it is very good. #: ''That was a '''killer''' show!''
===Synonyms=== * (kills) [[deadly]] * (good) [[cool]], [[awesome]]

They cropped their ears so people could not grab them, the same with their tail.

=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈhæn.dl/}} * {{audio|en-us-handle.ogg|US}} * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 handle.ogg|AU}} * {{hyph|han|dle}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Lincoln lock.JPG|thumb|The '''handle''' on a car door]] # {{countable}} A '''handle''' is the part of an object that you hold with your hand when you want to use or move the object. Some examples of '''handles''' are: the [[shaft]] of a sword, the [[knob]] of a door, etc. #: ''I grabbed the '''handle''' on the drawer and opened it.'' # {{countable}} {{slang}} A '''handle''' is a nickname or [[pseudonym]]. # {{context|Australia|New Zealand}} A '''handle''' is a 10 fl oz (285 ml) glass of beer in the Northern Territory. # {{countable}} {{context|US}} A '''handle''' is a 1.75-liter (half-gallon) bottle of alcohol.
=== Related words === * [[handlebars]] * [[love handle]]
== Verb == {{verb|handl|e}} # If you '''handle''' something, you [[touch]] it, you feel it with your hand. # How you '''handle''' an object is how you use it. #: ''You '''handle''' that gun pretty well.'' # To give and take; to have something pass through your hands; to buy and sell #: ''As a cashier, I '''handle''' money every day.'' #: ''That store '''handles''' many different items.'' # To deal with; to make a business of. #: ''They that '''handle''' the law knew me not'' – Jeremiah, 2:8 # To treat; to use, well or ill. #: ''How were you '''handled''' in prison?'' # To manage; to control; to practice skill upon. #: ''It won't be easy, but I think I can '''handle''' it.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈsɪn.tæks/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-syntax.wav|UK}} * {{hyph|syn|tax}} * {{hmp|sin tax}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=syntaxes}} # {{uncountable}} {{linguistics}} A part of the [[grammar]] of a [[language]]. '''Syntax''' is the rules for putting words together to make a [[sentence]]. #: ''[[English]] '''syntax''' is never easier than English [[spelling]].'' #: ''The linguist studied the '''syntax''' of many languages.'' #: ''The child had a problem with '''syntax''' after his head was hurt.'' #: ''The '''syntax''' of many [[computer]] languages is based on English '''syntax'''.'' # {{countable}} {{computing}} '''Syntax''' is the formal rules of {{r|formulat|ing}} [[statement]]s of a computer language. <!--from en.wikt-->
=== Note === The plural form syntices is a mistaken form that is usually used on [[blog]]s.
=== Related words === * [[grammar]] * [[morphology]] * [[morphosyntax]] * [[linguistics]]
[[Category:Language]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈaɪ.kən/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈaɪ.kɑːn/}} * {{audio|en-us-icon.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} An [[image]], [[picture]], or other [[represent]]ation of something. # {{countable}} A [[religion|religious]] painting that is often done on wooden panels. # {{countable}} A person or thing that is the best [[example]] of something. #: ''That man is an '''icon''' in the business; he is loyal and has good business sense.'' # {{countable}} A small picture which represents something (such as an icon on a computer screen). #: ''Click on the '''icon''' to open the program.'' # {{countable}} {{linguistics}} A type of [[noun]] where the form [[reflect]]s and is determined by the [[referent]]; [[onomatopoeia|onomatopoeic]] words are all icons.
=== Related words === * [[iconic]] * [[iconify]] * [[iconoclast]] * [[iconography]]
[[Category:Religion]] [[Category:Art]] [[Category:Semiotics]]

== Noun == {{noun2}} # {{pluralonly}} A person's '''daylights''' are his [[mental]] [[stability]] or his [[wits]]. #: ''You scared the '''daylights''' out of me!'' #: ''My dad will knock the living '''daylights''' out of me if I'm late.''
=== Related words === * [[daylight]]

An '''initialism''' is a type of [[abbreviation]] formed from the beginning letters of the phrase it represents. It is different from an [[acronym]] in that acronyms are said like words (NASA, LASER, DOS) while initialisms are pronounced by saying each of the letters (TNT, LGBT, AOC).

== Noun == {{noun|trash|none}} [[File:Vuilnis bij Essent Milieu.jpg|thumb|'''Trash''']] # {{lc|Useless}} things that are [[discard]]ed. #: ''I took it out of the wrapping and then threw away the '''trash'''.'' #: ''Please take out the '''trash'''.'' # A [[container]] where useless things are discarded. #: ''Just throw it in the '''trash'''.'' # Something of poor or bad [[quality]]. #: ''This radio is '''trash'''! It doesn't work!'' # {{slang}}; {{context|usually derogatory}} Lower [[class]] people. #: ''white '''trash''''' #: ''trailer '''trash''''' #: [[drug]].
=== Synonyms === * [[garbage]] * [[rubbish]] {{UK}} * [[refuse]] (noun)
=== Related words === * [[trailer trash]] * [[trash can]] * [[trashed]] * [[trashman]] * [[trashy]]
== Verb == {{verb|trash|es}} # {{US}} To make a [[mess]]; to ruin or destroy things. #: '''''Trash''' the house! he ordered.'' #: ''Scarface always '''trashes''' a house he burgles.'' #: ''The burglars '''trashed''' my house.'' #: ''They '''trashed''' John's house yesterday.'' #: ''Oh, my God! They're '''trashing''' my house right now!'' # {{US}} To [[discard]] or to throw away. #: ''Will you '''trash''' those old love letters?'' #: ''John always '''trashes''' my love letters.'' #: ''John '''trashed''' my love letters last Monday.'' #: ''I '''trashed''' John's old love letters yesterday.'' #: ''I'll spend the afternoon '''trashing''' your old love letters.''

In this sense, calling someone a '''badass''' is a [[compliment]]. #:''I heard that he smashed his guitar at the end of the encore. He's such a '''badass'''!''

{{see|kick-ass}} === Pronunciation === * {{audio|en-au-kick ass.ogg|Audio (AU)}}
== Expression == {{expression}} # {{vulgar}}; {{slang}} If you '''kick''' someone's '''ass''' you [[beat]] them in a [[fight]], or you [[hurt]] them [[a lot]]. #: ''I '''kicked''' his '''ass''' for [[insult]]ing my mom.'' #: ''Don't bother them, they'll '''kick''' your '''ass'''.'' #: ''He just got his '''ass kicked'''.'' # {{vulgar}}; {{slang}} If you '''kick''' someone's '''ass''' at a game or contest, you win by a lot. #: ''He really '''kicked''' my '''ass''' at football.'' # {{vulgar}}; {{slang}} If something '''kicks ass''' it is very good. #: ''The band totally '''kicked ass''' last night.''
== Interjection == {{interjection}} # {{slang}} You say '''kick ass'''! to show [[happiness]] or a feeling of [[accomplishment]]. {{synonyms|great|yes|awesome}} #:'''''Kick ass'''! I just won $250 playing [[poker]]!''

{{wikipedia}} === Pronunciation === * {{enPR|chĭp}}, {{IPA|/tʃɪp/}} * {{SAMPA|/tSIp/}} * {{audio|en-us-chip.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A small [[piece]] that is broken off of a larger [[object]]. #: ''A '''chip''' of [[paint]] fell off the [[wall]].'' # {{countable}} A [[damage]]d area of a [[surface]] where a chip has broken off. #: ''This cup has a '''chip''' in it.'' # {{countable}} A [[token]] that is used in place of cash when [[gambling]]. #: ''poker chip'' #: ''This '''chip''' is worth $1.'' # {{countable}} {{context|electronics}} A small [[circuit]] used in certain [[electronic]] [[device]]s. #: ''[[computer]] chip'' # {{countable}} {{context|US}} A thin, [[baked]] or [[fried]] piece of [[vegetable]], usually [[potato]]. #: ''[[potato chip]]s'' #: ''[[tortilla chip]]s'' # {{countable}} {{context|UK|AU|NZ}} A fried strip of potato, similar to [[French fries]]. # {{countable}} {{sport}} A shot where the ball goes up more than a regular shot. # {{countable}} {{context|curling}} A [[takeout]] that hits a [[rock]] at an angle. # {{countable}} A dried piece of [[dung]] that is used as [[fuel]]. # {{countable}} {{a|northern New Zealand}} A container that is usually used for holding strawberries or other fruit.
<gallery> File:Integrated circuit on microchip.jpg|An electronic chip File:Stack of poker chips.jpg|Poker chips File:Kartoffelchips-1.jpg|Potato chips File:4003 - Zermatt - Restaurant Weisshorn.JPG|Tortilla chips with salsa and guacamole File:Wood chips.JPG|Wood chips File:Fish and chips with peas.jpg|Fish and chips with peas File:Semi-sweet chocolate chips.jpg|Chocolate chips File:QueenHatshepsut-ExpeditionToPunt-PlasterCast-ROM.png|Part of this picture has been chipped away </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb|chip|p}} # {{transitive}} To [[break]] an object into small pieces. #: ''The workers '''chipped''' the dead branches into [[mulch]].'' # {{transitive}} To [[break]] small pieces off of an object. #: ''Be careful not to '''chip''' the paint.'' # {{transitive}}; {{context|golf}} To play a shot where the ball goes mostly [[upwards]] instead of [[forwards]]. # {{transitive}}; {{context|automotive}} To upgrade an [[engine management system]], usually to increase power. # {{intransitive}} To become chipped. #: ''This varnish '''chips''' easily.'' # {{intransitive}}; {{context|card games}} Often with "in", to [[ante]] (up).
=== Related phrases === * [[chip off the old block]] * [[fish and chips]] * [[have a chip on one's shoulder]]
[[Category:Foods]]

== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Laundry symbol dry cold.svg|thumb|A black dot in the center of a [[square]] and [[circle]]]] [[File:Lds conference center panoramic view slc utah.jpg|thumb|A conference center]] # {{countable}} The '''center''' of something, is the place that is as far from its [[outside]] as possible. #: ''The president and his problems continue to take '''center''' stage in the news.'' #: ''She placed a flowers at the '''center''' of the table and then hurried off.'' # {{countable}} A '''center''' is a building, area, or group of people with a particular purpose. #: ''They have opened a large shopping '''center''' in Taipei.'' #: ''The team was staying at the US Olympic training '''center'''.'' #: ''Recently, Bahrain has become a major international banking '''center'''.'' #: ''Scientists at the '''Center''' for Disease Control have found a new virus.'' # {{countable}} The town '''center''' is the place in the town where most of the shops are. # {{countable}} In [[politic]]s, the '''center''' is the position that is not politically [[right]] or [[left]]. # {{countable}} In [[sport]]s, a '''center''' is a [[player]] who plays in the middle of the [[field]], usually an attacker.
=== Synonyms === * [[middle]] * [[institution]]
=== Related words === * [[centre]] * [[centerist]] / [[centrist]] * [[centred]] / [[centered]] * [[central]] * [[centralism]] * [[centrally]] * [[centrality]] * [[centralise]] / [[centralize]] * [[centralised]] / [[centralized]] * [[centralisation]] / [[centralization]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''center''' something, you move it towards the center.

{{hard rule|[[WT:NOT]]}}
Wiktionary is an online [[dictionary]] and, as a means to that end, also an {{w|online community}}. Therefore, there are certain things that Wiktionary is ''not''.
== What Wiktionary is not == # Wiktionary is '''not an [[encyclopedia]], a genealogy database, or an atlas'''; that is, it is not an in-depth collection of factual information, or of data about places and people. If you are looking for an encyclopedia, try [[w:|Wikipedia]]. Wiktionary articles are about words. A Wiktionary entry should focus on matters of language and wordsmithing: spelling, pronunciation, etymology, translation, usage, quotations, and links to related words and concepts. # [[m:Wiki is not paper|Wiktionary is '''not paper''']]. Thus, Wiktionary effectively has no size limits, can include links, can be more timely, etc. It also means that the style and length of writing appropriate for paper may not be appropriate here. # Wiktionary is not a '''soapbox, chatroom, or discussion forum'''. Although there are many discussion pages in Wiktionary, they are just to discuss about making Wiktionary better, which is our goal. # Wiktionary is neither a '''“mirror”''' nor a '''repository of links, images, or media files'''. All content added to Wiktionary may be edited mercilessly to be included on the site. # Wiktionary is '''not a free wiki host or webspace provider'''. You may not host your own website at Wiktionary. If you are interested in using the {{w|wiki}} technology for a collaborative effort on anything other than writing a dictionary of all words in all languages, even if it is just a single page, there are many sites that provide wiki hosting (free or for money). You can even install wiki software on your server. # Wiktionary is '''not a battlefield'''. Every user is expected to interact with others [[w:Wikipedia:Be kind|civilly]], calmly and in a spirit of cooperation. Do not [[Wiktionary:No personal attacks|insult]], harass or intimidate those with whom you have a disagreement. Rather, approach the matter in an intelligent manner, and engage in polite discussion. Do not create or edit articles [[w:WP:POINT|just to prove a point]]. Do not make [[w:Wikipedia:No legal threats|legal or other threats]] against Wiktionary, Wiktionarians, or the Wikimedia Foundation. Threats are not tolerated and may result in a [[w:Wikipedia:Bans and blocks|ban]]. # Wiktionary is '''not [[w:censorship|censored]] for the 'protection of minors'''' ([[w:MPAA film rating system|content-rated]]). First, anyone can edit an article and the results are displayed instantaneously, so we cannot guarantee that a child will see or read nothing objectionable. Second, Wiktionary has no organized system for the removal of material that might be thought likely to harm minors. However, articles can be, and are, censored by consensus. # Wiktionary is '''not a place to test out software changes'''. If you wish to test out your code on [[mw:|MediaWiki]], please do so on [[testwiki:|Test Wikipedia]].
[[Category:Wiktionary]]

== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''crown''' is a round-shaped ring that [[king]]s and [[queen]]s wear on the head. It is made of [[expensive]] metals. It might have [[jewel]]s too. #: ''The queen wore a fancy '''crown'''.'' # {{countable}} The '''crown''' is the [[position]] of a [[sovereign]] (in a monarchy). # The top part of the [[head]]. # {{context|dentistry}} A [[prosthetic]] covering for a [[tooth]].
<gallery> File:Imperial State Crown of Queen Victoria.jpg|The Crown of Queen Victoria File:Double cowlick.jpg|The crown of a man's head File:Crown dentistry.jpg|A crown on a tooth </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb}} [[File:Coronation of Ferdinand II of Aragon.jpg|thumb|A statue showing the crowning of {{w|Ferdinand II of Aragon}}.]] # To put a crown on someone's head. # To formally announce the new [[king]] or [[emperor]]. #: ''After the death of the old king, the new king was '''crowned'''.'' # To declare the [[winner]]. # {{medicine}} During [[birth]], when the baby's head is seen in the mother's [[vaginal]] opening. #: ''The mother was in the second stage of labor and the baby had just '''crowned''', so the midwives encouraged her.''
=== Related words === * [[coronation]]

{{wikipedia}} === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/dʌmi/}} * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 dummy.ogg|AU}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Wodencafe-dummy.wav|US}}
== Noun == {{noun|dummy|dummies}} [[File:Dummy.jpg|thumb|Dummies]] # {{countable}} A '''dummy''' is a [[model]] of a [[person]]. A '''dummy''' is often used to show clothes or test [[safety]]. #: ''The dress looked better on the '''dummy'''.'' #: ''The company uses '''dummies''' to test the new cars in crashes.'' # {{countable}} {{colloquial}} A '''dummy''' is a person who is [[stupid]]; if someone is a '''dummy''' they are not [[intelligent]]. #: ''You got good grades, I know you are not a '''dummy'''.'' #: ''I got angry because they treated me like a '''dummy'''.'' #: ''Those guys are a bunch of '''dummies'''.'' #: ''I need easy instruction, something for '''dummies'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''dummy''' is something that is not there but people act like its there for some purpose. #: ''That [[file]] is just a '''dummy''' to help the [[program]] start.''
=== Synonyms === * [[model]] * Stupid person: [[idiot]], [[fool]] * Not real / not there: [[fake]], [[stand-in]]
=== Related words === * [[dumb]]
== Adjective == {{adjective}} # A '''dummy''' thing is something that is not there or is not the thing it is called. #: ''They used a '''dummy''' account to make the records look right.'' #: ''The card game has one '''dummy''' player for each real player.''
=== Synonyms === * [[fake]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/dʌm/}} * {{audio|en-ca-dumb.oga|CA}}
== Adjective == {{adj|dumb|dumber|dumbest}} # {{context|offensive when describing a person}} Not able to [[speak]]. If someone is dumb they can not say anything. {{syn|mute}} #: ''They went to a school for the [[deaf]] and '''dumb'''.'' #: ''Dogs are just '''dumb''' animals.'' # {{colloquial}} Another word for [[stupid]]. If you are '''dumb''' you are not [[intelligent]]. {{syn|stupid|idiotic}} {{ant|intelligent|smart|clever|wise}} #: ''That is a really '''dumb''' idea.'' #: ''How could I be so '''dumb'''? I know better than that!'' #: ''I'm not '''dumb''' enough to believe that.'' #: ''It is not nice to call someone '''dumb'''.'' # Temporarily unable or unwilling to speak.
=== Usage note === Using ''dumb'' for someone who cannot speak is offensive. It is seen as an [[insult]] to people who cannot speak. That was the first meaning, but now ''dumb'' usually means stupid. "Deaf and dumb" is also offensive, and it [[upset]]s people who are [[deaf]]. The word speech-[[impair]]ed is preferred.
=== Related words and phrases === * [[dummy]] * [[dumbwaiter]] * [[deaf and dumb]] * [[dumbass]] * [[dumb cane]]

I called your office and they said you never came in!'' # {{vulgar}}; {{slang}} A [[card game]] where players [[bluff]] about the cards they play and try to figure out when the other players are bluffing. #: ''Anyone want to play a few hands of '''bullshit'''?'' # {{vulgar}}; {{slang}} An object of frustration and/or disgust. #: ''"This is '''bullshit'''!" -- The Monarch'' # {{context|literally}} The [[feces]] of a [[bull]].

I called your office and you never even came in.'' # {{vulgar}}; {{slang}} To talk [[casual]]ly with no real [[purpose]]. #: ''I will probably just go and '''bullshit''' with Joe for awhile.''
