{{wikipedia|joint}} === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/dʒɔɪnt/}} * {{audio|en-au-joint.ogg|AU}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # A place where two things meet but are still able to move. # A place where two things join [[solid]]ly. # {{anatomy}} Any part of the body where two [[bone]]s join, sometimes letting that part of the body to be [[bent]] or [[straighten]]ed. # {{context|carpentry}} A way to join two pieces of [[wood]] together so that they [[interlock]]. # {{slang}} A [[bar]], [[restaurant]], or [[nightclub]]. #: ''It was the kind of '''joint''' you wouldn't want your boss to see you in.'' # {{slang}}; {{context|always with 'the'}} [[prison]]; [[jail]]. #: ''I'm not breaking any more laws because I don't want to go back to '''the joint'''.'' # {{context|smoking}} {{slang}} A [[marijuana]] [[cigarette]]. #: ''Let's smoke a '''joint''' and then go skateboarding.''
<gallery> File:Universal joint.png|Putting together a '''joint''' File:Simple CV Joint animated.gif|A CV '''joint''' File:Dado joint.svg|Putting together a wood '''joint''' File:Joint.jpg|A marijuana '''joint''' </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb}} # If you '''joint''' something, you connect them together with [[#Noun|joints]].

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ɪntʃ/}} * {{audio|en-us-inch.ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Noun == {{irrnoun|inches}} [[File:Inch tape.jpg|thumb|A tape measure that measures '''inches'''.]] # A unit of [[length]] that is equal to 2.54 [[centimetre]]s; there are 12 inches in a [[foot]]. #:''My pencil is six '''inches''' long.''
== Verb == {{verb|inch|es}} # {{intransitive}}; {{context|followed by a preposition}} To [[move]] very [[slowly]] in a direction. #: ''Fearful of falling, he '''inched''' along the window ledge.''
=== Related words === * [[inchworm]]
[[Category:Units of length]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/bʌɪnd/}} * {{audio|en-us-bind.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb2|bind|binds|bound|bound|binding}} # {{transitive}} If you '''bind''' something put [[rope]] or [[string]] around it, often many times. #: ''She tied the rope around their hands, '''binding''' them tightly together.'' #: ''He '''bound''' the books with string and carried them downstairs.'' # {{transitive}} If something '''binds''' two people or things, it [[connect]]s them. #: ''Now that he couldn't walk, he was '''bound''' to his nurse.'' # {{anchor|binding}}{{transitive}}, {{usually passive}} If someone is '''bound''' by a rule, promise, etc., they must not break it. #: ''The media are not '''bound''' by the same rules that govern lawyers.'' #: ''When they join the European Union, they will have to agree to be '''bound''' by the European Convention on Human Rights.'' #: ''The president is not '''bound''' to sign any law that Congress sends up.'' # {{ti verb}} If two things '''bind''', they stick together. #: ''Carbon '''binds''' with oxygen to form carbon dioxide.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''bind''' a book, you put it together so the pages stay together.
=== Synonyms === * [[tie]] * [[connect]] * [[unite]]
=== Related words === * [[binding]] * [[binder]] * [[unbound]] * [[bond]]
<gallery> File:Liberty bound poster.jpg|A woman '''bound''' to a pole File:Sheet bend.jpg|Two pieces of rope '''bound''' together File:Buchblock Buchdecke.jpg|'''Binding''' a book </gallery>
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''bind''' is a difficult position or situation. #: ''I've lost my job and I'm in a terrible '''bind'''.''
=== Related words === * [[double bind]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 creepy-crawly.ogg|AU}}
== Noun == {{irrnoun|creepy-crawlies}} # {{informal}} A '''creepy-crawly''' is a small animal that [[crawl]]s, such as an [[insect]], [[spider]], or [[worm]]; this word describes the way these animals move. #: ''While most people are disgusted by '''creepy-crawlies''', some find them interesting.''
=== Related words === * [[creepy]] * [[crawly]] * [[creep]] * [[crawl]]
[[Category:Insects]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|/krēp/}}, {{IPA|/kriːp/}} * {{SAMPA|/kri:p/}} * {{audio|en-us-creep.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # When an animal moves with its belly close to the ground. #: ''The '''creep''' of the snake makes it frightening.'' # Small movement of an object. # Small and progressive changes of a measure. #: ''Few people noticed the '''creep''' of the prices this year.'' # {{informal}} A very annoying person who makes you nervous. #: ''Stop staring at me all the time, you '''creep'''!''
== Verb == {{verb2|creep|creeps|crept|crept|creeping}} {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} An animal '''creeps''' when it moves with its belly close to the ground. {{syn|crawl}} #: ''Snakes and lizards '''creep'''.'' # {{intransitive}} A plant '''creeps''' when it grows close to the ground or stuck to a wall, instead of growing upwards. # {{intransitive}} To move slowly and quietly in a particular direction, like a snake can move. # {{intransitive}} To change slowly and gradually. #: ''When prices '''creep''', some people do not immediately notice the changes.''
=== Related words === * [[creepy]]

== Noun == {{noun}} #A '''replicator''' is a device or a structure that can make copies of itself. #:''Genes are natural '''replicators'''.'' #A '''replicator''' is also a (fictional) man-made device that can make copies of itself, or transform matter to build any object or structure, living or not. #:'''''Replicators''' still belong to science-fiction nowadays, but could exist one day thanks to technological progress.''
=== Related words === *[[replicate]] *[[replication]]

===Pronunciation=== * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈsaɪ.bɔː(r)ɡ/}} * {{audio|en-us-cyborg.ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Noun == {{noun}} #{{context|science fiction}} Mixing of '''''cyb'''ernetic'' and '''''org'''anism'', a '''cyborg''' is a being, usually human, that has an important part of [[mechanical]]/[[robotic]] devices in his or her body. He or she still has an organic brain, [[contrary]] to a robot. #{{context|science fiction}} A true robot that has a relation with organic life, such as looking like a normal human being or having a human [[soul]] inside. #:''Terminator is a '''cyborg'''.''
=== Related words === *[[cybernetic]] *[[organism]]
[[Category:Technology]] [[Category:Science fiction]]

== Expression == {{expression}} [[File:Panasonic-Anrufbeantworter.jpg|thumb|An answering machine]] #An '''answering machine''' is an automatic device on a phone that leaves a message to people calling when you are absent or when you do not want to be phoned. At the end of the message they can also leave you their own message.
=== Related words === *[[machine]] *[[answer]] *[[answering]]
[[Category:Machines]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/kjuːb/}}, {{SAMPA|/kju:b/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/kjub/}}, {{SAMPA|/kjub/}} * {{audio|en-us-cube.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Cube Animation.gif|right|thumb|A '''cube''']] # {{countable}} {{geometry}} A '''cube''' is a shape that has six square faces of the same size. # {{countable}} A '''cube''' is also a solid object that has more or less this shape. #: ''I usually take two sugar '''cubes''' with my coffee.'' # {{countable}} {{context|arithmetic}} The '''cube''' of a number ''n'' is this number multiplied three times by itself. Its symbol is ''n<sup>3</sup>''. #: ''The '''cube''' of 3 is 27, also written 3<sup>3</sup> = 27.''
== Verb == {{verb|cub|e}} # {{context|arithmetic}} To '''cube''' a number is multiplying this number three times by itself. #: ''3 '''cubed''' is 27.'' # To give something the shape of a cube. # {{context|especially cooking}} To cut something into cubes. #: ''To '''cube''' the meat.''
=== Related words === * [[cubic]] * [[cubism]] * [[cubist]] * [[cubium]] * [[cuboid]]
[[Category:Shapes]]

=== Related words === *[[fast]] ; [[faster]] *[[than]] *[[light]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/blaɪnd/}} * {{audio|en-us-blind.ogg|US}}
== Adjective == {{adj|blind|blinder|blindest}} [[File:Blinden, slechtzienden, blindenstokken, looproutes, Bestanddeelnr 932-3839.jpg|thumb|a '''blind''' (''sense 1'') man]] # {{context|not comparable}} If someone or something is '''blind''', they can't [[see]]. #: ''I'm not totally '''blind'''. I can see a little.'' # {{context|comparable}} If someone or something is '''blind''', they can't see the [[truth]] about something. #: ''How can you be so '''blind''' about your problems?'' {{-}} == Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If someone is '''blinded''', they become unable to see. #: ''The light was so bright that for a moment he was blinded.'' #: ''Don't wave that pencil in my face – do you want to blind me?''
== Noun == {{noun}} # A [[covering]] for a [[window]] to keep out light. The covering may be made of cloth or of narrow slats that can block light or allow it to pass. # Any device intended to [[conceal]] or [[hide]]; as, a duck blind. # In [[poker]] a forced bet. #: ''The player was in the big '''blind'''.'' # An 1800s baseball term meaning ''no score''.
== Adverb == {{adv}} # Without seeing; [[unseeingly]]. # In {{w|lang=en|three card brag}}, without [[looking]] at the [[card]]s [[dealt]].
[[Category:Disability]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/bleɪm/}} * {{audio|en-us-blame.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb|blam|e}} # {{transitive}} If you '''blame''' someone or something for something bad, you say or think that they are the reason for or cause of it. #: ''It's not your fault... don't '''blame''' yourself.'' #: ''If you keep asking the woman why he attacked her, you're '''blaming''' the victim.'' #: ''She's changed, but I '''blame''' it on the drugs.'' #: ''Everything's gone wrong, and I want to know who's to '''blame'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[fault]]
== Noun == {{noun4}} # {{uncountable}} The '''blame''' for something bad is the idea that you made or let it happen. #: ''You keep your mouth shut and I'll take the '''blame'''.'' #: ''I went told lies, beat up smaller boys, and put the '''blame''' on someone else.'' #: ''Coaches and players must share the '''blame''' for the worst season in club history.''
=== Synonyms === * [[fault]] * [[responsibility]]
=== Related words === * [[blameless]] * [[blamelessly]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|blĕs}}, {{IPA|/blɛs/}} * {{audio|en-us-bless.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb|bless|es}} # {{transitive}} You say, '''''bless''' you'' when someone [[sneeze]]s. # {{transitive}} You say, '''''bless''' you, him, her,'' etc. when that person has done something nice. # {{transitive}} If you are '''blessed''' with an ability or something, you are lucky to have it. # {{transitive}} If God '''blesses''' something, he gives it special attention and takes care of it.
=== Related words === * [[blessed]] * [[blessing]]
[[Category:Religion]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{enPR|ăl'-ə-vən}}, {{IPA|/ˈæl.ə.vən/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-alevin.wav|UK}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} An '''alevin''' is a young [[salmon]] fish who has just [[hatch]]ed.
=== Related words === * [[fry]] * [[parr]] * [[smolt]]
[[Category:Fishes]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/bluːm/}} * {{audio|en-us-bloom.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''bloom''' is a flower. #: ''The seeds you plant in the spring will give '''blooms''' from summer through fall.'' # {{uncountable}} If something is in '''bloom''', its flowers are open or it is reaching a state of fullness. #: ''The weather is warming and spring flowers are coming into '''bloom'''.'' #: ''She had a wide circle of friends and her career was in full '''bloom''' .'' # {{uncountable}} The '''bloom''' is the best time or a look of freshness or fullness. #: ''The '''bloom''' is off their love.'' #: ''It's wonderful to see the children in the '''bloom''' of youth.'' #: ''As she approached, he saw the round of her hips and the '''bloom''' of her breasts.''
=== Synonyms === * [[flower]] * [[blossom]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} If something such as a flower '''blooms''', it opens, or is reaching a state of fullness. #: ''The blue sky was the color of the sea, and flowers were '''blooming''' in the fields.'' #: ''She had a wide circle of friends and her life was in full bloom.'' #: ''Business is '''blooming''' on this busy street.''
=== Synonyms === * [[flower]] * [[blossom]]
=== Related words === * [[bloomer]] * [[in bloom]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{AU}} {{IPA|/bɒm/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/bɑm/}} * {{audio|en-us-bomb.ogg|US}} * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 bomb.ogg|AU}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''bomb''' is a weapon that [[explode]]s. #: ''The man killed himself and eight others by {{r|detonat|ing}} a very powerful '''bomb'''.'' #: ''On August 6, a U.S. B-29 dropped a 9,000-pound atomic '''bomb''' on Hiroshima.'' #: ''One U.S. soldier and two [[Iraqi]] children were killed when a roadside '''bomb''' exploded in central Baghdad.'' # {{countable}} If something, often a movie or a concert, was a '''bomb''', it was very unsuccessful. #: ''The first computer was a '''bomb''', but IBM improved it and the new machine sold very well.''
<gallery> File:Douglas SBD Dauntless dropping a bomb, circa in 1942.jpg|An airplane dropping a '''bomb'''. File:Pipe bomb - black powder.jpg|An [[explode]]d pipe '''bomb'''. File:Bomb icon.svg|A drawing of a '''bomb'''. </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''bomb''' a place, you drop or put one or more bombs there. #: ''This woman's mother and son were killed when American planes '''bombed''' the village.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''bomb''' somewhere, you go there at high speed. #: ''They walked up the mountain with their bikes and then '''bombed''' down as fast as they could go.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''bomb''' a test, course, etc., you get a very low [[grade]] on it. # {{intransitive}} If something, often a movie or a concert, '''bombs''', it is very unsuccessful. #: ''The show '''bombed''' in London as well as flopping on Broadway.''
=== Related words === *[[bombing]] *[[bomber]]
[[Category:Explosives]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/bɒs/}}, {{SAMPA|/bQs/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|bäs}}, {{IPA|/bɑs/}}, {{SAMPA|/bAs/}} * {{audio|en-us-boss.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=bosses}} # {{countable}} Your '''boss''' is the person who tells you what to do at work. #: ''My former '''boss''' was very happy for the chance to fire me.'' #: ''I started the company because I wanted to be my own '''boss'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''boss''' is a leader in an organisation. #: ''The Mayor was an old-style political '''boss''' who made his own decisions.''
=== Synonyms === * [[employer]] * [[manager]] * [[superior]]
=== Related words === * [[bossy]]
== Verb == {{verb|boss|es}} # {{transitive}} If you '''boss''' somebody around/about, you tell them what to do, especially when you don't have any special power to do so. #: ''This was just another occasion when Indians were '''bossed''' around by white people.''
=== Related words === * [[bossy]]
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # {{slang}} If something is '''boss''', it is very good.
=== Synonyms === * [[cool]]
[[Category:Leaders]]

=== Word parts === {{ety-suffix|fire|woman}}
== Noun == {{irrnoun|firewomen}} [[Image:Karaj Fire Department, Opening of fire station for women - 4 November 2006 (11 8508200540 L600).jpg|thumb|a '''firewoman''']] # {{countable}} A '''firewoman''' is a woman whose job is to fight fires and [[extinguish]] them. This word was created when woman began to do this job and not only men. {{syn|fireman|firefighter}} #: ''The '''firewoman''' sprayed the house with the [[fire hose]].''
=== Related words === * [[fire]] * [[woman]]
[[Category:Jobs]] [[Category:Firefighting]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/bəʊl/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/boʊl/}} * {{audio|en-us-bowl.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''bowl''' is a deep '''dish'''. #: ''In large mixing '''bowl''', [[stir]] together flours, baking powder, and salt until thoroughly combined.'' #: ''Why don't you let me fix you a nice hot '''bowl''' of soup.'' # {{countable}} The '''bowl''' is the part of an object that looks like a bowl. #: ''When's the last time you cleaned the toilet '''bowl'''?'' # {{US}} {{countable}} An important American football game played outside the regular season is sometimes called the ~ '''bowl'''. #: ''These two teams will head to the Super '''Bowl''' to decide the champion.'' # {{US}} {{countable}} A [[stadium]] is sometimes called the ~ bowl. #: ''Every Tuesday and Thursday evening, you can hear the finest classical music at the Hollywood '''Bowl'''.'' <gallery> File:Makutra.jpg|A bowl File:Yoshinoya Donburi 2007.jpg|A '''bowl''' File:Notre-dame-stadium.jpg|A stadium where American Football '''bowl''' games are played </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{ti verb}} {{sport}} If you '''bowl''', you [[roll]] a ball along the ground or floor as part of a game. # {{ti verb}} {{sport}} If you '''bowl''' in '''cricket''', you throw the ball at the [[batsman]]. # {{intransitive}} If you are '''bowling''' along, down, etc., you are moving very fast. #: ''We were '''bowling''' down the hill when we hit a tree.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''bowl''' somebody over, you hit them when you are running and make them fall down.
<gallery> File:BerriganBowls.jpg|People bowling File:Bowlerbowling.JPG|A man bowling File:Darren Gough bowling.jpg|A man is going to bowl the ball in cricket </gallery>
=== Related words === * [[bowling]] * [[bowler]]

=== Other spellings === *{{context|US}} i.e., *i. e. (with a space between) *ie:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˌaɪˈi:/}} * {{audio|en-us-i.e..ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Abbreviation == {{abbreviation}} {{AVL}} #This is a Latin abbreviation for '''''id est''''' (literally "that is"), and is used to explain something by saying it in a different way : ''in other words, which means'' are expressions having roughly the same meaning. #:''They are just liars, '''i.e.''' they never tell the truth.''
=== Synonyms === *[[in other words]]
[[Category:Latin]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/brɔːd/}} * {{audio|en-us-broad.ogg|US}}
== Adjective == {{adj|broad|broader|broadest}} {{AVL}} # If something is '''broad''', the distance from one side to the other is large. #: ''Her shoulders were swimmer's shoulders, strong and '''broad'''.'' # If something is '''broad''', it includes a lot. #: ''They have laws now which give very, very '''broad''' powers to the President.'' #: ''We have a range of activities '''broad''' enough to include teachers in all program areas and in all grade levels.'' # '''Broad''' senses, definitions, agreements, etc. are general, not detailed. #: ''We accept a '''broad''' definition of music to include any sound organized in an meaningful way.'' # A '''broad''' area is a large area. #: ''They walked through the '''broad''' field behind the building.'' # A '''broad''' [[accent]] is one that is very noticeable. # If something happens in '''broad''' daylight, it happens during the day where many people can see it.
=== Synonyms === * [[wide]] * [[general]]
===Antonyms=== * [[narrow]] * [[specific]]
=== Related words === * [[broadly]] * [[broaden]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{slang}} A '''broad''' is a woman. #: ''There's this German '''broad''', fuckin' bitch, who told me I'm going to jail for her pushin' her stupid ass.''
=== Synonyms === * [[chick]] * [[slut]] * [[prostitute]]

{{wikipedia}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/swɒmp/}} * {{audio|en-us-swamp.ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Magnolia-plantation-Audubon-swamp-sc1.jpg|thumb|A swamp]] # {{countable}} A '''swamp''' is an area where most of the land is [[underwater]]. Land in a '''swamp''' is not usually more than a [[meter]] (or a few [[feet]]) under water. #: ''We were [[wade|wading]] through the '''swamp'''.'' #: ''The '''swamp''' is home to many animals, including [[alligator]]s, [[frog]]s, and [[bird]]s.'' #: ''U.S. state of [[Louisiana]] is famous for its '''swamps'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[marsh]] * [[bog]] * [[wetland]]
=== Antonyms === * [[desert]] * [[dry land]]
=== Related words === * [[lake]] * [[pond]] * [[river]] * [[creek]] * [[stream]] * [[sea]] * [[ocean]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # If something is '''swamped''' it is being covered of filled with water. #: ''The deck of our boat was '''swamped''' by the storm.'' # If something is '''swamped''' is has gotten more of something than it can work with. #: ''Our office was '''swamped''' with phone calls.'' #: ''The store was '''swamped''' with customers last night.'' #: ''That many downloads would '''swamp''' our computers.''
=== Synonyms === * [[flood]]
[[Category:Geography]]

=== Other spellings === * [[metre]]
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈmiːtə(r)/}} * {{SAMPA|/"mi:t@(r)/}} * {{audio|en-us-meter.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A [[length]]; 100 [[centimeter]]s. #: ''This table is 2 '''meters''' [[wide]].'' # The [[rhythm]] of a [[poem]].
=== Usage note === This spelling is mostly used in the [[United States]]. The spelling ''metre'' is more common in most of the rest of the world.
[[Category:Units of length]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈkæ.bɪ.nɪt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈkæ.bɪ.nɪt/|/ˈkæb.nɪt/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-cabinet.wav|UK}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Display cabinets.jpg|thumb|Display '''cabinets''']] [[File:Metal File Cabinet.jpg|thumb|Filing '''cabinets''']] # {{countable}} A country's '''cabinet''' is the main group of [[politician]]s who work closely with the leader of the government. #: ''Nearly all the '''cabinet''' ministers in Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu's coalition government are immigrants or the sons of immigrants.'' #: ''He was senior businessman before he joined President Clinton's '''Cabinet''' as Treasury secretary.'' # {{countable}} A '''cabinet''' is a piece of [[furniture]] used to keep things in. #: ''He walked over to the filing '''cabinet''', took out the file and put it on his desk.''
=== Synonyms === * [[cupboard]]
[[Category:Furniture]] [[Category:Government]]

== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''detached house''' is a house standing alone, that has no common wall with another house. #:''People usually prefer '''detached houses''' not to hear the noise their neighbors could do.''
=== Related words === *[[detached]] *[[house]]
== Antonyms == *[[semi-detached house]]
[[Category:Buildings and structures]]

== Noun == {{noun}} #{{countable}} A '''semi-detached house''' is a [[house]] that has a common wall with another house. {{antonyms|detached house}} #:''I don't especially like my '''semi-detached house''' because I can hear what my neighbors do. It's not very intimate.''
=== Related words === *[[semi-detached]] *[[house]]
[[Category:Housing]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/kæɫkjuːleɪt/|/ˈkælkjəleɪt/}} * {{audio|en-us-calculate.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|cal|cu|late}}
== Verb == {{verb|calculat|e}} # {{transitive}} If you '''calculate''' something, you find its value, usually by using [[mathematics]]. #: ''These scores were '''calculated''' by subtracting total errors from total correct.'' #: ''The computers can '''calculate''' how much your family can afford to pay for college.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''calculate''' something, you find the answer by thinking about the facts. #: ''The leaders seems to have '''calculated''' that the political benefit outweighs the cost to their people.'' # {{transitive}} If something is '''calculated''' to do something, you hope or expect it to do it. #: ''She waved her hands around in a way '''calculated''' to make him laugh.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''calculate''' on something, you plan on it or expect it. #: ''He hadn't '''calculated''' on her being late.''
=== Synonyms === * [[figure]] * [[reckon]] * [[expect]]
=== Related words === * [[calculator]] * [[calculating]] * [[calculated]] * [[calculation]] * [[calculative]]

=== Word parts === {{multiword term|medical|student}}
==Noun== {{noun}} # {{countable}} An '''medical student''' is an [[adult]] [[student]] who goes to a [[school]] and is [[learn]]ing to be a [[doctor]] so that they can [[treatment|treat]]s [[sick]] people. #: ''The '''medical student''' has been learning for three years.''
===Synonyms=== * [[student doctor]]
[[Category:Medicine]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈkæn.dɪdət/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈkæn.dɪ.deɪt/|/ˈkæn.dɪ.dɪt/}} * {{audio|en-us-candidate.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''candidate''' is one person or thing that may be chosen, especially in an election. #: ''The three presidential '''candidates''' will be interviewed on TV tonight.'' #: ''Crouch said LaBossiere was the more qualified of the two job '''candidates'''.'' #: ''Because the school has a lot of poor children, it's a good '''candidate''' to receive extra money.''
=== Related words === * [[candidature]] * [[candidacy]]
[[Category:People]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈcɑrpɪt/}}, {{SAMPA|/"cArpIt/}} * {{audio|en-us-carpet.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-uk-carpet.ogg|UK}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''carpet''' is a floor covering, usually made of nylon or wool. #: ''He walked in with his boots leaving snow on the '''carpet'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''carpet''' of something is a thick [[layer]] of it. #: ''A '''carpet''' of snow lay on the ground.''
=== Related words === * [[carpeting]] * [[red carpet]] * [[magic carpet]]
=== Synonyms === * [[rug]] * [[covering]]
<gallery> File:2008-08-24 Carpet array.jpg|Rolls of '''carpet''' File:Red carpet.JPG|A red '''carpet''' File:Farsh Qom.JPG|A [[Persian]] '''carpet''' </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} {{usually passive}} If a floor or room is '''carpeted''', it has carpets on the floor. # {{transitive}} If something '''carpets''' a place, it covers the ground. #: ''The road was '''carpeted''' with broken glass.''
=== Synonyms === * [[cover]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|kăsh}}, {{IPA|/kæʃ/}} * {{SAMPA|k{S}} * {{audio|en-us-cash.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun4}} [[File:Symbol-Money.svg|thumb|'''Cash''' in dollar bills and coins]] # {{uncountable}} '''Cash''' is money in the form of [[bill]]s and [[coin]]s, rather than [[check]]s/[[cheque]]s or [[credit card]]s. #: ''The publisher supplied '''cash''' prizes and books for the winning essays written by fourth through sixth graders.'' #: ''Payment is by '''cash''', VISA, or MasterCard.''
=== Related words === * [[cashier]] * [[cash register]] * [[cash flow]] * [[cash cow]]
== Verb == {{verb|cash|es}} # {{transitive}} To [[exchange]] a check/cheque for money in the form of bills. #: ''I need to stop at the back to '''cash''' my paycheck before we go out to dinner.''
[[Category:Money]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{enPR|käst}}, {{IPA|/kɑːst/}}, {{SAMPA|/kA:st/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|kăst}}, {{IPA|/kæst/}}, {{SAMPA|/k{st/}} * {{audio|en-us-cast.ogg|US}} * {{hmp|caste}}
== Verb == {{verb2|cast|casts|cast|cast|casting}} [[File:Full-disk Color Image of Crescent Saturn with Rings and Ring Shadows.jpg|thumb|[[Saturn]] '''casting''' a shadow on its rings]] # {{transitive}} If <math>x</math> casts light or [[shadow]] on <math>y</math>, <math>x</math> causes <math>y</math> to be lit or in [[shadow]]. #: ''The street light outside my window '''cast''' shadows on the wall.'' #: ''The campfire '''cast''' a warm light on her face.'' # {{transitive}} If you cast light on an idea or problem, you make it clearer by giving more information about it. #: ''Our research '''casts''' new light on the connection between temperature and plant growth.'' # {{transitive}} If you cast doubt on something, you make make people less likely to believe it. #: ''The video '''casts''' doubt on the story told by police.'' # {{ti verb}} If you cast a look, glance, you look quickly. #: ''She '''cast''' about for her pen.'' #: ''He '''cast''' a quick look at the TV.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''cast''' a [[vote]], you vote in an [[election]]. #: ''I've decided to '''cast''' my vote for the Democratic Party.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''cast''' metal, plastic, etc., you make an object by applying wet or melted material to another material and waiting for it to harden. # {{transitive}} If you '''cast''' somebody in a part in a play, movie, etc., you choose them to play that part. # {{transitive}} If you '''cast''' something somewhere, you throw it there.
=== Synonyms === * [[throw]] * [[mould]]
=== Related words === * [[-cast]] * [[casting]]
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Skateboard-cast-broken leg-690475-l.jpg|thumb|A boy with a '''cast''' on his leg]] [[File:Plaster mask.jpg|thumb|Making a cast of a face]] # {{countable}} The '''cast''' of a play, movie, or show are all the people who act in it. #: ''The director has brought back many of the '''cast''' and crew of the earlier movie.'' # {{countable}} The '''cast''' of [[character]]s is the complete list of characters. # {{countable}} A '''cast''' is a hard protective covering on part of your body that has been seriously hurt or broken. # {{countable}} A '''cast''' is a shape made by applying wet or melted material to another material and waiting for it to harden. # {{countable}} A '''cast''' is a throw, especially in fishing when you throw your line out.
=== Synonyms === * [[throw]] * [[mould]]
[[Category:People]] [[Category:Acting]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/sɛl/}} {{SAMPA|/sEl/}} * {{audio|en-us-cell.ogg|US}} * {{hmp|cel|sell}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Cell Alcatraz Federal Prison.JPG|thumb|A jail '''cell'''.]] [[File:Biological cell.svg|thumb|A '''cell'''.]] # {{countable}} A '''cell''' is a [[room]] in a [[jail]] where [[prisoner]]s are kept. #: ''He was arrested and kept in a small '''cell''' for one day.'' # {{countable}} {{biology}} A '''cell''' is a [[unit]] of a living [[organism]]. #: ''A plant '''cell''' has a cell wall.''

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈtʃærɪti/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈtʃɛrəti/}} * {{audio|en-us-charity.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=charities}} # {{countable}} A '''charity''' is an organisation that collects money or [[good]]s and uses them to help poor or sick people, often with the help of [[volunteer]]s. #: ''The group, a Catholic '''charity''' that runs schools on Indian reservations, collected nearly $17 million from the public.'' #: ''The party was a '''charity''' event that raised over $400,000 to fight breast cancer.'' #: ''The money was given away to local '''charities'''.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Charity''' is the work of helping the poor and the sick. #: ''All the money raised goes to '''charity'''.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Charity''' is the money, goods, or help that people give to the poor and the sick. #: ''Our family was poor, but my mother would never accept '''charity'''.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Charity''' is the quality of being kind, thoughtful, and helpful. #: ''He led a life of '''charity'''.''
=== Related words === * [[charitable]]
[[Category:Organizations]] [[Category:Philanthropy]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/tʃeɪs/}} * {{audio|en-us-chase.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-au-chase.ogg|AU}}
== Verb == {{verb|chas|e}} [[File:Acd diving.jpg|thumb|One dog '''chasing''' another]] # {{ti verb}} If you '''chase''' something, you go after it quickly. #: ''Dogs often play at '''chasing''' their own tail.'' #: ''In my dream, someone's '''chasing''' after me and I'm running down this street.'' #: ''The children were '''chasing''' the ball down the soccer field.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''chase''' somebody or something away, you make them leave. #: ''He waved his arms to '''chase''' the birds out of the cherry tree.''
=== Related words === * [[chaser]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''chase''' is an act of going quickly after something or trying to get it. #: ''TV has too many high-speed car '''chases'''.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/tʃæt/}} * {{audio|en-us-chat.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb|chat|t}} [[File:Cit-cat.jpg|thumb|These women are '''chatting''']] # {{intransitive}} If two or more people '''chat''', they talk with each other in a [[casual]] way, sometimes by typing on a [[computer]] or [[cell phone]]. #: ''His friends dropped by frequently just to '''chat'''.'' #: ''The band was taking a break and '''chatting''' with the guests.''
=== Related words === * [[chatty]]
=== Related words === * [[chatroom]] * [[chat up]] * [[chit-chat]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''chat''' is a casual [[conversation]], sometimes by typing on a computer or cell phone. #: ''People come to the bar to have a drink and a '''chat'''.''
[[Category:Communication]]

A [[proposed]] [[country]] is a country which has been suggested and discussed but never created.

[[Category:Countries|*]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/t͡ʃɪə(r)/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/t͡ʃɪr/}} * {{audio|en-us-cheer.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{ti verb}} If you '''cheer''', you [[shout]] to show that you are happy about something or to encourage someone. #: ''The band begins to play and the crowd '''cheers'''.'' #: ''People '''cheered''' the home team wildly.'' #: ''We hope everybody will come out and '''cheer''' on the runners.'' # {{ti verb}} If something '''cheers''' somebody, it makes them feel happier. #: ''There isn't much on the street to '''cheer''' the poor.''
=== Antonyms === * [[discourage]]
=== Related words === * [[cheer up]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''cheer''' is a shout to show that you are happy about something or to encourage someone. #: ''As the clock counted down the final seconds of the game the '''cheers''' from the crowd grew louder and louder.'' #: ''Three '''cheers''' for the raiders! Hip hip hooray!'' # {{uncountable}} '''Cheer''' is a feeling of happiness. #: ''Thanksgiving is a time for families to gather with good '''cheer''' and put problems behind them.''
=== Related words === * [[cheers]] * [[cheerless]] * [[cheerlessness]] * [[cheerlessly]] * [[cheery]] * [[cheeriness]] * [[cheerily]] * [[cheerleader]]

=== Other spellings === * [[check]]
=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|chĕk}}, {{IPA|/tʃɛk/}} * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 cheque.ogg|AU}} * {{hmp|check|Czech}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''cheque''' is a written [[promise]] that allows the receiver to take [[money]] from a [[bank account]]. It is used instead of [[cash]] to pay for things. #: ''Do you take personal '''cheques'''?'' #: ''Did you cash the '''cheque''' yet?'' #: ''I wrote them a '''cheque''' for $300.''
[[Category:Money]] [[Category:Banking]]

{{documentation subpage}} This template is used for citing websites. == Usage == ;Common form for cases where little is known about authorship of the page (with current date) {{cite web |url= |title= |accessdate={{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}} |format= |work= }} ;Using last, first (with current date) {{cite web |url= |title= |accessdate={{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}} |last= |first= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;Using author (with current date) {{cite web |url= |title= |accessdate={{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}} |author= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;Using non-linked retrieved date, last, first {{cite web |url= |title= |accessmonthday= |accessyear= |last= |first= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;Using non-linked retrieved date, author {{cite web |url= |title= |accessmonthday= |accessyear= |author= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;All parameters, horizontal format (delete the ones you don't need) {{cite web |url= |title= |accessdate= |accessmonthday= |accessdaymonth = |accessyear= |author= |last= |first= |authorlink= |coauthors= |date= |year= |month= |format= |work= |publisher= |pages= |language= |doi= |archiveurl= |archivedate= |quote= }} ;All parameters, vertical format 
{{cite web
|url=
|title=
|accessdate=
|accessdaymonth=
|accessmonthday=
|accessyear=
|author=
|last=
|first=
|authorlink=
|coauthors=
|date=
|year=
|month=
|format=
|work=
|publisher=
|pages=
|language=
|doi=
|archiveurl=
|archivedate=
|quote=
}}
=== Required parameters === *'''url''': URL of online item. *'''title''': Title of online item. ''For producing a [[WP:CONTEXT#Dates|wikilinked date]] of retrieval:'' :*'''accessdate''': Full date when item was accessed, in [[ISO 8601]] YYYY-MM-DD format, for example "accessdate = {{CURRENTYEAR}}-{{CURRENTMONTH}}-{{CURRENTDAY2}}". ''Must not be wikilinked'' ''For producing a non-wikilinked date of retrieval:'' :*'''accessmonthday''' and '''accessyear''': Month and day when item was accessed, for example "accessmonthday = May 10", and year when item was accessed, for example "accessyear = 2005". Produces: ''Retrieved on May 10, 2006.'' :*'''accessdaymonth''' and '''accessyear''': Month and day when item was accessed, for example "accessmonthday = 10 May", and year when item was accessed, for example "accessyear = 2005". Produces: ''Retrieved on 10 May 2006.'' === Optional parameters === *'''author''': Author **'''last''' works with '''first''' to produce last, first **'''authorlink''' works either with '''author''' or with '''last''' & '''first''' to link to the appropriate wikipedia article. Does not work with URLs. **'''coauthors''': allows additional authors *'''date''': Full date of publication, preferably in [[ISO 8601]] YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. ''2006-02-17''. May be wikilinked. **OR: '''year''': Year of publication, and '''month''': Name of the month of publication. If you also have the day, use ''date'' instead. Must not be wikilinked. *'''format''': Format, e.g. PDF. HTML implied if not specified. *'''work''': If this item is part of a larger work, name of that work. *'''publisher''': Publisher, if any. *'''pages''': ''pp. 5–7'': first page and optional last page. This is for listing the pages relevant to the citation, not the total number of pages in the book. This is especially useful for [[PDF]] format, where the page can be linked to with the #page=''number'' anchor tagged on the end of the URL: *:pages = [http://www.example.org/file.pdf#page=123 p. 123] *'''language''': language of publication (don't specify "English" as this is the default). * '''doi''': A [[digital object identifier]] for the document, such as ''10.1038/news070508-7'' **'''Doilabel''': If the doi contains some characters that must be [[Percent-encoding|escaped]], use "doilabel" for the unescaped version. See {{tl|doi}}: "id" is equivalent to "doi" and "label" is "doilabel" *'''archiveurl''': URL of the archive location of the item (requires '''archivedate''') *'''archivedate''': Date when the item was archived (requires '''archiveurl'''), in [[ISO 8601]] YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g. ''2006-02-17''. Must not be wikilinked; it will be linked automatically. *'''quote''': Relevant quote from online item. ==Examples== ;Some standard use cases *{{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |publisher=Open Publishing |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |publisher=Open Publishing |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} *{{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} *{{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} *{{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |author=Doe, John |title=My favorite things part II |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} *{{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} *{{cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/fans/ |title=Digest of rules |publisher= National Football League |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/fans/ |title=Digest of rules |publisher= National Football League |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} ;Non-linking date of retrieval (using accessmonthday and accessyear) *{{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessmonthday=July 6 |accessyear=2005 }}
→ {{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessmonthday=July 6 |accessyear=2005 }} ;Using format *{{cite web |title=List of psychotropic substances under international control |publisher=International Narcotics Control Board |url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |format=PDF |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |title=List of psychotropic substances under international control |publisher=International Narcotics Control Board |url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |format=PDF |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} ;language *{{cite web |author=Joliet, François |title=Honnit soit qui mal y pense |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 |language=French }}
→ {{cite web |author=Joliet, François |title=Honnit soit qui mal y pense |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 |language=French }} ;coauthors *{{cite web |first=John |last=Doe |coauthors=Peter Smith, Jim Smythe |title=My favorite things part II |publisher=Open Publishing |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2006-05-16 }}
→ {{cite web |first=John |last=Doe |coauthors=Peter Smith, Jim Smythe |title=My favorite things part II |publisher=Open Publishing |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2006-05-16 }} ;No author *{{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |publisher=Open Publishing |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2006-05-16 }}
→ {{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |publisher=Open Publishing |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ | accessdate=2006-05-16 }} ;No author, no publisher *{{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }}
→ {{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 }} *{{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06}}
→ {{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06}} *{{cite web |title=List of psychotropic substances under international control |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |format=PDF |accessdate=2005-07-06 |language=Greek }}
→ {{cite web |title=List of psychotropic substances under international control |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |format=PDF |accessdate=2005-07-06 |language=Greek }} ;Using archiveurl and archivedate to refer to items that went away but are available from an archive site *{{cite web |title=List of psychotropic substances under international control |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |format=PDF |accessdate=2005-07-06 |archiveurl=http://www.archive.org/2005-09-11/www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |archivedate=2005-09-11 }}
→ {{cite web |title=List of psychotropic substances under international control |date=[[2005-04-30]] |url=http://www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |format=PDF |accessdate=2005-07-06 |archiveurl=http://www.archive.org/2005-09-11/www.incb.org/pdf/e/list/green.pdf |archivedate=2005-09-11 }} *{{cite web |url=http://joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi?archive=currnews&story=20060405-01shore.htm |title=Interview with Maggie Downs |date=[[2006-03-31]] |publisher=The Desert Sun |archiveurl=http://72.14.207.104/search?q=cache:JAxf4v-pQmgJ:joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi%3Farchive%3Dcurrnews%26story%3D20060405-01shore.htm |archivedate=2006-04-26 }}
→ {{cite web |url=http://joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi?archive=currnews&story=20060405-01shore.htm |title=Interview with Maggie Downs |date=[[2006-03-31]] |publisher=The Desert Sun |archiveurl=http://72.14.207.104/search?q=cache:JAxf4v-pQmgJ:joanjettbadrep.com/cgi-bin/fullStory.cgi%3Farchive%3Dcurrnews%26story%3D20060405-01shore.htm |archivedate=2006-04-26 }} ;Using quote *{{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 |quote=Lorem ipsum dolor. }}
→ {{cite web |title=My favorite things part II |work=Encyclopedia of things |url=http://www.example.org/ |accessdate=2005-07-06 |quote=Lorem ipsum dolor. }} ;No parameters (error) *{{cite web}}

===Pronunciation=== * {{audio|en-us-hermit.ogg|Audio (US)}} * {{hyphenation|her|mit}}
==Noun== {{noun}} #{{countable}} A '''hermit''' is a person who lives [[alone]], far from other people, and does not like to [[interact]] with other people. #:''We walked far and came to the house of the '''hermit''' who lives in the forest.'' #{{countable}} A '''hermit''' is a [[religious]] person who lives alone and does not like to interact with other people for religious reasons.
===Related words=== * [[hermit crab]] * [[hermitage]] * [[hermitize]]
===Synonyms=== * [[recluse]]
[[Category:People]]

==Noun== {{noun}} [[File:Grab von franz kafka.jpg|thumb|Franz Kafka's gravestone]] #A '''gravestone''' is a [[stone]] on a [[grave]], usually with the name of the dead person written on it. #:''The old '''gravestone''' was smooth from many years of rain, but she could still read the name on it.''
===Related words=== *[[grave]] *[[stone]]
===Synonyms=== *[[headstone]] *[[tombstone]]
[[Category:Burial]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈæŋ.kəl/}} * {{audio|en-us-ankle.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun|ankle}} [[File:Ankle.jpg|thumb|A human '''ankle''']] # {{countable}} The '''ankle''' is the joint between the foot and the leg. #: ''She [[sprain]]ed her '''ankle''' when she fell on the ice.''
=== Related words === * [[foot]] * [[leg]]
[[Category:Body parts]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{AU}} {{IPA|/aːk/}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ɑː(r)k/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|klerk}}, {{IPA|/klɝk/}} * {{audio|en-us-clerk.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''clerk''' is a person who keeps an organization's records. #: ''I called the city '''clerk''''s office to see if they had a record of her birth.'' # {{countable}} A sales '''clerk''' is the person in a shop who helps you find things you want to buy. #: ''A convenience store '''clerk''' was arrested for selling cigarettes to children.'' # {{countable}} A desk '''clerk''' is the person at a hotel who registers guests. #: ''The desk '''clerk''' called a taxi for us.'' # {{countable}} A law '''clerk''' is a person, often a junior lawyer, who is the assistant of a judge or another lawyer.
=== Related words === * [[clerkship]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # If you '''clerk''', you work as a clerk, especially as a law clerk. #: ''She '''clerked''' for the judge in 1992, and says she and her fellow clerks worked "as many hours as we could stay awake, often past midnight and on weekends."''
[[Category:People]] [[Category:Legal jobs]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/klaɪm/}} * {{audio|en-us-climb.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb}} [[File:Baumklettern in Eiche.jpg|thumb|a girl climbing a [[tree]]]] # {{ti verb}} If you '''climb''' something, you [[move]] up or down it. #: ''They '''climbed''' the stairs to the top of the [[tower]] again and went out onto the roof.'' #: ''The kids spent the afternoon '''climbing''' up and down the tree.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''climb''' into, out of, through something, etc., you move with [[difficulty]], often using your hands and knees. #: ''The old man '''climbed''' into the back seat of her small car.'' #: ''They got changed, said good night, and '''climbed''' into bed.'' #: ''They '''climbed''' out of the pool and walked toward the changing room.'' # {{intransitive}} If prices, [[profit]]s, temperatures, etc. '''climb''' or if a road, a path, or a piece of land '''climbs''', it goes up. #: ''This year, gas prices have '''climbed''' steadily from a low of 75 cents to a peak of almost $1.30 in August.'' #: ''Narrow steps '''climb''' to the door of a small [[temple]].'' #: ''It became very warm as the sun began to '''climb'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[rise]] * [[crawl]]
=== Antonyms === * [[descend]]
=== Related words === * [[climber]] * [[unclimbed]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''climb''' is an upwards movement, often a slow or difficult one. #: ''It isn't far, but it's a steep '''climb''' and they were sweating when they reach the top.'' #: ''Driving into the east end of town after a long winding '''climb''' out of the [[valley]], I saw the small house.'' #: ''The Yen has made a strong '''climb''' this year.'' # {{countable}} A '''climb''' down is a long slow downwards movement.
=== Synonyms === * [[rise]] * [[crawl]]
=== Antonyms === * [[descent]]
=== Related words === * [[climb-down]]

=== Word parts === {{compound|hill|billy}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈhɪlˌbɪli/}} * {{audio|en-us-hillbilly.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=hillbillies}} # {{countable}} A person who lives in the [[country]] in an area with many [[hill]]s, and who has little [[money]]. Usually, this means an [[American]] from a [[region]] called [[Appalachia]] or a region called the [[Ozark Mountains]]. These people have [[home]]s and [[farm]]s in the [[valley]]s between the hills. #: ''My dad is a '''hillbilly''' from eastern [[Kentucky]].'' #: ''People often make fun of '''hillbillies''' without ever actually knowing one.''
=== Usage notes === Some people call themselves '''hillbillies''' but other people are insulted to be called '''hillbillies'''.
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # Having to do with hillbillies, or typical of hillbillies.
=== Related words === * [[hillbilly music]]
[[Category:People]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/kluː/}} * {{audio|en-au-clue.ogg|AU}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''clue''' is a piece of information that helps you answer a question or solve a problem. #: ''He said nothing, made no gesture, and gave no '''clue''' about what he was thinking.'' #: ''Something in those boxes might provide a '''clue''' to his death.'' #: ''She disappeared without a '''clue'''.'' # {{informal}} {{singular}} If you have no '''clue''' about something, you don't know at all. #: ''I'm afraid I have no '''clue''' how to get there.'' #: ''Don't ask him. He doesn't have a '''clue''' about computers.'' #: ''The guy's an idiot. He hasn't got a '''clue'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[hint]] * [[idea]] * [[trace]]
=== Related words === * [[clueless]]
== Verb == {{verb|clu|e}} # {{ti verb}} {{informal}} If you '''clue''' somebody in to something, you give them that information that they didn't have. #: ''I had no idea what she was angry about until my sister '''clued''' me in.'' #: ''The look on her face finally '''clued''' me in: she didn't speak English.'' #: ''I finally '''clued''' in to the fact that it wasn't going to work.''
=== Related words === * [[clued]] in / out

=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|kwîr}}, {{IPA|/kwir/}} * {{SAMPA|/kwir/}} * {{audio|en-us-queer.ogg|US}}
== Adjective == {{adj|queer|queerer|queerest}} # If something is '''queer''', it is a little bit [[strange]], it is not quite [[normal]]. # {{dated}}{{slang}} If someone feels queer, that person is mentally strange or sick. # {{slang}} {{context|see usage notes}} Another word for [[homosexual]] or for [[LGBT]] people [[in general]]. It is sometimes used as a [[derogatory]] term and some people see it as a [[slur]]. # {{context|see usage notes}} [[denoting|Denoting]] or relating to a sexual or gender [[identity]] that does not [[correspond]] to [[established]] ideas of [[sexuality]] and [[gender]], especially heterosexual norms.
== Usage notes == * The word '''queer''' meaning [[homosexual]] (senses '''3''' and '''4''', and the '''noun''' sense) is still considered highly [[derogatory]] and [[offensive]] when used by non-[[homosexuals]] (especially [[heterosexuals]], not [[gay]], [[lesbian]], [[bisexual]] and [[pansexual]] etc.) or people who does ''not'' [[identify]] as queer, it is often used by gay man themselves as a [[positive]] and [[inoffensive]] term, such as ''queer cinema, queer politics''.
=== Synonyms === * {{a|not normal}} [[odd]], [[strange]], [[weird]], [[unusual]], [[bizarre]] * {{a|homosexual}} [[gay]]
=== Antonyms === * [[normal]] * [[straight]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{slang}} {{offensive}} {{context|see usage notes above}} A person who is [[homosexual]]. # {{context|see usage notes above}} A person whose gender [[identity]] is [[nonbinary]] or differs from the sex they had or were [[identified]] as having at [[birth]].
=== Synonyms === * [[gay]] * [[fairy]] * [[faggot]] * [[fag]]
=== Related words === * [[genderqueer]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{slang}} To '''queer''' somebody's pitch means to [[upset]] someone's plans. # {{rare}} To '''queer''' something is to see it, [[examine]] it, or show it from a queer [[perspective]].

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/kəʊtʃ/}}, {{SAMPA|/k@UtS/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/koʊtʃ}}, {{SAMPA|/koUtS/}} * {{audio|en-us-coach.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun|2=coaches}} [[File:NarrowGauge coach Vígľaš.jpg|thumb|A '''coach'''.]] # {{countable}} {{sport}} A '''coach''' is a teacher of a sport. #: ''Even though his team won, first-year '''coach''' Andrew Johnson was not happy.'' #: ''Parkview's new assistant girls soccer '''coach''' Karen Kingston has led the Panthers team to a 4-1 record.'' #: ''Mrs. Schenkman, the seventh grade girls' basketball '''coach''', had ended practice for the day.'' # {{countable}} A '''coach''' is a private teacher, often to help prepare for a particular test, job, or situation. # {{countable}} A '''coach''' is a bus or a car of a train with seats for many people. #: ''Thomas the Tank Engine was pulling his '''coaches''' Annie and Clarabel back into Knapford Station.'' # {{countable}} A '''coach''' is a vehicle pulled by a horse.
=== Synonyms === * [[tutor]] * [[trainer]] * [[instructor]]
== Verb == {{verb|coach|es}} # {{ti verb}}, {{sport}} If you '''coach''' a person or a team, you teach them how to do a sport. #: ''She '''coaches''' girls gymnastics at Middlebury High School.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''coach''' someone, you help them prepare for a particular test, job, or situation.
=== Synonyms === * [[train]] * [[instruct]]
[[Category:People]]

== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Cervus cashmeerianus Smit.jpg|thumb|A Kashmir stag]] #The '''Kashmir stag''' ''({{w|Cervus canadensis hanglu}})'' is a type of [[red deer]] native to northern [[Pakistan]] and [[India]].
[[Category:Mammals]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|kōst}} * {{IPA|/kəʊst/}} * {{SAMPA|/k@Ust/}} * {{audio|en-us-coast.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} The '''coast''' is the area of land closest to the sea. #: ''The hotel was near the '''coast''' and their room had a balcony from which they could see the distant ocean.'' #: ''The numbers of fish along the Atlantic '''coast''' declined from heavy fishing, construction of dams, and pollution.'' # If the '''coast''' is clear, nobody is looking, so you can do something without anyone knowing. #: ''He looked out the window to see if the '''coast''' was clear.''
=== Related words === * [[coastal]]
<gallery> File:Barbados_beach.jpg|A sandy coast File:Cliffs_and_foreshore_at_Boulby.jpg|A rocky coast File:Ca-map.png|Canada with St. John's on the east coast and Prince Rupert on the west coast </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} If a vehicle '''coasts''', it continues to move forward without needing new energy. #: ''The car gradually '''coasted''' to a stop.'' #: ''He rested as the bike '''coasted''' down the hill.''
[[Category:Landforms]]

=== Pronunciation === ;verb * {{enPR|kəm-bīn'}}, {{IPA|/kəmˈbaɪn/}} * {{SAMPA|/k@m"baIn/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-combine (verb).wav|UK}}
;noun * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈkɒm.baɪn/}}, {{SAMPA|/"kQm.baIn/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|käm'bīn}}, {{IPA|/ˈkɑm.baɪn/}}, {{SAMPA|/"kAm.baIn/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-combine (noun).wav|UK}}
== Verb == {{verb|combin|e}} {{AVL}} # {{ti verb}} If you '''combine''' two or more things, you put them together. #: ''In a large bowl, '''combine''' 1/2 cup white sugar and cinnamon.'' #: ''Her new book '''combines''' elements of similar stories told throughout eastern North America.'' #: ''All of these factors '''combine''' to create a system that is difficult to understand.'' # {{transitive}} If something combines two or more things, it has both/all of them. #: ''This is a world that '''combines''' the old with the new.''
=== Synonyms === * [[mix]] * [[join]] * [[incorporate]] * [[join]] * [[link]]
=== Antonyms === * [[separate]] * [[divide]]
=== Related words === * [[combination]] * [[recombine]] * [[recombination]] * [[recombinant]]
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Claas-lexion-570-1.jpg|thumb|A combine]] # {{countable}} A '''combine''' is a large farm vehicle the cuts grain and separates the seeds.

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/kəˈmɑːnd/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/kəˈmænd/}} * {{audio|en-us-command.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|com|mand}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{uncountable}} '''Command''', is the power to control people or things. #: ''The information moved from the soldiers up the chain of '''command''' right to the president.'' #: ''Machine-gun fire swept through the general's '''command''' post.'' #: ''With their centralized '''command''' structure, it's hard to believe that it could be an accidental action.'' #: ''We'll look at the problems they face and the military options at their '''command'''. '' #: ''These women reject the idea that they are under their husband's '''command'''.'' #: ''We have not leader. Somebody needs to take '''command''' and get us moving.'' #: ''Saddam Hussein was in '''command''' of one of the world's biggest military machines.'' # {{cu noun}} '''Command''' is the people or place that '''orders''' come from. #: ''This operation was planned carefully from the central '''command'''. '' #: ''Reporters recently spoke to leaders at the Army's Strategic Defense '''Command'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''command''' is a direction for a computer to do something. #: ''A complicated '''command''' like "COPY: *. *B:PRNT1 i" could take some time for the computer to complete.'' # {{countable}} A '''command''' is an order that somebody do something or that something happen. #: ''He gave the '''command''' to attack.'' # {{cu noun}} If you have '''command''' of something, you understand it well. #: ''He has an excellent '''command''' of both French and Spanish.''
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''command''' someone to do something, you tell them to do it because you have power over them. #: ''He'd first joined the Army in 1969 and '''commanded''' a unit in Vietnam.'' #: ''"That's quite enough of that. Stop it right now," '''commanded''' his teacher.'' # {{transitive}} If you command attention, respect, etc., you get it because you should get it. #: ''The amazing power of weather '''commands''' respect and fear.'' #: ''Her fire-red hair '''commanded''' attention.'' #: ''The wines from 1989 from that area today '''command''' high prices.''
=== Related words === * [[commanding]] * [[commander]] * [[commandment]] * [[commando]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/θʌmp/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-I learned some phrases-thump.wav|UK}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''thump''' something, you [[hit]] it, often with your closed hand. # {{ti verb}} If something '''thumps''', it hits something else, making a loud, low sound. # {{intransitive}} If your heart '''thumps''', it beats so strongly and quickly that you can easily notice it.
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''thump''' is a loud, low sound made when something hits something else. # {{countable}} A '''thump''' is the action of something hits something else.
=== Synonyms === * [[punch]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈkɒn.sən.treɪt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈkɑn.sən.treɪt/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-concentrate.wav|UK}}
== Verb == {{verb|concentrat|e}} # {{intransitive}} If you '''concentrate''' on something, you use most of your time and work there. #: ''We '''concentrated''' our rebuilding efforts on villages in the North of the city, where most of the damage had been done.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''concentrate''' on something, you think about it and not about other things. #: ''I went to a quiet room so I could '''concentrate'''.'' #: ''It's better to look at the big picture instead of '''concentrating''' on the details.'' # {{intransitive}} {{usually passive}} If something is '''concentrated''' somewhere, there is a lot of it in that place. #: ''The fighting was '''concentrated''' in a few small areas.''
=== Related words === * [[concentrated]] * [[concentration]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{cu noun}} A '''concentrate''' is a liquid such as juice or chemicals from which most of the water has been removed. #: ''Instead of fresh orange juice, we usually make it from '''concentrate'''.''

== Verb == {{verb|consum|e}} # {{transitive}} If you '''consume''' energy, [[resource]]s, time, etc., you use it and it is no longer available. #: ''Only 10% of the energy '''consumed''' by a light bulb produces usable light.'' #: ''Most of our leisure time is '''consumed''' by TV.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''consume''' [[alcohol]], food, etc., you eat or drink it. #: ''They discovered that about half the calories '''consumed''' by an adult bat are used up during flight.'' #: ''Pregnant women should not '''consume''' alcohol.'' #: ''Many people do not '''consume''' adequate amounts of food for good health.'' # {{transitive}} If a fire '''consumes''' something, it burns it until it's gone. #: ''In 1988 a fire '''consumed''' about half of the park's trees.'' # {{transitive}} If you are '''consumed''' by a thought or idea, you cannot think about anything else. #: ''Our minds were '''consumed''' by the things we saw and dreamed of having.''
=== Antonyms === * [[produce]]
=== Related words === * [[consumer]] * [[consuming]] * [[consumption]] * [[consumerism]] * [[consumable]]

== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If two things are '''distinct''', they are [[clearly]] different or separate. #: ''Sports [[psychologist]]s recognized that there were two '''distinct''' types of athletes who could become gold-medal winners.'' #: ''There are aspects of this group's identity that are '''distinct''' from other groups from the same area.'' #: ''They are a separate people with a '''distinct''' language, identity and culture.'' # {{attrib}} A '''distinct''' impression, advantage, [[possibility]], etc. is one that clearly exists. #: ''I had the '''distinct''' impression that he was secretly laughing at me.'' #: ''The change gives the government a '''distinct''' advantage.'' #: ''With the cold, snow was a '''distinct''' possibility.'' # If something is '''distinct''', it can be clearly seen, heard, or sensed. #: ''As Gillian approached Theo's dressing room, the angry voices became more '''distinct'''.''
=== Antonyms === * [[indistinct]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/deə(r)/}}, {{SAMPA|/de@(r)/}} * {{audio|en-us-dare.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb|dar|e}} # If you '''dare''' to do something, you have the [[courage]] to do it, even if you are [[afraid]]. #: ''The President '''dared''' to make an unpopular decision.'' # If you '''dare''' someone to do something, you [[challenge]] them to do something that is a [[risk]], or even [[dangerous]]. #: ''I '''dare''' you to climb that tree.''
== Verb == {{verb4|dare|dared|daren't}} :''Note: The modal form is usually used in a [[negative]] statement or in a [[question]].'' # {{Modal}} If you '''dare''' not do something, you are afraid to do it. #: ''I '''daren't''' tell my parents what happened. They'll be very cross.'' #: '''''Dare''' he risk crossing the woods at night?'' #: ''He '''dare''' not enter.'' # {{Modal}} You say ''How dare someone do something?'' to show that you are angry about something that someone has done. #: ''How '''dare''' you come in here without knocking?''
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''dare''' is a [[challenge]] to somebody. #: ''He never says "No" to a '''dare'''.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/dæm/}} * {{SAMPA|/d{m/}} * {{audio|en-us-damn.ogg|Audio (US)}} * {{hmp|dam}}
== Interjection == {{interjection}} # {{slang}} You say '''damn''' when you are angry or surprised about something. {{syn|darn|dang}} #: '''''Damn'''! That hurts. Be careful.'' #: '''''Damn'''! This machine isn't working again.''
== Adverb == {{adv}} # {{slang}} If something is '''damn''' good, '''damn''' sure, etc., it is very much that way. #: ''I want to make '''damn''' sure he knows about it.'' #: ''You know '''damn''' well I don't drive.'' #: ''Be careful! You '''damn''' near killed me.''
== Adjective == {{adj}} # {{attrib}} {{slang}} You use '''damn''' to show that you are [[angry]]. #: ''He doesn't know a '''damn''' thing about fixing cars.'' #: ''Don't be such a '''damn''' fool.''
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} {{slang}} {{context|usually subjunctive}} You say "'''damn''' you" or "'''damn''' (something)" to show that you are [[angry]] or that you don't [[care]]. #: ''He slammed his glass down on the table." I am dying, God '''damn''' it, dying!"'' # {{transitive}} {{slang}} {{context|usually passive}} You say "I'll be '''damned'''" to show that you are surprised. #: ''You mean I was right? Well, I'll be '''damned'''!'' # {{transitive}} {{slang}} {{context|usually passive}} You say "I'll be '''damned''' if something happens" to show that you don't want it to happen or that you don't think it will happen. # {{transitive}} {{context|usually passive}} If someone is '''damned''', go to [[hell]] when they die. #: ''Living that way will '''damn''' your soul to Hell.'' #: ''Demons and monsters were in the army of the '''damned'''.''
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} {{slang}} If you don't give a '''damn''', you don't [[care]]. #: ''Look, don't tell me about your problems. I don't give a '''damn'''.'' # {{countable}} {{slang}} If something isn't worth a '''damn''', it has no value.
=== Synonyms === * [[fuck]] * [[shit]]
=== Related words === * [[damnable]] * [[damnedest]] * [[damnation]]

=== Pronunciation === ;noun * {{enPR|kŏn'tĕnt}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/'kɒntɛnt/}}, {{SAMPA|/"kQntEnt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/'kɑntɛnt/}}, {{SAMPA|/"kAntEnt/}} * {{audio|en-us-content.ogg|US}} ;adjective * {{enPR|kəntĕnt'}} * {{IPA|/kən'tɛnt/}} * {{SAMPA|/k@n"tEnt}}
== Noun == {{noun}} {{AVL}} # {{countable}} {{usually plural}} The '''contents''' of a container, such as a bag, a file, a book etc., are the things that are in it. #: ''A couple of green plastic bags had torn open, and the '''contents''' had spilled out onto the floor.'' #: ''Scientists examined the '''contents''' of the dead bird's stomach.'' #: ''The students were generally happy with the course '''content''' and the instructor.'' #: ''More writing could improve students' '''content''' knowledge as well as their writing skills.'' # {{countable}} {{singular}} The fat, water, alcohol, etc. '''content''' of something is the amount of that substance in something else. #: ''The red wine had a deep color and high alcohol '''content'''.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Content''' is the feeling of being happy and satisfied. #: ''She could sleep to her heart's '''content'''.''
=== Related words === * [[table of contents]]
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # {{predicate}} If someone is '''content''', they are happy and satisfied. #: ''She had always been perfectly '''content''' to live in the city.'' #: ''Women with many friends are actually less '''content''' with their lives than those with a smaller group of friends.''
=== Related words === * [[contented]] * [[contentment]] * [[contentedly]] * [[contently]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If somebody '''contents''' themselves with something, they accept it even though they wanted something different.

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈkraɪsɪs/}} * {{audio|en-us-crisis.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|cri|sis}}
== Noun == {{noun|crisis|crises}} # {{countable}} A '''crisis''' is a '''situation''' that has become very bad or [[dangerous]] and can have bad changes to [[security]], [[economic]], [[political]], [[social]] or [[environmental]] [[issue]]s. #: ''The latest change in the hostage '''crisis''' came one day after Israel freed 51 prisoners from a jail in south Lebanon.'' #: ''This will be president's last trip to the Persian Gulf until the '''crisis''' has been resolved.'' #: ''The conditions of these people were extremely difficult and we faced really serious humanitarian '''crisis'''.'' #: ''The US financial system is in '''crisis'''.'' #: ''He has clear ideas about how to solve our energy '''crisis'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''crisis''' is a serious emotional problem. #: ''My high school friends thought I was confused, that I was having an identity '''crisis'''.'' #: ''My dad quit his job. I think he's going through a midlife '''crisis'''.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/krɪsp/}} * {{audio|en-us-crisp.ogg|US}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-crisp.wav|US}}
== Adjective == {{adj|crisp|crisper|crispest}} # If something is '''crisp''', it breaks easily and makes a [[crack]]ing or [[snap]]ping sound when you break or bite it. #: ''Fry the bacon until it is brown and '''crisp'''.'' #: ''Add the butter and continue cooking another 5 minutes or longer to brown and crisp them even more.'' #: ''Nothing beats the taste of a '''crisp''', juicy apple picked fresh from the tree.'' # If cloth or paper is '''crisp''', it is clean or new and often [[stiff]]. #: ''The young man stood tall and straight in a '''crisp''' white shirt and dark pants.'' #: ''Fifteen minutes later Wendy crawled between clean '''crisp''' sheets, realized that she was very, very tired, and fell instantly asleep.'' # If the weather is '''crisp''', it is cold and dry, often with a clear sky. # If food tastes '''crisp''', it has a fresh [[acid]] flavour. # If a person is '''crisp''', they are professional and quick, but not especially friendly. # If a picture is '''crisp''', it is very clear.
=== Synonyms === * [[sharp]]
=== Antonyms === * [[soft]] * [[blurry]]
=== Related words === * [[crispy]] * [[crispiness]] * [[crisply]]
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Salt-and-Vinegar.JPG|thumb|Crisps]] # {{countable}} {{usually plural}} {{UK}} '''Crisps''' are thin, deep-fried potatoes. #: ''I ate a packet of {{lc|potato}} '''crisps''' yesterday. {{-}} === Synonyms === * (potato) [[chips]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} To make crisp. # {{intransitive}} To become crisp.

== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Two Butchers.jpg|thumb|two butchers]] # {{countable}} A '''butcher''' is a [[person]] who [[slice#verb|slices]] and [[sell]]s [[meat]]. #: ''I went to the '''butcher''' to buy a [[steak]]''. # {{countable}} A '''butcher''' is a person who [[kills]] and [[prepare]]s [[animal]]s as meat. #: ''The '''butcher''' killed the [[pig]] and made [[bacon]].'' # {{countable}} A '''butcher''' is a person who kills in a [[violent]] way. #: ''{{w|Jack the Ripper}} was a [[crazy]] '''butcher''' of women.''
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''butcher''' an animal, you kill it and cut it up into meat. #: ''He had to '''butcher''' the [[sheep]] to get chops for his [[dinner]].''

=== Related words === * [[delightful]] * [[delightfully]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{ti verb}} If you '''delight''' somebody, you make them feel very happy. #: ''We '''delight''' in the beauty around us.'' #: ''The gift '''delighted''' her.''
=== Related words === * [[delighted]] * [[delightedly]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/dɪˈmɑːnd/}}, {{SAMPA|/dI"mA:nd/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/dɪˈmænd/}}, {{SAMPA|/dI"m{nd/}} * {{audio|en-us-demand.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} {{AVL}} # {{singular}}, {{uncountable}} '''Demand''' for something is how much people want of it. #: ''Right now we have a supply in excess of '''demand''' for crude oil, gasoline, and heating oil.'' #: ''The power companies should begin to prepare for increased '''demand''' for electricity.'' #: ''Several sectors were not able to increase their production levels to satisfy the '''demand''' requirements.'' #: ''Colleges have hired more part-time instructors to meet this increased educational '''demand'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''demand''' is what you say must be done or what you say you must have, a strong request. #: ''His '''demands''' for new machines were ignored by the company.'' # {{usually plural}} The '''demands''' on someone or something are the difficult things that are required of them. #: ''I can't deal with all these '''demands''' on my time.'' #: ''The '''demands''' on the machines are beyond what they can produce.''
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''demand''' something, you say strongly that you must receive it or that it must happen. #: ''The Lebanese Foreign Minister '''demanded''' an immediate withdrawal of Israeli forces.'' #: ''People who lost their home are '''demanding''' answers about how the fire got out of control.'' # {{transitive}} If <math>x</math> '''demands''' <math>y</math>, <math>x</math> needs or requires <math>y</math>. #: ''The problems are real and they '''demand''' attention.''
=== Synonyms === * [[ask]] * [[require]]
=== Related words === * [[demanding]] * [[undemanding]]

Don't bite it.'' {{-}} == Verb == {{verb|pit|t}} # {{transitive}} If something is '''pitted''', it is marked with little [[hollow]]s. #: ''The metal is '''pitted''' due to the [[exposure]] to [[acid rain]].'' # {{transitive}} If you '''pit''' something, you remove the [[seed]] from a [[fruit]]. #: ''Please '''pit''' the [[cherries]] before giving it to the [[children]].''
