page.title: Wiktionary:How to write Simple English entries

revision.text:
{{soft rule}} This page describes '''how to write Simple English entries'''.
==Think about your readers== First, think about your readers. Many readers of [[w:Simple English Wikipedia#Simple English|Simple English]] are people whose [[w:First language|mother language]] is not English. Other readers may be young (they may be [[child]]ren who don't have much knowledge of [[English]]) or have [[w:Learning disability|learning difficulties]]. The language is simple, but the ideas don't have to be.
==Basic English and Voice Of America Special English== Simple English Wikipedia follows some of the rules of [[w:Basic English|Basic English]], but is not so strict about using only a certain number of words. Simple English is still changing, and does not have only one word list. A good starting point to writing in Simple English is to learn to write using [[w:Basic English|Basic English]] words. This helps you to write with a limited [[Wikipedia:vocabulary|vocabulary]].
Start with [[w:Basic English|Basic English]] (BE) [[Wiktionary:Basic English alphabetical wordlist|850]]. Let us say that your readers know the [[Wiktionary:Basic English alphabetical wordlist|BE 850]] words. If your writing sounds strange, or is not clear, use a less common word. The less common word may be in [[Wiktionary:Extended Basic English alphabetical wordlist|BE 1500]] or [[w:Special English|Voice Of America (VOA) Special English]].
===Example=== The example below shows why we do not insist on using only [[w:Basic English|Basic English]] words. The full English sentence is from [[w:Winston Churchill|Winston Churchill]]:
Full English: "I have nothing to offer but ''blood, toil, tears, and sweat''."
Basic English [[Wiktionary:Basic English alphabetical wordlist|BE 850]]: "''... blood, hard work, drops from eyes, and body water.''"
*"Blood" is a [[Wiktionary:Basic English alphabetical wordlist|BE 850]] word. *"Hard work" is good for those who understand English as their [[Wikipedia:First language|mother language]]. But a learner could understand the word "hard" as "solid" or "difficult to understand". Perhaps "much work" is better. *"Drops from eyes" sounds strange to people whose mother language is English. "Tears" is a [[Wiktionary:Extended Basic English alphabetical wordlist|BE 1500]] word, and you can use it. *"Body water" also sounds strange to a person whose mother language is English. "Sweat" and "perspiration" both sound better. "Sweat" is a more common word, and you can use it by linking to the article on [[w:sweat|sweat]]. Often, for difficult words that are from [[Latin]] (like "perspiration") there will also be a native ([[Old English]] or [[w:Anglo-Saxon|Anglo-Saxon]]) word like "sweat" meaning the same thing, that is much more common and basic, but this is not always the case.
Another way is to write the more difficult words, but explain what they mean in parentheses, "(" and ")", if they cannot be linked. For example, write "[[blood]], toil (hard work), [[tear]]s, and [[w:sweat|sweat]]".
==Method== # Write your words normally, as you would speak to another person. # Look for your words in the word lists. Try to use the simplest word list: ## In Basic English [[Wiktionary:Basic English alphabetical wordlist|BE 850]] ([[w:Wikipedia:Basic English picture wordlist|pictures]]) ## In Basic English [[Wiktionary:Extended Basic English alphabetical wordlist|BE 1500]]. ## In [[w:Special English|VOA Special English]] [[Wikipedia:VOA Special English Word Book|Word Book]]. ## If a word is a name, [[idiom]]atic (the meaning of the words is not clear from the roots), or [[Wikipedia:jargon|jargon]] (special words used by experts), then it should be described in more detail. Linking to an article about the word can also help. ##: ''Stephen Hawking is a [[w:cosmology|cosmologist]]--someone who studies the structure of the [[universe]] (stars and space).'' ## Not all words can have a good encyclopedia article written about them. To link to the dictionary definition of a word rather than an encyclopedic article, link to the [[wikt:Main Page|Simple English Wiktionary]] using a link like <nowiki>[[wikt:this]]</nowiki> (put your word in place of "this"). For a more complex definition, you may also link to the [[:en:wikt:Main Page|English Wiktionary]] like this: <nowiki>[[:en:wikt:this]]</nowiki>. # Change to active voice. Example: change from "The bird was eaten by the cat." to "The cat ate the bird." # Look for a Basic English verb in past, present or future only. # For writing special to science or trade, do as asked by the process of [[Wikipedia:AECMA Simplified English]] (see external link below for International Aerospace Maintenance Language). #After finishing the article, check to have at least one link (to another article in Simple English Wikipedia) and one Interwiki link (to a version of Wikipedia in another language). The first is so the article is not a dead-end article, and the second is so that robots can fill in all the missing links to other language versions.
==What not to do== Do '''not'''... *Use bad grammar and bad spelling. *Use bad English: This is Simple English, not Bad English. *Use [[idiom]]s (words or phrases that mean something other than what they say). *Use words you're not sure about without using a [[dictionary]]. *Write entries so short that they offer no useful information. *Put links in titles (or other elements that structure the article). Try to keep the navigation and the structure of an article separate.
== See also == *[[Wiktionary:Simple talk|Simple talk]] - discussion *[[Help:How to edit]] *[[simple:w:Wikipedia:Aids for Writing Simple English|Aids for Writing Simple English]] *[[simple:w:Wikipedia:Examples of simpler English|Examples of simpler English]] *[[simple:w:Help:Translate English into Simple English|Translate English into Simple English]] *[[w:E Prime|E Prime]]
== Other websites == *[http://ogden.basic-english.org/basiceng.html Ogden's Basic English web site] **[http://ogden.basic-english.org/wordalpn.html BE 1,500] **[http://ogden.basic-english.org/intlword.html Supplementary and Special Word Lists] **[http://ogden.basic-english.org/verbs.html BE Verbs] *[http://www.voanews.com/specialenglish/index.cfm VOA Special English official web site] *[http://www.asd-ste100.org/ ASD Simplified Technical English] *[http://basilwhite.com/basicenglish.htm How to use Microsoft Word to check a document for Basic English] *[http://www.online-utility.org/english/simple_basic_helper.jsp Online utility for checking Basic English text] - supports Basic English and various other dictionaries *[http://www.sfu.ca/wp/distance.htm Writing and Publishing Program]: online writing and editing courses (from Simon Fraser University) *[http://svcs.cs.pdx.edu/trac/write_idea/ WriteIdea]: writers' tool for writing simple text. Both java and [http://writeidea.smallwhitecube.com web-based] versions. *[http://wordcount.org/main.php Wordcount, a very ''rough'', but easy to use, guide on how often words are used].

There are several ways to start a new page. These can vary based on the type of page started, as well as the wiki and namespace. == Using Wikilinks == MediaWiki makes it very easy to link wiki pages using a standard syntax (see [[mw:Help:Links|Links]]). If you (or anyone else) creates a link to an article that doesn't exist yet, the link will be coloured red, like this. Clicking a red link, will take you to the edit page for the new article. Simply type your text, click save and the new page will be created. Once the page has been created, the link will change from red to blue (purple for pages you've visited) indicating that the article now exists. Usually this is the best way to create a new page, because it means that right from the start, the page will be linked from at least one other place on the wiki (and typically you will want to mesh it into other related pages later) If you are creating a new page without creating any link to it, you may need to ask yourself: Does this page really fit in with the topics already covered in the wiki? Also, how are you expecting visitors to find this page? Normally there is no reason to create a page without first creating a red link to it. == Using the URL == You can use the wiki's URL for creating a new page. The URL to an article of the wiki is usually something like this: *http://www.example.net/index.php/'''ARTICLE'''    or *http://www.example.net/wiki/'''ARTICLE''' If you replace '''ARTICLE''' with the name of the page you wish to create, you will be taken to a blank page which indicates that no article of that name exists yet. Clicking the "''edit''" [[mw:Help:Navigation#Page Tabs|page tab]] at the top of the page will take you to the edit page for that article, where you can create the new page by typing your text, and clicking submit. == From the search page == If you search for a page that doesn't exist (using the search box at the top of the page) then you will be provided with a link to create the new page. == Create redirects to your new page == Don't forget to setup redirects when you create a page. If you think another person may search for the page you've created by using a different name or spelling, please create the proper redirect(s). See [[mw:Help:Redirects|Help:Redirects]]. == Protecting your new page == Normally a new wiki page can be edited by other people (that is one of the main ideas of a wiki!) However, a sysop could 'protect' the page, if needed, to prevent normal users from editing it. This is just the basis for starting a new page. For a more in-depth tutorial, see [[Help:Creating a new entry]]. [[Category:Help|Starting a new page]]

== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''postmark''' is a stamp that shows where a letter was sent from. #: ''The postcard had an Orlando '''postmark''' on it.''
== Verb == {{verb}} # If you '''postmark''' something, you add a postmark to it. #: ''This letter was '''postmarked''' on the 23rd of January.''
=== Related words === * [[post]] * [[mark]]

== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''plaything''' is a toy or something else you play with. #: ''The computer has turned into a '''plaything'''.''
=== Related words === * [[play]] * [[thing]]

{{see|instep}}
== Expression == {{expression}} # If you are '''in step''', you move with someone at the same speed. #: ''The army walked '''in step'''.''
== Preposition == {{preposition}} # In agreement with. #: ''Moscow is anxious to stay '''in step''' with Washington.''
=== Related words === * [[in]] * [[step]]
[[Category:Prepositions with with-PP complements]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈdaɪət/}} * {{audio|en-us-diet.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{cu noun}} A '''diet''' is the food that an [[animal]], [[person]], or group usually eats. #: ''Several studies have suggested that high-fat '''diets''' can directly increase the risk of this cancer.'' #: ''Studies confirm that [[vegetarian]] is a healthful and balanced '''diet'''.'' #: ''I exercise, watch my '''diet''' and have good [[gene]]s.'' #: ''A healthy '''diet''' should not exceed 30 percent fat per day.'' #: ''He was unhealthy thanks to poor '''diet''' and heavy smoking.'' # {{countable}} A '''diet''' is a controlled set of foods chosen for health purposes. #: ''Oprah Winfrey wasn't the only [[celebrity]] who transformed her body through exercise and '''diet''' last year.'' #: ''He said he lost weight because of his new vegetarian '''diet'''.'' #: ''It's strange to see somebody at a movie buy [[jumbo]] popcorn and a huge '''diet''' coke.'' #: ''They [[demand]] that you start getting serious about both proper exercise and '''diet'''.'' #: ''She stuck to the strict '''diet''' for the first two weeks and her blood pressure came down.'' # {{countable}} A '''diet''' of something is something your experience regularly, usually something negative. #: ''The Daily News has served up a steady '''diet''' of local news.'' # {{countable}} A '''diet''' is a [[council]] of political leaders. #: ''This week, the Japanese [[parliament]], the '''Diet''', considered but did not act on a [[resolution]] apologizing for Pearl Harbor.''
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} If you '''diet''', you limit the food you eat to lose weight. #: ''Weight lost by '''dieting''' alone almost never stays off.''
=== Related words === * [[dietarian]] * [[dietary]]
[[Category:Nutrition]]

== Verb == {{verb}} # {{ti verb}} If something '''disappoints''' somebody, it makes them unhappy because it was not as good as they expected. #: ''I'm afraid you really '''disappointed''' me. I thought you were more honest.'' #: ''We thought the party would be good and it didn't '''disappoint'''.'' # {{ti verb}} If something '''disappoints''' somebody, they thought it would happen but it didn't. #: ''I'm sorry to '''disappoint''' you, but the meeting has been cancelled.'' #: ''When the president returned, it '''disappointed''' our hopes for change.''

== Noun == {{noun}} # {{cu noun}} A '''disaster''' is a serious problem. #: ''Feed the Children has been involved in '''disaster''' relief around the world.'' #: ''The San Francisco Earthquake was the deadliest natural '''disaster''' in U.S.'' #: ''President Bush declared New Orleans a federal '''disaster''' area.'' #: ''The flight had just left the airport when '''disaster''' struck.'' #: ''A major environmental '''disaster''' is the drying up of the Aral Sea.'' #: ''What can the country and each one of us do to avoid economic '''disaster'''?'' #: ''A spokesman said the plan was a recipe for '''disaster''' and should be defeated.'' #: ''When families get together, there is always the potential for '''disaster'''.'' #: ''We need additional vehicles to assist us in distributing the goods to the victims of '''disasters'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[problem]] * [[incident]] * [[accident]]
=== Related words === * [[disastrous]] * [[disastrously]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{US}} {{enPR|läʹvə}}, {{IPA|/ˈlɑːvə/}} * {{CA}} {{IPA|/ˈlɑːvə/|/ˈlævə/}} * {{audio|en-us-lava.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Pahoehoe toe.jpg|thumb|lava]] # {{countable}} {{geology}} '''Lava''' is the [[molten]] [[rock]] that is spit out of a [[volcano]] when it [[erupts]]. #: ''When the volcano erupted, it spit out lots of '''lava'''.'' # {{uncountable}} {{geology}} '''Lava''' is [[magma]] that is found on the [[surface]] of the [[Earth]].
=== Usage notes === Lava is different than [[magma]]. Magma is molten rock that is under the surface of the Earth, while lava is molten rock that is on the surface of the Earth. For example, molten rock inside a volcano is magma; when it erupts, it becomes lava.
=== Related words === * [[lavalike]] / [[lava-like]] * [[lava dome]] * [[lava lamp]] * [[magma]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|drăg}}, {{IPA|/dræɡ/}} * {{audio|en-us-drag.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb|drag|g}} [[File:Reindeerdrag.jpg|thumb|A man '''dragging''' an animal]] [[File:Drag-and-drop.png|thumb|Something being '''dragged''' on a computer]] # {{transitive}} If you '''drag''' something, you pull it, usually with difficulty. #: ''She heard the noise of a chair being '''dragged''' to the window.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''drag''' your feet, you move or do something slowly. #: ''Six months later, when nothing had happened, they complained that the city was still '''dragging''' its feet.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''drag''' somebody somewhere, you take them there but they don't want to go. #: ''Dad sent me to '''drag''' you back home.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''drag''' yourself somewhere, you go there with difficulty, often because you're tired or sick. #: ''I '''dragged''' myself out of bed and made a cup of coffee.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''drag''' something on a computer screen, you move it from one place to another using a pointer. # {{transitive}} If something '''drags''' you down, it makes you feel unhappy. {{-}} == Noun == {{noun}} # {{uncountable}} If something is a '''drag''', it's not fun and you don't want to do it. #: ''Christmas was a real '''drag''' this year, since I was living alone.'' # {{uncountable}} If someone is a '''drag''', they don't enjoy fun activities or they stop you from having fun. #: ''He's such a '''drag''' to be with, studying all the time.'' #: ''Christmas was a real '''drag''' this year, since I was living alone.'' # {{countable}} If you take a '''drag''' from a cigarette, you close your mouth and inhale through it. #: ''I took the final '''drag''' from my final cigarette, and put it out, for good.'' # {{uncountable}} {{physics}} '''Drag''' is the [[resistance]] of a [[fluid]] to something moving that is moving through it. <!--from en.wikt-->

{{Wikipedia}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{enPR|drēm}}, {{IPA|/driːm/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/drim/|[d̠͡r̠˔ʷɪi̯m]|/dʒrim/}} * {{SAMPA|/dri:m/}} * {{audio|en-us-dream.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} '''Dreams''' are the [[image]]s and things you see when you are [[sleep]]ing. #: ''In my '''dream''' I had forgotten the baby in a drawer.'' #: ''I had a '''dream''' that I was in a magical world with fairies and evil witches.'' # {{countable}} A '''dream''' is something you wish for or hope will happen. #: ''The company is succeeding beyond anyone's wildest '''dreams'''.'' #: ''He decided to [[fulfil]] his childhood '''dream''' of becoming a police officer.''
=== Synonyms === * [[fantasy]] * [[wish]] * [[hope]] * [[imagination]]
=== Antonyms === * [[reality]]
== Verb == {{verb}} {{verb2|dream|dreams|dreamt|dreamt|dreaming}} # {{intransitive}} If you '''dream''' about something, you wish for it. #: ''She '''dreamed''' of becoming a concert pianist.'' #: ''If we go to sleep, we'll '''dream''' that we're awake.''
=== Synonyms === * [[imagine]] * [[wish]] * [[hope]]
=== Related words === * [[undreamed]] * [[dreamer]] * [[dreamy]] * [[dreamily]] * [[daydream]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/dʌmp/}} * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 dump.ogg|Audio (AU)}}
== Verb == {{verb}} [[File:MH-60S Helicopter dumps water onto Fire.jpg|thumb|'''Dumping''' water on a fire]] # {{transitive}} If you '''dump''' something, you get rid of it. #: ''For years the military '''dumped''' nuclear waste into local rivers and lakes.'' # {{ti verb}} If you '''dump''' something, you put it down carelessly. #: ''She '''dumped''' her stuff onto the table.'' #: ''Giant trucks had begun '''dumping''' truckloads of sand on the beach.'' #: ''He '''dumped''' the kids at the park and headed back home.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''dump''' someone, you stop {{r|dat|ing}} them. #: ''My girlfriend '''dumped''' me last night.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''dump''' something, you sell it below cost, often in another country. #: ''The Americans have accused Canada of '''dumping''' its softwood on the US market.'' # {{transitive}} {{technical}} If you '''dump''' data, you save it from a large computer to a [[storage]] device.
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Landfill face.JPG|thumb|A garbage '''dump''']] # {{countable}} A '''dump''' is a large area for [[garbage]]. {{syn|dumper}} #: ''2,000 tons of waste arrive in San Francisco's garbage '''dump''' every day.'' # {{countable}} A '''dump''' is the act of emptying something quickly. {{syn|dumper}} #: ''They turned off the cement mixer and prepared for the '''dump'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''dump''' is a place where weapons are kept. {{syn|dumper}} #: ''The army found a weapons '''dump''' near the border.'' # {{countable}} A '''dump''' is a building or apartment that is dirty and not nice to be in. {{syn|dumper}} #: ''Let's get out of here. This place is a '''dump'''.'' # {{countable}} {{technical}} A '''dump''' is the act of saving data from a large computer to a storage device. {{syn|dumper}} # {{countable}} {{slang}} If you take a '''dump''', you push [[waste]] out of your [[anus]]. {{syn|dumper}} #: ''I've gotta go to the toilet and take a '''dump'''.''
=== Related words === * [[dumpster]] * [[dump truck]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ɪn'geɪʤ/}} * {{audio|en-us-engage.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|en|gage}}
== Verb == {{verb|engag|e}} {{AVL}} # {{intransitive}} If you '''engage''' in an [[activity]], you do it. #: ''My broken foot left me with few [[athletic]] activities that I could '''engage''' in.'' #: ''Most of the men did not '''engage''' in casual sex.'' #: ''Both employees '''engaged''' in behavior that didn't belong in the workplace.'' #: ''Should United States forces '''engage''' in fighting in these [[situation]]s?'' # {{transitive}} If you '''engage''' somebody, you get and keep their attention. #: ''Teachers are always thinking of ways to '''engage''' students.'' # {{transitive}} {{formal}} If you '''engage''' somebody, you [[hire]] them. # {{ti verb}} If you '''engage''' a part of a machine, you make it contact another part so that they both move. #: ''He reaches up and throws a red-handled [[lever]] to '''engage''' the black iron gears.'' # {{ti verb}} If an army '''engages''' an enemy, they start fighting.
=== Antonyms === * [[disengage]]
=== Related words === * [[disengage]] * [[engaged]] * [[engaging]] * [[engagingly]] * [[engagement]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/fɛns/|[fɛns]|[fɛnts]}} * {{SAMPA|/fEn(t)s/}} * {{audio|en-us-fence.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''fence''' is like a thin [[wall]] that is not part of a building. It stops [[people]] or [[animal]]s from going from one outdoors place to another. It may have many big holes that you can see through, but not big enough for people to walk through. #: ''We put up a tall '''fence''' around the yard so that the dog couldn't get out.'' # {{countable}} A '''fence''' is a person who buys things from people who stole the things, and then sells the things again to other people. #: ''I don't think anyone will steal this, because they wouldn't get much money for it. They'd have to sell it to a '''fence'''.''
<gallery> File:Wood fence.jpg File:2008-08-01 No Tresspassing sign at RDU.jpg File:HPI Fence.JPG File:Nylofor Medium.jpg File:Auschwitz.Birkenau.Fence.jpg </gallery>
== Verb == {{verb|fenc|e}} [[File:0408 USA Olympic fencing.jpg|thumb|Two [[fencer]]s '''fencing''' with each other]] # {{transitive}} When someone '''fences''' a piece of land, they put up a '''fence''' around it. #: ''This field has been '''fenced''' for years, because they used to keep cows here.'' # {{intransitive}} When someone '''fences''', they fight with [[sword]]s as a [[sport]]. #: ''I can hear the sound of the swords hitting each other, from people '''fencing''' in the gym.'' # {{transitive}} When someone '''fences''' something, they sell it to a '''fence'''. #: ''We can't give you back what we stole. We '''fenced''' it.''

revision.text: {{Wiktionary:Simple talk/Archives}} == Do seahorse exist? == I think the last surviving seahorse lives 100 years ago. :Yes. At the moment the article hasn't been translated to "simple english" but you can find stuff about them here http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_horse [[User:RTG|RTG]] 16:21, 29 October 2008 (UTC) == Migrate templates == From {http://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/User_talk:71.63.182.214#Wrong_wiki here] I see that templates for vandalism are not enabled here. [[User:RTG|RTG]] 16:19, 29 October 2008 (UTC) :No, sorry, I had the right wiki. XD I was taking care of some vandalism that appeared on the IRC recent changes feed. I'm making a number of templates now. Best, [[User:PeterSymonds|PeterSymonds]] 16:21, 29 October 2008 (UTC) ::That guy had the wrong wiki as he was making articels of sorts. Cheers [[User:RTG|RTG]] 01:21, 30 October 2008 (UTC) The templates you're looking for exist as {{test}}, {{test1}}, {{test2}}, {{test3}}, {{test4}}, {{test5}}.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 11:13, 30 October 2008 (UTC) == Bot policy == To facilitate [[m:steward|steward]] granting of bot access, I suggest implementing the [[m:Bot policy|standard bot policy]] on this wiki. In particular, this policy allows stewards to automatically flag known interlanguage linking bots (if this page says that is acceptable), which form the vast majority of such requests. The policy also enables [[m:Bot policy#Global_bots|global bots]] on this wiki (if this page says that is acceptable), which are trusted bots that will be given bot access on every wiki that allows global bots. This policy makes bot access requesting much easier for local users, operators, and stewards. To implement it we only need to create a redirect to this page from [[Project:Bot policy]], and add a line at the top noting that it is used here. Please read the text at [[m:Bot policy]] before commenting. If you object, please say so; I hope to implement in one week if there is no objection, since it is particularly written to streamline bot requests on wikis with little or no community interested in bot access requests. [[User:Brett|Brett]] 23:54, 2 November 2008 (UTC) :Since there are no objections, I have requested implementation of standard bot policy.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 13:16, 24 November 2008 (UTC) == Transitive verb == what is a transitive verb?--unsigned question by 202.93.37.88 A transitive verb is one that takes an object. In ''I at my lunch'', ''my lunch'' is the object of ''ate'', which is a transitive verb. In ''I have eaten'', there is no object, so the verb is not transitive. It is intransitive. Some verbs are always transitive, some never transitive, and some are sometimes transitive.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 17:35, 25 November 2008 (UTC) == Closure Request == This project has been requested for closure. See [[m:Proposals for closing projects/Closure of Simple English (2) Wiktionary]]. Thanks. [[User:SwirlBoy39|'''ѕ'''wirl'''в'''oy]] [[User talk:SwirlBoy39|₪]] 16:32, 27 November 2008 (UTC) == Admin votes == Hello folks! I just wanted to let people know that there are two active votes for adminship over at [[Wiktionary:Administrators]] which people might be interested in, let's see some community involvement. :) --[[User:Neskaya|Neskaya]] 09:01, 28 November 2008 (UTC) == Encyclopedic entries == The recent addition of many place names and other terms that are linked to them has caused some consternation. At times, these have clearly become encyclopedic, running to a number of paragraphs (at which point I've shortened them). At other times, they have been simple statements no different from those you would find in en.wikt (e.g., [http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Zionist zionist], [http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Palestine Palestine], [http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Tehran Tehran], etc.). I was uncomfortable with a number of the pages, but this was somewhat beyond my ken, so I [http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Wiktionary:Information_desk#Help_dealing_with_geographical_terms_at_Simple.wikt asked] for an opinion on en.wikt. I'm glad that people seem to be interested in helping, but I was somewhat surprised to see [[user:Wpedzich‎]], who I assume must be a steward, simply come in and wipe it all out without any discussion whatsoever. Perhaps people might provide their thoughts on what constitutes an encyclopedic entry.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 11:47, 28 November 2008 (UTC) :Naturally, "opinions may vary", but I'd start off from [[:en:Wiktionary:What Wiktionary is not]]. Of course, please don't throw stones at me just because that page comes from English (and not Simple English) Wiktionary. The document reads: "Wiktionary is not an encyclopedia, a genealogy database, or an atlas", therefore it doesn't present factual information. I believe everybody has their own definition of a dictionary, although I'd say the die-hard, never-to-be-omitted points would be (apart from the lack of factual information): the etymology, meanings (not definitions or descriptions) and the usage of the word (examples), plus its translations. The definitions that I've removed today lacked all these points except the definition, therefore making them short encyclopedic (if not merely descriptive) entries. :I understand that some of my actions may seem objectionable, however I felt that even with the limitations of Simple English as the chosen language, the pages did not constitute full dictionary entries that could be satisfactorily kept. If the general opinion is different, I'm committed to restoring the entries of the satisfactory quality personally. [[User:Wpedzich|Wpedzich]] 12:10, 28 November 2008 (UTC) ::I'm interested to understand the distinction you're drawing between meanings and definitions. As a side note, the policy on Simple English Wiktionary is NOT to include etymologies and translations. The reasoning is that those are already available on en.wikt.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 12:25, 28 November 2008 (UTC) :::Surprising, although naturally I will not battle the consensus. I would support the idea that each project should be self-contained enough to include all the relevant dictionary material without the need of being supplemented by English Wiktionary... anyway - I'll get down to restoring those entries that satisfy the basic definition - I'm just wondering about the usefulness of maps, national emblems and photos in a dictionary entry. Suggestion? [[User:Wpedzich|Wpedzich]] 12:42, 28 November 2008 (UTC) ::::Thank you for picking through each of the deleted entries, though that wasn't my main intent. I just wanted to get a better idea of what people considered encyclopedic. My personal feeling is that a map is useful, but that national emblems and such are generally superfluous. I'm still curious about the difference between a meaning and a definition.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 13:13, 28 November 2008 (UTC) :::::I think the maps are fine, but flags and emblems are useless and detracts from dictionary definitions. Those are better at simplewiki. [[User:DavidWS|DavidWS]] 13:33, 28 November 2008 (UTC) :(I'll make this indent a bit smaller). The choice of words can be quite unfortunate for a lexicographer ;) The way I understand the difference here is that an encyclopedic entry, especially after the prolonged experience with WIkipedia I've had speaks in whole sentences, while a dictionary entry rarely does. "Warsaw: capital city of Poland" suits the purpose of a dictionary much better than "Warsaw is the capital city of Poland", even though the difference is in only one word. [[User:Wpedzich|Wpedzich]] 14:05, 28 November 2008 (UTC) ::I see. Again, local policy is to use full sentences. The reason is that for people who are learning English, these are often easier to understand. They also help to illustrate how a word is used. Clearly, the examples also do that, but where some people are likely to overlook context labels and may not go so far as to read an example, an entry like [[criminal]] can help to illustrates that one sense of the adjective typically is attributive while the other doesn't have this limitation. Similarly, if you look at the entry for [[concentrate]], you see how verb sense number 3 indicates that a goal complement (i.e., somewhere) is usually included. These principles are discussed in the work of John Sinclair who is one of the fathers of modern corpus-based learner-focused lexicography.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 14:34, 28 November 2008 (UTC) ====POV Issues==== Another note on this subject. I'm a bit concerned with the POV that some of these entries are showing. I do not think that we should be keeping redirects for National Flowers, Birds, or what of the like, although the entries that the redirects point to are fine. I simply don't think that all the POV-pushing is going to do us any good, and have re-tagged some of the redirects for deletion on this principle. I'm also trying to remove as much POV-pushing as I can see. --[[User:Neskaya|Neskaya]] 08:55, 29 November 2008 (UTC) == Plant names == I'm not entirely clear on when [[:Category:Plants|plant names]] should be capitalized and when they should be lower case. Can somebody help out?--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 12:25, 3 December 2008 (UTC) :I don't know. If you give examples, I can do some web searches to try to find out how they're usually done. ☺[[User:Coppertwig|Coppertwig]]([[User talk:Coppertwig|talk]]) 00:18, 14 December 2008 (UTC) == New goal == I'm planning to work on the [[BE1500]]. There are now 648 red links, by my count. Maybe others would like to help. I don't know whether anyone is already working on it. ☺[[User:Coppertwig|Coppertwig]]([[User talk:Coppertwig|talk]]) 00:10, 14 December 2008 (UTC) :Thanks for helping with this goal, Empire3131! :Are we supposed to put a {{BE1500}} template at the top of BE1500 words, like the one for BE850 words? I guess not, since there is no such template. (I think I asked this before but I don't quite remember.) ☺[[User:Coppertwig|Coppertwig]]([[User talk:Coppertwig|talk]]) 01:44, 7 January 2009 (UTC) ::Your welcome, Coppertwig. [[User:Empire3131|Empire3131]] 01:49, 7 January 2009 (UTC) == Double Redirects == All Double Redirects, but the Mediawiki one (Which can't be fixed), are fixed! [[User:Empire3131|Empire3131]] 20:00, 3 January 2009 (UTC) :thank you.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 01:52, 4 January 2009 (UTC) == Apology == I want to apologize for my recent attempt to shutdown the Simple English Dictionary. I love the concepts of simple wikis and I am even an admin on Simple Wikiquote. Lately, I have began to realize that even though this wiki may be small, that doesn't mean we should close it. It has a helpful purpose, and it should remain as is. The purpose of Simple English isn't to disband, it's just like all the other wikimedia projects. It's here to keep knowledge free.I hope you accept my apology, and I hope to see you as I begin editing. We don't shut down because it's small, we help it stand up! [[User:SwirlBoy39|'''ѕ'''wirl'''в'''oy]] [[User talk:SwirlBoy39|₪]] 22:23, 3 January 2009 (UTC) *: Good. [[User:Empire3131|Empire3131]] 00:37, 4 January 2009 (UTC) Well, that's a remarkable change of heart. Perhaps you could go back and move to close the vote where you opened it.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 01:46, 4 January 2009 (UTC) ::Unfortunately, I can't close it now as there is actually some opposes. [[User:SwirlBoy39|'''ѕ'''wirl'''в'''oy]] [[User talk:SwirlBoy39|₪]] 03:32, 4 January 2009 (UTC) == English question == im kinda a confused about this phrase...im not good in english so please assist me... i asked a person ones... how are you? he replied: im never been good... (is that means hes all good? or he was not good-never?) how we will get the vocabularies from wikipedia :I'm afraid that ''I'm never been good'' is not grammatical English. Perhaps what you heard is ''I've never been better.'' This means that the person is very good. I hope that helps.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 13:25, 4 January 2009 (UTC) ::You're right, Brett. I didn't think of that. Or, maybe it could have been "I've never been so good." That also means the person is feeling very good. ☺[[User:Coppertwig|Coppertwig]]([[User talk:Coppertwig|talk]]) 01:42, 13 January 2009 (UTC) == Pages telling people how to write pages here == Are there pages telling people how to write pages here? Do we write a different page for every form of a verb? For example, "resided". ☺[[User:Coppertwig|Coppertwig]]([[User talk:Coppertwig|talk]]) 01:42, 13 January 2009 (UTC) :I think that's O.K. It's better the the asteroids and romanian rivers over at wp:simple [[User:Empire3131|Empire3131]] 01:47, 13 January 2009 (UTC) ::There's nothing wrong with each form of a word to having a page. Personally, I don't see it as a priority.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 12:04, 13 January 2009 (UTC) == visibility a long major is restriced == what deos this mean :It doesn't mean anything. You must have misheard. I expect that the original was, ''visibility along major roads is restricted.'' This means that if you are driving on a major road, like a highway, you cannot see far ahead of you, probably because of weather such as rain, snow, or fog.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 12:39, 15 January 2009 (UTC) == Bot == Hi, does anyone have any objections to me trying out my interwiki bot? (a test run). It would be [[User:MaximillionBot]]. It would add and fix interwiki links. [[User:Maximillion Pegasus|Maximillion Pegasus]] 16:53, 18 January 2009 (UTC) :No objection. Try it out, but don't just set it free until we see what it does. If it works out, I'll give it a bot flag.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 10:48, 19 January 2009 (UTC) ::Ok, I'll try it out here a little bit later on today. [[User:Maximillion Pegasus|Maximillion Pegasus]] 15:30, 19 January 2009 (UTC) :::I tested it out here. Seems to work good. Let me know if you see any problems. Also, would anyone have an objection to me also using the bot to do automatic archival of this talk page? (It would have a setup like Misza's bot) Anything older than 10 days maybe? [[User:Maximillion Pegasus|Maximillion Pegasus]] 16:13, 19 January 2009 (UTC) ::::OK, I'll flag it. As for archiving, that's fine, but discussions are sparse around here. Ten days seems far too short a time. How about three months?--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 17:48, 19 January 2009 (UTC) :::::If a bot automatically archives after three months, it's easier just to do it manually. [[User:Maxim|Maxim]] | [[User talk:Maxim|talk]] 23:52, 23 January 2009 (UTC) == Tips for new users == It seems like we've picked up a number of high-quality productive users recently. Thank you for all your additions. I'd just like to point out a few minor things: *With nouns, please indicate whether each sense is countable or not if you can. *Similarly, with verbs, please indicate transitive or intransitive for each sense if you can. *Please give full-sentence definitions *Bold every instance of the headword *Where possible, provide examples that exemplify, rather than those that simply use a word. Thanks again for your efforts.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 13:51, 19 January 2009 (UTC) :For examples, you mean that the examples must provide an example of a common way the word is used (like "The '''apple''' was eaten for lunch" or "She picked an '''apple''' from the tree")? [[User:Maxim|Maxim]] | [[User talk:Maxim|talk]] 23:59, 23 January 2009 (UTC) ::It isn't that they ''must'' show how the word is used, but it is more useful for our target audience. ::When you exemplify a word, you use it in the way that it is naturally used. An word like ''bear'' in the sense of to give birth is usually used in the passive, so it should be exemplified that way. The colour ''blond'' is usually used to talk about hair, so an example about a blond car would not be the best. A word like ''domicile'' is a formal word, so a casual example like ''I think I'll head back to my domicile'' provides a distorted picture of the word.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 12:37, 2 February 2009 (UTC) == Redirects == I've noticed that redirects are discouraged at Wiktionary, and I've checked the amount of redirects there is, and there's a bunch. A lot of MediaWiki: ones, created as a result of the creation of the template namespace, as well as a fair bunch in the mainspace. What should done with them? [[User:Maxim|Maxim]] | [[User talk:Maxim|talk]] 22:54, 26 January 2009 (UTC) :I'm afraid I don't know.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 12:38, 2 February 2009 (UTC) == Heading levels == Hi there all. I've noticed that we have been using Level 2 headings for the headings of the kind of word that a word is (for example, noun or verb) and Level 3 headings for the headings of the Pronounciation. I would like to propose to the community that we standardize the level of headings that we use here. For example, we either bring the level of heading for the Pronounciation up from a Level 3 heading to a level 2 heading, or we bring down the headings for the kind of word it is from Level 2 heading to Level 3 heading. What do you guys think of this proposal? Thanks, [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 23:41, 2 February 2009 (UTC) :I think it is standardized. As you said, the standard is level 3 for pronunciation and level 2 for categories.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] 00:29, 3 February 2009 (UTC) ::Alright. Just thought that I would bring this up. Cheers, [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 00:34, 3 February 2009 (UTC)

{{wikipedia}} === Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈɒk.ʌlt/|/əˈkʌlt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/əˈkʌlt/}} * {{audio|en-au-occult.ogg|Audio (AU)}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If something is '''occult''' it is [[hide|hidden]] or [[secret]]—or it is about hidden or secret things. ## If something is '''occult''' it is part of the universe most people do not see. An '''occult''' thing is something that is [[strange]] or [[weird]], and might be called [[magic]]. ##: ''I've seen many '''occult''' happenings, including [[ghost]]s and [[witchcraft]].'' ## About an [[unusual]] [[belief]] held by [[mysterious]] groups outside of the normal belief system. This is often a belief that involves magic or [[spirit]]s. Many '''occult''' groups keep their beliefs secret, but not all do. ##: ''Her occult activities included witchcraft, [[voodoo]], and [[hoodoo]].'' ##: ''The Order of the Golden Dawn was a famous British '''occult''' group.'' ## {{medicine}} An '''occult''' problem is one that you cannot [[see]] without special [[tool]]s (like [[x-ray]]s) ##: ''The baby had an '''occult''' cleft palate.''
=== Related words === * [[magic]] * [[mystic]], [[mystical]], [[mysticism]] * [[paranormal]] * [[religion]]
== Verb == {{verb|occult}} #If you '''occult''' something, you [[cover]] it. #: ''The Earth '''occults''' the Moon when a [[lunar eclipse]] happens.''
== Noun == {{noun4}} # {{uncountable}} {{context|usually has the before it}} '''The occult''' is anything to do with things that are not normal; [[supernatural]] or paranormal.
[[Category:Forteana]] [[Category:Occult| ]]
{{context|plural}}<noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ɪkˈsaɪt/}} * {{audio|en-us-excite.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|ex|cite}}
== Verb == {{verb|excit|e}} # {{transitive}} If something '''excites''' you, it makes you feel interested, happy, and awake. #: ''A good DJ can '''excite''' the crowd and make people dance.'' #: ''The new pictures from space '''excite''' the imagination.'' # {{transitive}} If something '''excites''' someone, it makes them think about sex. # {{transitive}} If something '''excites''' a [[nerve]] or a part of an [[animal]] or plant, it makes it more active.
=== Synonyms === * [[arouse]] * [[stimulate]]
=== Related words === * [[exciting]] * [[excitedly]] * [[excited]] * [[excitement]] * [[excitable]] * [[excitably]] * [[excitation]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ɪkˈstɛnt/}} * {{audio|en-us-extent.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|ex|tent}}
== Noun == {{noun}} {{AVL}} # {{countable}} {{singular}} You use "to an '''extent'''" to explain how true something is or how much it happens. #: ''The US and, to a lesser '''extent''', Britain have controlled the meeting.'' #: ''I think our success will depend, to a certain '''extent''', on getting enough money.'' # {{countable}} {{singular}} The '''extent''' of something is how far it goes, how much area it covers, or how much it does. #: ''Now he could see the full '''extent''' of the island, stretching away to the south.'' #: ''The purpose of this study was to assess the '''extent''' of alcohol use among the community college student population.'' #: ''The buildings were still burning and the '''extent''' of the damage is not yet known.''
=== Synonyms === * [[area]] * [[level]] * [[size]] * [[range]] * [[amount]] * [[degree]]
=== Related words === * [[extend]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/fəˈsɪlɪti/}} * {{audio|en-us-facility.ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Noun == {{noun|facility|facilities}} {{AVL}} # {{plural}} A place's '''facilities''' are its rooms, equipment, and services. #: ''Picnic, barbecue and playground '''facilities''' are located throughout the park.'' #: ''The money helps to provide equipment and '''facilities''' for physical education.'' # {{countable}} A '''facility''' is a building for a particular purpose, such as doing sport, policing, health care, etc., often a large public building. #: ''He found that Houston neighborhoods had quality recreational '''facilities''', a friendly environment and extra security.'' #: ''The town now has the cleanest wastewater treatment '''facility''' in the state.'' #: ''I hated the idea of putting my mother in a nursing '''facility'''.'' #: ''I put most of what I owned to a storage '''facility''', and moved to California.'' #: ''The church has started operating an educational '''facility''' just off Highway 11.'' # {{countable}} If you have a '''facility''' for something, you do it well or learn it easily. #: ''Your son has a special '''facility''' for causing problems.'' # {{plural}} The '''facilities''' is the washroom or toilet. #: ''Excuse me, but may I used the '''facilities'''?''
=== Synonyms === * [[service]] * [[institute]] * [[talent]] * [[feature]]
=== Derived words === * [[facilitate]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/fʌˈmɪliɜr/}} * {{SAMPA|/fV"mIli3r/}} * {{audio|en-us-familiar.ogg|US}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If something is '''familiar''', you already know it or about it. #: ''"Three strikes and you're out" is a very '''familiar''' phrase these days.'' #: ''The words sounded very '''familiar''' to her, and then she remembered: she had written them.'' #: ''Why would someone leave '''familiar''' territory and travel all this distance.'' #: ''People sitting on the grass was a '''familiar''' sight on Saturdays in the park.'' #: ''New a month ago, he's become quite '''familiar''' to all of us.'' # If you are '''familiar''' with something, you already know it or about it. #: ''What does that mean? I'm not '''familiar''' with the word?'' # If you are being '''familiar''', you are acting in a friendly way.
=== Related words === * [[familiarly]] * [[familiarity]] * [[unfamiliar]] * [[unfamiliarity]] * [[familiarise]]/[[familiarize]] * [[familiarised]]/[[familiarized]] * [[familiarisation]]/[[familiarization]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''familiar''' is the magical pet of a [[witch]], often a cat.

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈfæn.si/}} * {{audio|en-us-fancy.ogg|US}}
== Adjective == {{adj|fancy|fancier|fanciest}} {{adj|more=true}} # If something is '''fancy''', it nicer than usual, often with [[decoration]]s and bright colours. #: ''That's a very '''fancy''' dress you're wearing.'' #: ''We tried to make things look '''fancy''' for the party.'' # A '''fancy''' restaurant, party, etc. is [[fashionable]] and [[expensive]]. #: ''She's going to a '''fancy''' party and the rest of us aren't welcome.'' # '''Fancy''' movements are [[difficult]] but done with a lot of skill. #: ''He got around the other players with some very '''fancy''' footwork.'' # '''Fancy''' apples, tuna, etc. are the best kind of that food. #: ''Cherries from Canada can be marked either "CANADA '''FANCY'''", "CANADA CHOICE" or "CANADA STANDARD"''
=== Antonyms === * [[plain]] * [[ordinary]]
=== Related words === * [[fancily]] * [[fanciness]]
== Verb == {{verb|fanc|y}} # {{transitive}} If you '''fancy''' something, you like or want it. #: ''No thanks. I don't really '''fancy''' coffee.'' #: ''I thought you might '''fancy''' a drink.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''fancy''' someone, you like them in a [[sexual]] way. #: ''She's very nice, but I don't really '''fancy''' her, if you get my meaning.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''fancy''' yourself something, you think you are that (but maybe other people don't agree). #: ''He '''fancies''' himself a great football player.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''fancy''' something up, you make it more fancy. # You say "'''Fancy''' that!" or fancy something, to show that you're surprised about it or think it unlikely. #: '''''Fancy''' her getting the job!''
=== Synonyms === * [[like]] * [[want]]
=== Related words === * [[fancier]]
== Noun == {{noun|2=fancies}} # {{countable}} A '''fancy''' is a like or a wish. # {{countable}} A '''fancy''' is an idea or a dream. # {{uncountable}} '''Fancy''' is imagination.
{{exstub}}

revision.text:
{{also|-fashion}} === Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈfæʃən/}} * {{audio|en-us-fashion.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{cu noun}} A '''fashion''' is a [[style]], often [[clothing]], that is popular at a particular time and place. #: ''The '''fashion''' was for men to have long hair.'' #: ''At 62, he drives a small old car, and doesn't follow '''fashion''' trends.'' #: ''The models in their fancy '''fashions''' walked past the rich women in their seats.'' # {{countable}} A '''fashion''' is a way or manner. #: ''It's a good idea to pay what you owe in a timely '''fashion'''.'' #: ''I could see that she had made the list in her typical well-organized '''fashion'''.'' #: ''Hockey players fight all the time, but football players rarely act in a similar '''fashion'''.'' # {{uncountable}} The '''fashion''' business is the business of designing and making clothes. #: ''Lagerfeld is the current designer for the Chanel '''fashion''' house.'' #: ''Women who wanted to wear modern styles had them copied from Western '''fashion''' magazines by local dressmakers.''
=== Related words === * [[fashionable]] * [[fashionably]] * [[fashionista]] * [[unfashionable]] * [[unfashionably]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''fashion''' something, you design and make it, usually by hand. #: ''He makes beautiful art '''fashioned''' from simple things he gets from the garbage.''
[[Category:Fashion| ]]

=== Other spellings === * [[sick-o]]
== Noun == {{noun|3=sickoes}} # {{countable}} A '''sicko''' is a person who is [[mentally ill]] ([[crazy]]). # {{countable}} A '''sicko''' is a very bad person. #: ''He's a real '''sicko''' to rape children.'' # {{countable}} {{context|Australia}} A '''sicko''' is when you [[pretend]] to be sick to keep from [[work]]ing.
=== Related words === * [[sick]] * [[sickness]] * [[psycho]]
[[Category:People]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈsɪkən/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-sicken.wav|UK}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If something '''sickens''' you, it makes you [[sick]]; this often means making your [[stomach]] sick, so that you might [[vomit]]. #: ''The infection will '''sicken''' him until amputation is needed.'' # {{transitive}} If something '''sickens''' you, it is very [[bad]] and you [[hate]] it. #: ''It '''sickens''' me when people don't wash their hands after they use the toilet.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''sicken''' you become sick, or you become more sick. #: ''He will '''sicken''' if he doesn't get medicine soon.''
=== Synonyms === * [[disgust]] * [[nauseate]]
=== Related words === * [[sick]] * [[sickness]] * [[sicko]] * [[sickening]]

revision.text:
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If you are '''mentally ill''', you have a [[disease]] that affects your [[mind]]. You might do or [[think]] strange things. {{syn|crazy|insane}}
=== Related words === * [[mental illness]] * [[mental]] * [[ill]]

{{wikipedia}} == Noun == {{noun|mental illness|mental illnesses}} # {{cu noun}} A '''mental illness''' is a [[disease]] that affects your [[mind]]. This might make you do or [[think]] strange things. It might make you [[happy]], [[sad]], or [[afraid]] all the time.
===Synonyms=== * [[insanity]]
=== Related words === * [[mentally ill]] * [[mental]] * [[ill]] * [[crazy]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ɪnˈseɪn/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-insane.wav|UK}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Wodencafe-insane.wav|US}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # {{context|can be offensive}} If you are '''insane''' you can not think well because of [[mental illness]]. #: ''He was sent to a mental [[hospital]] because he was '''insane'''.'' #: ''Nothing he signed can be used because he was '''insane''' when he signed.'' # An '''insane''' [[idea]] is very strange, like something a crazy person might think of. #: ''That has got to be the most '''insane''' thing I have ever heard.'' # If something is '''insane''' it does not make [[sense]]. It is strange in a bad way. #: ''The price of gas these days is '''insane'''.''
=== Synonyms === * [[crazy]] * [[mentally ill]]
=== Antonyms === * [[sane]] * [[normal]]
=== Related words === * [[insanity]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/seɪn/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-sane.wav|UK}}
== Adjective == {{adj|sane|saner|sanest}} {{adj|more=true}} # If you are '''sane''', you [[think]] and [[feel]] in a [[normal]] way. You do not have [[mental illness]]. # If something is '''sane''', it is [[organized]] and normal; it makes [[sense]].
=== Antonyms === * [[insane]] * [[crazy]] * [[mentally ill]]
=== Related words === * [[saneness]] * [[sanity]]
[[Category:Mind]]

==Expression== {{expression}} #{{simile}} If you are '''crazy like a fox''' you do something [[smart]] that looks [[stupid]]. In this way you [[trick]] ([[fool]]) other people.
===Synonyms=== *[[sneaky]] *[[crafty]] *[[clever]]
===Related words=== *[[crazy]] *[[fox]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/ɑdz/}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ɒdz/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Wodencafe-odds.wav|US}}
== Noun == {{noun2}} # {{uncountable}}, {{mathematics}} In [[statistics]], the '''odds''' are the chance something will happen divided by the chance it will not happen: ## If "p" is the '''odds''' it will happen: <math>\frac{p}{1 - p}</math> ## The '''odds''' something will not happen: <math>\frac{1 - p}{p}</math> #:''What are the '''odds''' of winning in this game?'' #:''The '''odds''' of rolling a six are one in six, or 1 / 6.'' # {{uncountable}}, {{colloquial}} The '''odds''' of something happening are the [[chance]]s it will happen. #:''I don't like the '''odds''' here.'' #:''The '''odds''' of rolling a six are one in six, or 1 / 6.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{US}} {{IPA|/raɪd/}} * {{SAMPA|/r\aId/}} * {{audio|en-us-ride.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb2|ride|rides|rode|ridden|riding}} # If you '''ride''' something, you [[sit]] on it while it [[move]]s. #: ''I can '''ride''' a horse, but I cannot '''ride''' a [[motorcycle]].'' # If you '''ride''' someone, you have [[sex]] with them.
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''ride''' is a journey you take by riding. #: ''It was a long '''ride''' from Canada to Mexico.'' # {{countable}} {{informal}} A '''ride''' is a [[vehicle]] like a car, motorcycle or bicycle. #: ''That is a nice '''ride''' you are driving.'' # {{countable}} A '''ride''' is a machine that you ride on for fun. #: ''Roller-coasters and merry-go-rounds are my favorite '''rides'' at the park.'' # A [[lift]] given to someone in another person's vehicle. #: ''Can you give me a '''ride'''?'' # A '''ride''' is an act of [[sexual intercourse]].
[[Category:Transportation]] [[Category:Sex]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{US}} {{enPR|răp}}, {{IPA|/ræp/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-wrap.wav|UK}} * {{hmp|rap}}
== Verb == {{verb|wrap|p}} [[File:Celoštátna súťaž v darčekovom balení s medzinárodnou účasťou (25682540240).jpg|thumb|People '''wrapping''' gifts]] # If you '''wrap''' something you cover it with something like [[paper]] or [[cloth]]. This might be done by winding the paper or cloth over it. #: ''I wrapped the gifts in paper.'' #: ''The string was '''wrapped''' around a stick.'' # If you '''wrap''' something up you [[finish]] it. #: ''We need to '''wrap up''' this meeting and get back to work.''
== Noun == {{noun}} # A piece of [[clothing]] that you can wrap around your body to keep warm. # Something you wrap things in; a [[wrapper]]. #: ''I bought some gift'''wrap''' from the gift.'' # A food wrapped in soft bread. #: ''I had a chicken '''wrap''' for lunch.'' # You can say, "''That's a '''wrap'''!''" to say you have finished something.
<gallery> File:Roti Wrap Trafasie.jpg|Wraps File:Saree wrapping.jpg|This woman is helping a girl put on a type of wrap called a ''[[sari]]'' File:Plastfolie.JPG|Plastic wrap on a bowl File:Bubble Wrap.jpg|Bubble wrap </gallery>

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/fɔːlt/|/fɒlt/}}, {{SAMPA|/fO:lt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/fɔːlt/|/fɑːlt/}} * {{audio|en-us-fault.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-uk-fault.ogg|UK}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{uncountable}} If something is your '''fault''', you did something wrong or didn't do something right. #: ''It doesn't matter whose '''fault''' it is, let's work together to make it right.'' #: ''I'm sorry. It's my '''fault'''. I forgot to turn it off.'' #: ''It's clear that both sides are at fault.'' # {{countable}} A '''fault''' is a problem or a mistake. #: ''We found a few '''faults''' in the plan, but we'll fix them later.'' # {{countable}} A '''fault''' in your character is something about you that is not nice or good. #: ''The other girls thought that her only '''fault''' was that she was really stupid.'' # {{countable}} A '''fault''' is a long crack in the earth. #: ''The earthquake occurred near the San Andreas '''fault'''.'' # {{countable}} {{sports}} In sports like tennis or volleyball, a '''fault''' is hitting the ball in the wrong way, or to or from the wrong place.
=== Synonyms === * [[mistake]] * [[error]] * [[blame]]
=== Related words === * [[faulty]] * [[faultless]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''fault''' somebody for something bad, you say they did something wrong or didn't do something right. #: ''You can't '''fault''' him for not knowing about the change.''
=== Related words === * [[unfaulted]]

== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:B747 toilet.jpg|thumb|A '''toilet'''.]] # {{countable}} A '''toilet''' is something you may put human [[waste]] ([[feces]] and [[urine]]) into. #: ''Excuse me, I need to use the '''toilet'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''toilet''' is a [[bathroom]]. #: ''Where is the '''toilet'''?''
=== Synonyms === * [[commode]] * [[john]] * {{UK}} [[loo]] * {{US}} [[pisser]] * [[washroom]]
=== Related phrases === * [[go toilet]]

revision.text: ==Abbreviation== {{abbreviation}} # Short for [[kilometer]] or kilometers. #:''It is a about 100 '''km''' from here.'' #:''We were driving about 50 '''km'''/hour.''

==Number== {{proper noun|II}} # This is the [[Roman numeral]] for [[two]] ([[2]]). It may be written as '''II''' or '''ii'''. # '''II''' after a name means ''the [[second]]''. #:''"Pope John Paul '''II'''" is said as "Pope John Paul the second".''
[[Category:Roman numerals]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/zɛst/}} * {{audio|en-us-zest.ogg|US}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-zest.wav|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{uncountable}}, {{colloquial}} If you have '''zest''', you are full of [[excitement]] or [[enthusiasm]]; you are full of [[life]]. # {{uncountable}}, {{colloquial}} If [[food]] has '''zest''', it has a lot of [[flavor]]. It might be [[spicy]]. #: ''The hot [[pepper]]s add '''zest''' to the soup.'' # {{uncountable}}, {{colloquial}} If music has '''zest''', it is [[fast]] and [[lively]]. #: ''Play it with more '''zest''' this time.'' # {{cu noun}} {{context|cooking}} The [[outer]] [[skin]] of a [[citrus]] [[fruit]], used as a [[flavour]]ing.
=== Synonyms === * [[excitement]] * [[enthusiasm]]
== Verb == {{verb|zest}} # {{context|cooking}} If you '''zest''' something, you take the zest off of the [[fruit]].
=== Related words === * [[zesty]] * [[zestful]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈeː.ʤən.si/}} * {{audio|en-us-agency.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|agen|cy}}
== Noun == {{noun|agency|agencies}} # {{countable}} An '''agency''' is a group of people called [[agent]]s working together, or a place where agents work. ## An '''agency''' is a [[company]] ([[business]]) which usually [[represent]]s other people. The people at the agency work as agents to [[represent]] (stand for) their [[customer]]s. ##: ''Our '''agency''' works to help people find jobs in music.'' ## '''Agency''' is a company that does something specific. ##: ''Our ad '''agency''' has made advertisements for many important businesses.'' ## An '''agency''' is a certain part of a government. ##: ''He works for the real CIA, the actual Central Intelligence '''Agency'''.'' # {{uncountable}} '''Agency''' is the ability to do something.
=== Related words === * [[agent]] * [[directorate]]
[[Category:Philosophy]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/pæd/}} * {{audio|en-au-pad.ogg|Audio (AU)}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''pad''' is a [[material]] that is [[pack]]ed [[together]], usually to be [[between]] two other things. ## A '''pad''' is a flat thing you can sit on; a [[cushion]]. ## A '''pad''' is something worn in some [[sport]]s to protect [[athlete]]s ([[player]]s). ## A '''pad''' is the thick skin on an animals foot. ## A '''pad''' is a stack of [[paper]] for writing on. ## A '''pad''' is a piece of cloth used to stop [[menstrual]] blood from [[leak]]ing. # {{countable}} {{context|US}} {{slang}} A '''pad''' is a [[bed]]. # {{countable}} {{colloquial}} A '''pad''' is the place you live; it is your [[home]]. # {{countable}} {{music}} A '''pad''' is a low [[pitch]]ed musical sound that fills in the [[music]]. This is often in [[electronica]] or [[blues]]. # {{countable}} {{context|US}} A '''pad''' is a [[leaf]] of the [[water lily]].
=== Related words === * [[helipad]] * [[keypad]] * [[launchpad]] * [[notepad]]
== Verb 1 == {{verb|pad|d}} # {{transitive}} If you '''pad''' something, you [[stuff]] it. # If you '''pad''' something, you add pads to it. # If something '''pads''' something else, it blocks [[force]] or [[hitting]]. #: ''The cushion '''padded''' my fall.'' # If something '''pads''' something, it covers all or most of it. #: ''The walls were '''padded''' with cloth.'' #: ''The walls were '''padded''' so the crazy person who was kept there could not hurt himself.''
== Verb 2 == {{verb|pad|d}} # {{transitive}} If you '''pad''' along a [[road]], you [[travel]] down it. # {{intransitive}} If you '''pad''', you travel on foot. # {{intransitive}} If you '''pad''', you walk [[quietly]], usually without any shoes on.

==Number== {{proper noun|III}} # '''III''' or '''iii''' is the [[Roman numeral]] for [[three]] ([[3]]). # '''III''' after a name means ''the [[third]]''. #:''"Pope Innocent '''III'''" is said as "Pope Innocent the third".''
[[Category:Roman numerals]]

revision.text: ==Abbreviation== {{abbreviation}} # Short for [[doctor]]. Used as a [[title]] before a doctor's name. #:''I went to see '''Dr.''' Smith for some [[medicine]].'' #:'''''Dr.''' Schwarz has a [[Ph.D.]]''

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈɡəʊl.dən/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈɡoʊl.dən/|[ˈɡəl.dən]}} * {{audio|en-us-golden.ogg|US}} * {{audio|en-au-golden.ogg|AU}} * {{hyph|gol|den}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If something is '''golden''' it is made from [[gold]]. # If something is '''golden''' it is the same [[color]] as gold: ## If something is '''golden''' it is a color between [[yellow]] and [[brown]]. ##: ''Her hair was a '''golden''' blond.'' ## If something is '''golden''' it is a yellow. # If something is '''golden''' it is very good. #: ''It was a '''golden''' age, when everything seemed beautiful.'' #: ''I use to be a '''golden''' boy like you.'' -- {{w|Don Henley}}, "The Garden of Allah" # Your '''golden years''' are when you are [[old]] and [[retired]] from work. #: ''I use to watch a show about old ladies. It was called "''The '''Golden''' Girls.''"'' # The '''golden anniversary''' is the 50<sup>th</sup> [[anniversary]]. #: ''Her grandparents were celebrating the '''golden''' anniversary of their wedding.''
=== Synonyms === * [[gold]] * [[yellow]] * [[blond]]
== Noun == {{noun|golden|none}} # '''Golden''' is a [[color]] between [[yellow]] and [[brown]].
[[Category:Gold]]

{{wikipedia}} == Abbreviation == {{abbreviation}} # A short way of saying ''{{lc|Doctor}} of {{lc|Philosophy}}'', the highest [[degree]] you can get at a [[university]]. #: ''The [[laboratory]] Erika worked at wanted her to work on their most [[important]] [[project]]s, but she did not have enough [[education]], so they paid for her to get a '''Ph.D.''' in {{lc||Chemistry}}.''
=== Usage notes === * Although it stands for "Doctor of Philosophy," a '''Ph.D.''' can be a degree in almost any [[subject]]. * In the United States, anyone with a '''Ph.D.''' is called "Doctor," even though they are not a medical doctor.
=== Related words === * [[M.D.]]

== Abbreviation == {{abbreviation}} # A short way of saying ''{{lc|Medical}} {{lc|Doctor}}'', the [[degree]] you must have to give [[medicine]].
=== Related words === * [[Ph.D.]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/maʊnt/}} * {{audio|en-us-mount.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # If you '''mount''' something you get on to it. #: ''They '''mounted''' their horses and rode off.'' # If you '''mount''' something you attach it to something else. #: ''I need someone to '''mount''' this diamond on a ring.'' # to put a theatrical work on the stage #: ''The show was '''mounted''' in Montreal and New York.''
=== Related words === * [[dismount]] * [[stage]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} '''Mount''' is another word for [[mountain]]. This may be shortened to "Mt." to name a mountain. #: ''Jesus gave us the Sermon on the '''Mount'''.'' #: ''We were all worried when '''Mount''' Saint Helens exploded.'' # {{countable}} A '''mount''' is an animal you ride, often a [[horse]]. #: ''The policemen sat on his '''mount''' watching the park.''

{{wikipedia}}
==Noun== {{noun}} [[File:BadSalzdetfurthBadenburgerStr060529.jpg|thumb|A clock with Roman numerals]] [[File:CuttySarkRomNum.jpg|thumb|Roman numerals on a boat]] #A '''Roman numeral''' is a way of writing numbers used in [[Rome]] a long time ago. We do not write numbers like this much now. This is most often used to name parts of a [[series]]. Example are "[[I]]" (1), "[[II]]" (2), "[[III]]" (3), and "[[IV]]" (4).
== Numerals == * [[I]] (1) * [[II]] (2) * [[III]] (3) * [[IV]] (4) * [[V]] (5) * [[VI]] (6) * [[VII]] (7) * [[VIII]] (8) * [[IX]] (9) * [[X]] (10) * [[XX]] (20) * [[XXX]] (30) * [[XL]] (40) * [[L]] (50) * [[LX]] (60) * [[LXX]] (70) * [[LXXX]] (80) * [[XC]] (90) * [[C]] (100) * [[CC]] (200) * [[CCC]] (300) * [[CD]] (400) * [[D]] (500) * [[DC]] (600) * [[DCC]] (700) * [[DCCC]] (800) * [[CM]] (900) * [[M]] (1,000) * [[MM]] (2,000) * [[MMM]] (3,000) ===Related words=== *[[Rome]] *[[Roman]] *[[numeral]], [[number]]
[[Category:Roman numerals]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/dɪˈsɛndənt/}} * {{audio|en-us-descendant.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|des|cen|dant}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''descendant''' is [[something]] or [[someone]] that comes [[after]] something or someone ([[ancestor]]). #: ''Dogs are '''descendants''' of early wolves.'' #: ''You are a '''descendant''' of your [[grandparent]]s.'' #: ''I am a '''descendant''' of Grover Cleveland.''
=== Examples === Children, [[grandchildren]], great grandchildren. great great grandchildren are all descendants of the original mother and father. They are in the ''direct line of descent''. They have a [[hereditary]] [[relationship]].
=== Related words === * [[descend]] * [[descent]]
[[Category:People]]

=== Word parts === {{compound|any|one}}
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{a|northern dialect, not standard}} {{IPA|/ˈɛn.iː.wɒn/}}, {{SAMPA|/"En.i:.wQn/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈæn.i.wʊn/|/ˈɛn.i.wʊn/}}, {{SAMPA|/"{n.i.wUn/|/"En.i.wUn/}} * {{audio|en-us-anyone.ogg|US}}
== Determiner == {{determiner}} # {{det|s}} Any person. You use this word when there is no [[limit]] to who might be meant. You might be able to change '''anyone''' to any person's name. #: ''Help! Can '''anyone''' hear me?'' #: ''I don't know '''anyone''' here.'' #: '''''Anyone''' who saw the accident should phone the police.''
=== Synonyms === * [[anybody]]
=== Antonyms === * [[no one]]
=== Related words === * [[any]] * [[one]] * [[everyone]] * [[anything]]

If something '''crawls''', it [[walk]]s on four or more legs. For a person, this means using the hands and arms like legs. #: ''I '''crawled''' through the tunnel.'' # If something '''crawls''', it moves slowly. #: ''Yesterday seemed so long, like time was '''crawling'''.'' # If your [[skin]] '''crawls'''. you feel [[bug]]s are crawling over your body. This is often a way of saying you are [[afraid]] or [[disturbed]]. #: ''Just hearing about that makes my skin '''crawl'''.'' # If a place is '''crawling''' with something, that thing [[cover]]s that place. #: ''The club was '''crawling''' with people I'd like to meet.''

=== Related words === * [[crawler]] * [[crawl way]] * [[creepy-crawly]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # A '''crawl''' is when something crawls on more than two legs. #: ''If was a long '''crawl''' though the bushes.'' # If something is moving '''at a crawl''', it is going slowly. #: ''We were making progress, but only at a '''crawl'''.'' # The '''crawl''' is a way of [[swim]]ming. #: ''The first stroke we learned in swimming class was the '''crawl'''.''
[[Category:Swimming]]

This is sometimes used for similar things on other [[planet]]s. #: '''''Geology''' is not required for most students.'' #: ''The '''geologies''' of different types of mountains tell why they look different.'' #: ''The '''geology''' of [[Mars]] is different from that of Earth because Mars does not have a liquid center.''

== Noun == {{noun|2=heroes}} [[File:Godiva statue Broadgate Oct 2011.jpg|thumb|Lady Godiva, a heroine]] # {{countable}} A '''hero''' is a person who is very [[brave]] and does [[great]] things. The '''hero''' may be real or not real, and often [[defeat]]s [[dangerous]] {{r|enem|ies}} of the people. #: ''The '''hero''' Hercules was said to have killed the nine head snake called "hydra."'' #: ''I'm sorry your son died in battle, but he died a '''hero'''.'' # {{countable}} Your '''hero''' is a person you greatly [[admire]]. This may also be someone you want to be similar to. #: ''Leonardo DaVinci used to be my '''hero'''.'' # {{countable}} Your '''hero''' is someone who [[save]]s or [[defend]]s you. #: ''"Oh, my '''hero'''!" she said to her rescuer.'' # {{countable}} A '''hero''' is the main [[character]] in a story or [[film]] ([[movie]]). #: ''A female '''hero''' is a [[heroine]]''. # {{countable}}, {{colloquial}} Short for [[hero sandwich]]. # {{countable}} A good person with special [[power]]s; a [[superhero]].
=== Usage notes === The word ''hero'' was used for a [[male]] in the past, and a ''[[heroine]]'' was [[female]]. Now ''hero'' is often used for both [[sex]]es.
=== Antonym === * [[villain]]
=== Related words and phrases === * [[heroic]] * [[heroism]] * [[heroine]] * [[superhero]] * [[hero sandwich]] * [[unsung hero]] * [[antihero]]
[[Category:People]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈrəʊtɪk/}}, {{SAMPA|/"r@UtIk/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|rōt'ĭk}}, {{IPA|/ˈroʊtɪk/}}, {{SAMPA|/"roUtIk/}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If a sound in a word is '''rhotic''', it has the [[sound]] the letter ''[[r]]'' makes in most [[American]], [[Canadian]], and [[Irish]] ways of talking. # If a [[dialect]] (form of a language) or [[accent]] is '''rhotic''', it uses this sound after a [[vowel]]: often used in dividing English accents into the rhotic and the '''[[non-rhotic]]'''. (Note that all accents of English pronounce the rhotic sound if "r" or "rh" is immediately followed by a vowel – which means it is always pronounced at the start of a word.)
=== Antonym === * [[non-rhotic]]
=== Related words === * [[rhoticism]]
=== Note === The English rhotic [[consonant]] is written as [r] or [ɹ̠] (less precisely [ɹ]) in [[IPA]] (the International Phonetic Alphabet), or as the rhotic [[vowel]] /ɝ/ or /ɚ/ if no other vowel is there. The IPA symbol [r] represents a [[trill]]ed R, but /r/ sometimes used for all English [[pronunciation]]s of R (IPA symbols between // are [[phonemic]] transcriptions). This is because the various pronunciations are allophones, i.e. English speakers would hear all of them as R. Trilled /r/ is found in [[Scottish]] English and [[Indian]] English.

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{US}} {{IPA|/strɪŋ/}} * {{SAMPA|/strIN/}} * {{audio|en-us-string.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Bear cotton thread.jpg|thumb|{{lc|Thread}} is a kind of '''string'''.]] # {{countable}} A '''string''' is a long, thin and [[flexible]] [[cord]] that is used for [[tie|tying]]. {{syn|cord|rope|line|thread}} # {{countable}} A '''string''' is something that is long and can be [[bend|bent]]. #: ''There are 4 '''strings''' on a [[violin]].'' # {{countable}} A '''string''' is a group of things [[position]]ed or [[stick|stuck]] together in a [[line]]. #: ''My dog tried to grab one [[sausage]] with his mouth, but he took the whole '''string''' of sausages.'' # {{countable}} A '''string''' is a set of [[event]]s that happen one after the other. {{syn|sequence|series}} #: ''She remembered her past '''string''' of [[success]]es and felt happy.'' # {{countable}}, {{computing}} A '''string''' is a group of letters, numbers, [[punctuation]] marks, etc. ([[character]]s) that is stored in a [[computer]]'s [[memory]]. The characters can repeat and they are placed together in some order. # {{countable}}, {{music}} A '''string''' is a musical [[instrument]] that makes sounds from strings. # {{countable}}, {{physics}} A '''string''' is an [[infinite]]ly [[thin]] object that is 10<sup>-35</sup> [[meter]]s long. A part of physics called string [[theory]] claims that strings are [[subatomic]] [[particle]]s (they are the smallest bits of [[atom]]s) and physical [[state]]s affect the way they move repeatedly (they [[vibrate]]). # {{uncountable}}, {{slang}} '''String''' is [[marijuana]]. # {{countable}}, {{sport}} In [[billiards]] and other similar [[cue sport]]s, a '''string''' is one of the imaginary lines that divide a table. Each string joins two diamonds (points) that are marked in two opposite rails (edges) of the table. Strings may or may not be marked in the table. #: ''The long '''string''' connects the two diamonds at the center of the two short rails, so it divides the table in two.'' # {{countable}}, {{old}} A '''string''' is some thin part of a [[plant]] that looks like a thread (a plant [[fiber]]). # {{countable}}, {{old}} A '''string''' is a cord in a body of an animal, like a [[nerve]] or [[tendon]]. # {{plural only}} ''See [[strings#Noun]].''
=== Related words === * [[no strings attached]] * [[shoestring]] * [[stringy]]
== Verb == {{verb2|string|strings|strung|strung|stringing}} # {{transitive}} To '''string''' something is to put it on a [[#Noun|string]] or line. #: ''The beads can be '''strung''' to make a necklace.'' # {{transitive}} To '''string''' something is to put strings on it. #: ''I help my father '''string''' [[tennis]] [[racket]]s so he can sell them.'' # {{transitive}} To '''string''' something is to [[tie]] or [[hang]] it. #: ''They '''strung''' many small [[bell]]s in the [[tree]]s.'' # {{intransitive}} To '''string''' is to form into a string, like when a substance [[stretch]]es or when a group of people form a line. # {{intransitive}}, {{sport}} In [[billiards]] and other similar [[cue sport]]s, when two players '''string''', they each shoot a ball to the opposite end of the table. The balls then hit the opposite edge (or "rail") and go back to the starting one. The player with the ball that is the nearest to the starting rail makes the first move in the game.

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/bɛrəl/}} * {{audio|en-us-barrel.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Barrel (PSF).png|thumb|A drawing of a '''barrel'''.]] # {{countable}} A '''barrel''' is a [[tall]] and [[round]] [[container]]. # {{countable}} A '''barrel''' is the amount of something that is in a [[full]] barrel, or that would fit in the barrel. For example, a '''barrel''' of water or a '''barrel''' of [[beer]]. # {{countable}} The '''barrel''' of a [[gun]] is the part the [[bullet]] goes through. # {{countable}} The '''barrel''' of a [[clarinet]] is the part you [[connect]] the mouth piece. # {{countable}} The '''barrel''' of a [[horse]] or [[pony]] is its [[rib]]s. # {{countable}} A '''barrel''' is a solid metal tube that may be part of some [[machine]]s.
=== Related words and phrases === * [[barrel of monkeys]] * [[barrel roll]] * [[like shooting fish in a barrel]] * [[lock, stock, and barrel]] * [[over a barrel]]
== Verb == {{verb|barrel|l}} # {{intransitive}} If you '''barrel''', you move very [[quickly]].
[[Category:Containers]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈbæŋ.krəpt/|/ˈbæŋ.krʌpt/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈbæŋk.rəpt/|/ˈbæŋk.rʌpt/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-bankrupt.wav|UK}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If you are '''bankrupt''' you have declared [[bankruptcy]] (protection by [[law]] from [[debt]] you cannot [[pay]]). #: ''I don't have to pay now because I am '''bankrupt'''.'' # {{colloquial}} If you are '''bankrupt''' you have no [[money]]. #: ''I have been '''bankrupt''' all summer.'' # {{colloquial}} If you are '''bankrupt''' of something, you do not have that thing. For example, someone who is "morally '''bankrupt'''" has no [[moral]]s. #: ''We can't survive if our country becomes morally '''bankrupt'''.''
=== Synonyms === * {{a|out of money}} [[broke]], [[poor]]
=== Related words === * [[bank]] * [[bankruptcy]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''bankrupt''' someone, you make them [[#Adjective|bankrupt]].
[[Category:Money]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|gap}}, {{IPA|/ɡæp/}} * {{audio|en-us-gap.ogg|Audio (US)}} * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 gap.ogg|Audio (AU)}}
==Noun== {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''gap''' is a difference in the level of two groups. #: ''The money is to help bridge the '''gap''' between rich schools and poor schools.'' #: ''The gender '''gap''' in education is widening; fewer girls are going to school.'' #: ''The plan should narrow the growing '''gap''' between what students know and what businesses want.'' #: ''The company has closed the wage '''gap''' by raising women's salaries.'' # {{countable}} A '''gap''' is a small space or a short time between two things. #: ''Watch the '''gap''' between the platform and the train.'' #: ''There was a two-hour '''gap''' between when he arrived and the meeting time.'' #: ''Josh is one student who fell through the '''gaps''' and never learned to read.'' # {{countable}} A '''gap''' is missing space, time, information, etc. #: ''We don't know exactly what happened, but the new information will help us fill in some '''gaps''' in the story.'' #: ''There are still some '''gaps''' in the budget, but most things have been paid for.''
===Synonyms=== *[[space]] *[[break]] *[[difference]] *[[hole]] *[[opening]]
===Related words=== *[[gap year]]
