=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/træp/}} * {{audio|en-us-trap.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} [[File:Leghold trap.JPG|thumb|right|Leghold '''trap''']] # A '''trap''' is a [[machine]] or other [[device]] made to catch and sometimes [[kill]] [[animal]]s. #: ''He uses '''traps''' to deal with his mice problem.'' # A '''trap''' is a [[trick]] made to catch someone more [[general]]ly. #: ''She fell into the '''trap''' of misspelling "misspelling."'' # A '''trap''' is the [[cover]] over a [[hole]] or [[opening]]; a [[trapdoor]]. #: ''Close the '''trap''' before someone falls'' # A '''trap''' is any device used to hold and [[sudden]]ly let go of an object. #: ''They shot out of the school gates like greyhounds out of the '''trap'''.'' # A '''trap''' is a device in a [[pipe]] set up to hold and [[seal]] [[liquid]]s and stops [[gas]]es and [[let]]s [[liquid]]s [[flow]]. # A '''trap''' is a place in a [[water pipe]] or [[pump]] where air [[gather]]s. # {{history}} A '''trap''' is a light two-[[wheel]]ed [[carriage]] with [[spring]]s. #: ''Have James prepare the '''trap''' – I wish to visit the parson.'' # A '''trap''' is a [[kind]] of [[ladder]]. # {{slang}} A '''trap''' is a person's [[mouth]]. #: ''Keep your '''trap''' shut''. # {{slang}} {{vulgar}} A '''trap''' is a [[transvestite]], or a man who [[dress]]es as a woman, who goes with a man pretend to be a woman. #: ''I saw your brother asking a '''trap''' out last night at the bar.'' # {{computing}} A '''trap''' is [[exception]] made by the [[processor]]. # {{context|Australia}} {{slang}} {{history}} A mining [[license]] [[inspector]] during the Australian [[gold rush]]. # '''Trap''' is dark [[color]]ed [[rock]]. # {{uncountable}} '''Trap''' is a type of music.
=== Synonyms === * [[snare]] * [[trapper]]
=== Related words === * [[activity trap]] * [[beartrap]]/[[bear trap]] * [[booby trap]] * [[bus trap]] * [[firetrap]] * [[fish-trap]] * [[honey trap]] * [[mantrap]] * [[mousetrap]] * [[offside trap]] * [[optical trap]] * [[rattletrap]] * [[tourist trap]] * [[trapdoor]] * [[trapping]] * [[trapper]] * [[trappery]]
== Verb == {{verb|trap|p}} # {{transitive}} To '''trap''' something is to catch in a trap. # {{transitive}} To '''trap''' something is to [[ensnare]] it. # {{transitive}} To '''trap''' is to provide something with a trap. # {{intransitive}} To '''trap''' id to set traps for [[game]]; to make a [[business]] of trapping game. # {{intransitive}} To '''trap''' is to leave [[suddenly]] or [[flee]]. # {{intransitive}} {{computing}} To '''trap''' is to capture something such as a [[mistake]] so someone can fix it.
=== Related words === * [[trapper]] * [[entrap]] * [[entrapment]]

Feedback can be given [[anonymous]]ly on a page by clicking the choice in the left-side [[margin]] which best matches your opinion of the page. Go [//tools.wmflabs.org/simple/feedback/?action=results&wiki=simple.wiktionary here] to see feedback. You can also give feedback on page definitions by commenting below. General ideas about Simple English Wiktionary should be given at [[Wiktionary:Simple talk]]. [[Category:Wiktionary|Feedback]]
= Comments = This is the worst dictionary I’ve ever seen! Most of the time, you can barely find the definition of the word without scrolling through all of the other extraneous crap. How about definition FIRST, and then all of the other stuff! SOOO annoying! <!--Please don't make changes above this line-->
== [[:sting]] ==
you say the past of sting is stang, but then go on to give three examples, the first and third use the past simple but use stung, not stang. So, the question is, is the past of sting: stang or stung. Both exist, however, it seems that stung is now the accepted or more common. Some clarification would help here. :I believe that '''stang''' is rarely used now and stung is used in place of it. --[[User:Minorax|Minorax]] ([[User talk:Minorax|talk]]) 08:52, 5 June 2020 (UTC)

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|bŭt}}, {{IPA|/bʌt/}} * {{SAMPA|/bVt/}} * {{audio|en-us-butt.ogg|US}} * {{hmp|but}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} Your '''butt''' is your [[bottom]], your [[bum]], the part of your body that you sit on. {{syn|bum|bottom|ass|buttocks|backside|behind|rear|rear-end|booty|tush|tushie|hein|heinie|gluteus-maximus|bottom|derrière}} #: ''The exercise works your legs, '''butt''', and back.'' # {{countable}} When someone says, ''get your '''butt''' over''/''back''/''out of here'', they mean move yourself. #: ''Get your '''butt''' over here.'' = come here # If someone or something is a pain in the '''butt''', they are [[unpleasant]] or [[annoying]]. #: ''Stop that! You're such a pain in the '''butt'''.'' # {{countable}} If you work/run/study/play your '''butt''' off, you do so very hard. #: ''We played our '''butts''' off in the game today, and we still lost.'' # {{countable}} The '''butt''' of something is its end. {{syn|end}} #: ''He threw his cigarette '''butt''' on the ground.'' #: ''He put the '''butt''' of the gun against his shoulder and looked down its long barrel.'' # {{countable}} If you're the '''butt''' of a joke, people are laughing at you because the joke makes you seem foolish or bad. #: ''He hated being the '''butt''' of other people's jokes.'' # {{countable}} {{context|British}} A '''butt''' is a large container for liquids. {{syn|barrel}} #: ''The rain flowed into the '''butt'''.''
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If animals '''butt''' something, they hit it with their head or horns. #: ''The two goats '''butted''' each other and one fell over.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''butt''' up against something, you reach it or come into conflict with it; often used when something stops progress. #: ''The car '''butted''' up against the gate and could not go further.'' # {{intransitive}} If two people '''butt heads''', they disagree or argue strongly. #: ''The managers '''butted''' heads about the new schedule.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''butt''' two things (for example, pipes or boards), you join their ends together so they meet directly. #: ''They '''butted''' the two metal pipes together before welding the joint.'' # {{intransitive}} If you '''butt''' in, you interrupt a conversation or activity by speaking or acting when you should not. #: ''Please don't '''butt''' in while I'm talking.'' # {{intransitive}} {{slang}} If you tell someone to '''butt out''', you tell them not to interfere; to leave a matter alone. #: ''This is between them — you should '''butt''' out.''
=== Related words ===
* [[buttocks]]
[[Category:Body parts]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{US}} {{IPA|/əˈskraɪb/}} * {{audio|en-au-ascribe.ogg|AU}}
== Verb == {{verb|ascrib|e}} # {{transitive}} To [[attribute]] a cause or [[characteristic]] to someone or something. #: ''We may '''ascribe''' the [[failure]] to the [[leader]], but it is also explained by bad luck.'' # {{transitive}} To attribute a book, painting or any work of art or [[literature]] to a [[specific]] writer or painter or creator. #: ''It is [[arguable]] as to whether we can truly '''ascribe''' this play to Shakespeare.''
=== Synonyms === * [[attribute]] * [[impute]]
=== Related words === * [[ascribable]] * [[ascription]] * [[ascriptive]]

revision.text: [[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px]] Welcome to Wiktionary. Everyone is welcome to make helpful changes to the dictionary. However, please do not [[Wiktionary:No personal attacks|attack]] other editors{{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|, as you did on [[:{{{1}}}]]}}. If you disagree with changes, please talk about the changes and not the editors who made them. Take a look at the [[Wiktionary:Welcome|welcome page]] to learn more about changing Wiktionary. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{2|}}}|{{{2}}}|Thank you.}}<!-- Template:uw-npa1 --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px]] {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|With regard to your comments on [[:{{{1}}}]]: }}Please see "[[Wiktionary:No personal attacks]]". Talk about ''changes'' editors have made, not the editors. Personal attacks damage the community and scare away users. Please note that more personal attacks will lead to you being [[Wiktionary:Blocking policy|blocked]] for disruption. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{2|}}}|{{{2}}}|Thank you.}}<!-- Template:uw-npa2 --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:Information.svg|25px]] Hello, I noticed that you recently created a new entry or made changes to one{{#if: {{{1|}}}|, such as "[[{{{1}}}]]",}} by adding material copied from a book, magazine, newspaper or another website without the [[Wiktionary:Copyrights|permission of the copyright holder]]. Many sources, including websites found on the Internet, are copyrighted. I'm afraid Wiktionary cannot accept '''any''' material copied from such sources as it can get into serious legal trouble. The entry or changes have been or will soon be deleted. Next time, look up sources to find out ''information'' for entries and explain it in your own words, and don't copy ''sentences'' or ''images'' from them. Thank you.<!-- Template:uw-copyright1 --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:{{{icon|Stop hand nuvola.svg}}}|25px]] Please stop adding [[Wiktionary:Copyrights|copyrighted]] material to Wiktionary without permission from the copyright holder{{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|, as you did to "[[:{{{1}}}]]"}}.
For legal reasons, we cannot accept text or images borrowed from books, magazines, newspapers or other websites. Such additions will be deleted. You may use these sources to find out ''information'' for Wiktionary, but cannot copy ''sentences'' or ''images'' from them. Wiktionary takes copyright violations very seriously and users who add copyrighted material again and again '''will''' be [[Wiktionary:Blocks and bans|blocked]] from changing Wiktionary. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{2|}}}|{{{2}}}|}} {{documentation}}

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px]] Welcome, and thanks very much for your recent changes to {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|the Wiktionary article "[[:{{{1}}}]]"|Wiktionary}}. However, please take a moment to review your changes for [[spelling]], [[grammar|grammatical]], [[capitalization]], and [[punctuation]] errors before you save. This will help lessen the editing others must do on the entry, and will help keep Wiktionary looking neat and professional.
This message is not meant to discourage you from changing Wiktionary but rather to encourage the best possible writing from our authors. Please take a look at the [[Wiktionary:Welcome|welcome page]] to learn more about changing this dictionary. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{2|}}}|{{{2}}}|Thank you.}}<!-- Template:uw-spellcheck --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px]] Thank you for your changes to Wiktionary. When using certain templates on talk pages{{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|, as you did to "[[:{{{1}}}]]"}}, don't forget to [[:w:Wikipedia:Template substitution|substitute the templates]] by adding "'''subst:'''" to the template tag. For example, use "{{subst:vandalism1}}" instead of "{{vandalism1}}". This reduces server load and prevents accidental blanking of the template. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{2|}}}|{{{2}}}|Thank you.}} <!-- Template:Uw-subst --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px]] Hello. In case you didn't know, when you post messages on talkpages and Wiktionary pages {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|, such as you did in "[[:{{{1}}}]]"}}, you should [[:w:Wikipedia:Signatures|sign your posts]] by typing four [[tilde]]s ("~~~~") at the end of your message. You may also click on the signature button [[File:Signature_icon.png]] which is above the edit window. This will put a signature containing your user name or [[IP address]] and the time you posted the message. This information is useful because other editors will be able to tell who said what, and when. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{2|}}}|{{{2}}}|Thank you.}} <!-- Template:uw-tilde --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px]] Welcome. Our [[Wiktionary:Image use|policy]] is that images cannot be uploaded directly to the Simple English Wiktionary, and any images uploaded here{{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|, such as "[[:File:{{{1}}}]]",}} will be deleted. Please upload any images to the [[commons:|Wikimedia Commons]]. Images uploaded there can be used in Simple English Wiktionary entries in the usual way. {{{2|Thank you.}}}<!-- Template:uw-upload --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px|left]] Please do not remove [[Wiktionary:Deletion policy#Quick deletion|quick deletion]] tags from entries{{#if:{{{1|}}}|, as you did to "[[:{{{1}}}]]",}} without a good reason. If you think the entry should not be deleted, please explain your reason on the entry's [[:w:Wikipedia:Talk page|talk page]]. Thank you. <!-- Template:Uw-qd --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px|]] Hello, and welcome to Wiktionary! I don't want to seem unfriendly or make you feel unwelcome, but I noticed {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|your user subpage at [[:{{{1|}}}]]|your user page}}, and I am concerned that it might not meet Wiktionary's [[:w:Wikipedia:User page|user page guideline]]. After you have read that guideline, could we discuss my concerns here? I'd like to hear your views, such as why you want the current page, and whether you might agree to change it to something else. There are several ways we can deal with this matter: * If you can explain why your user page meets Wiktionary's user page guideline, I can stop worrying about it. * If you decide to delete the page yourself, please add "{{delete}}" to the top of your user page. An [[Wiktionary:Administrators|administrator]] will then delete it. * If the two of us can't agree on what needs to be done, I can list your user page at "[[Wiktionary:Requests for deletion]]" so that we can discuss with other editors whether the page should be kept or deleted. {{documentation}}

[[File:{{{icon|Information.svg}}}|25px]] Please do not make test changes in Wikipedia articles{{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{1|}}}|, such as those you made to "[[:{{{1}}}]]",}} even if you want to fix them. Such edits seem to be [[Wiktionary:Vandalism|vandalism]] and have been changed back or deleted. If you would like to try out changing Wiktionary again, please use the [[Wiktionary:Sandbox|sandbox]]. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{2|}}}|{{{2}}}|Thank you.}}<!-- Template:uw-test2 --><noinclude> {{documentation}} <!-- Categories, interwikis and TemplateData goes to the /doc subpage --> </noinclude>

== Welcome to the Simple English Wiktionary == {| style="background-color:#F5FFFA; padding:0;" cellpadding="0" |class="MainPageBG" style="border:1px solid #084080; background-color:#F5FFFA; vertical-align:top; color:#000000; font-size:85%"| {| width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="5" style="vertical-align:top; background-color:#F5FFFA; padding:0;" !
Hi, {{PAGENAME}}! [[Wiktionary:Welcome|Welcome]] to Simple English Wiktionary! Thank you for [[Special:Contributions/{{SUBST:PAGENAME}}|your changes]]! If you need help, check out [[Help:Contents|the Help section]] of Wiktionary, or leave a message on my talk page. Whenever leaving messages on talk pages, please remember to sign your name by typing four 'tildes' (like this: ~~~~); doing this makes your name and the date show up. Also, it helps if you write something in the box that says 'change summary' whenever you change an entry. Below are some useful links to make your time here simpler. If you make a short entry please mark it with {{tl|stub}}. Happy changing! ~~~~
|} {| width="100%" style="background-color:#F5FFFA;" |class="MainPageBG" style="width: 55%; border:1px solid #FFFFFF; background-color:#F5FFFA; vertical-align:top"| {| width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="5" style="vertical-align:top; background-color:#F5FFFA" !
Getting Started

Getting Help

Policies and Guidelines
|- | style="color:#000"| * [[Wiktionary:Neutral point of view|Neutral point of view]] * [[Wiktionary:What Wiktionary is not|What Wiktionary is not]]
* [[Wiktionary:Copyrights|Copyrights]] • [[Wiktionary:Image use policy|Using images and Pictures]] * [[Wiktionary:Vandalism|Vandalism]] • [[Wiktionary:Deletion policy|Deletion policy]] |- |} |class="MainPageBG" style="width: 55%; border:1px solid #FFFFFF; background-color:#F5FFFA; vertical-align:top"| {| width="100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="5" style="vertical-align:top; background-color:#F5FFFA" !
The Community
|- |style="color:#000"| * [[Wiktionary:Assume good faith|Assume good faith]] * [[Wiktionary:Community Portal|Community Portal]] • [[Wiktionary:Simple talk|Simple talk]] * [[Wiktionary:Announcements|Announcements]] |- !
Things to do

{| width="100%" style="background: #FEC; border: 1px solid #FDA; line-height: 1.8em; margin-bottom: 1em; -moz-border-radius: 0.5em;" cellspacing="10" ! style="background: #FFE3AE; font-size: 1.3em; padding: 0.5em; border: 1px solid #FC9; -moz-border-radius: 0.3em;" | Welcome, {{BASEPAGENAME}}! |- | {| width="100%" cellspacing="10" style="border: 1px #FDA solid; background: #FFFFE5; -moz-border-radius: 0.5em;" | Hello, '''{{BASEPAGENAME}}''', and [[Wiktionary:Welcome|welcome]] to the '''Simple English Wiktionary'''! At Wiktionary, remember to [[Wiktionary:Be bold|be '''bold''']]! This means that you should not be afraid to change any entries. This is because, if you make any mistakes, you can always fix it later! If you have any questions, you can always ask them at [[Wiktionary:Simple talk|Simple Talk]].

[[File:Stop x nuvola.svg|left|40px]]'''Your account has been blocked indefinitely''' because {{{1|{{{reason|it is an obvious violation of our username policy – it is a bad word, attacks or pretends to be another person, or clearly suggests that you do not wish to make Wiktionary better}}}}}} (see our [[Wiktionary:Blocking policy|blocking]] and [[Wiktionary:Username|username]] policies for more information). We invite everyone to make changes to Wiktionary that improve it, but users are not allowed to edit with unsuitable usernames, and we do not allow [[trolling]] or other bad behavior. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{sig|}}}|~~~~}}
{{documentation}}

[[File:Information.svg|left|80px]] Your account, {{BASEPAGENAME}} has been [[WT:BLOCK|blocked]] from changing Wiktionary because {{{reason|{{{1|the username may not meet our [[Wiktionary:Username|username policy]]}}}}}}. '''This is not anything against you, and you are encouraged to [[Special:Userlogin/signup|choose a new account name]] that meets our guidelines – we hope to see you editing again soon!''' :If you feel this block was made wrongly, you may quickly and easily ask to be unblocked. [[Wiktionary:Username|Our username policy]] says how you should choose your username. Put simply, you should not have a username that people find offensive, advertises a real world group or company, or is confusing (for instance, if it pretends to be another user). If you have already made changes and wish to keep your changes under a new name '''you may ask us to [[Wiktionary:Changing username|rename your account]]'''. If you want to, please follow these directions: ;Ask for an unblock :Type {{unblock|reason}} on your user talk page which you should still be able to change – you want to change your username, so say that. If an [[WT:ADMIN|admin]] thinks that you should be unblocked, he or she will do so for you, normally for 24 hours. ;Request a change in username :Go [[WT:CHU|here]] and ask for a new name. It will be changed by someone once they get the request. If you have made few or no changes, then it would be a lot easier to simply [[Special:Userlogin/signup|'''create a new account''']]. Please note that the software Wikipedia uses may automatically block you from creating a new account – this is a mistake, and shouldn't have happened. If this has happened, attract attention using the unblock template as explained above, and an admin will fix it for you. If you think you shouldn't have been blocked, add {{unblock|''your reason here''}} {{{{{subst|}}}#switch:{{NAMESPACE}}|User talk=below|on [[Special:MyTalk|your user talk page]]}} or email the administrator who blocked you. {{{{{subst|}}}#if:{{{sig|}}}|~~~~}}
{{documentation}}

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{enPR|bägən}}, {{IPA|/ˈbɑːɡən/|/-ɡɪn/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|bärgən}}, {{IPA|/ˈbɑːrɡən/}} * {{audio|en-us-bargain.ogg|US}} * {{hyph|bar|gain}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # If you make a '''bargain''' with someone, that means you agreed with them to make an [[exchange]] or [[trade]]. #: ''He gave me his sandwich and I gave him my apple; it was a '''bargain'''.'' #: ''I made a '''bargain''' with Joe: if he would wash my car I would mow his lawn.'' # If you buy something that is a '''bargain''', that means it is a good [[deal]]; [[cheap]]. #: ''This house cost me $1. What a '''bargain'''!''
=== Synonyms === * [[haggle]] * [[contract]] * [[purchase]]
=== Antonyms === * [[rip-off]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} To '''bargain''' is to make a [[deal]]. #: ''We had to '''bargain''' for three hours to make an [[agreement]].'' # {{transitive}} To '''bargain''' is to [[barter]]; to [[trade]].

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/bæʃ/}} * {{audio|en-au-bash.ogg|AU}}
== Noun == {{noun|bash|bashes}} # If you are going to a '''bash''', you are going to a large [[party]]. #: ''We are going to have a '''bash'''!'' # A '''bash''' is an [[attack]]. #: ''The guys went out to '''bash''' a few gays.''
== Verb == {{verb|bash|es}} # To '''bash''' someone is to [[attack]] them, often with [[fist]]s; to [[strike]] hard. #: ''Gay '''bashing''' is deplorable.'' #: ''The [[bully]] always '''bashes''' the little kids.'' # If someone '''bashes''' your idea, that means they don't like it. #: ''My plan was subject to much '''bashing''' by the press.'' # To '''bash''' is to run into; to [[collide]]; to [[smash]]. #: ''I was '''bashed''' against the wall, and it hurt.''
[[Category:Parties]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/buː/}} * {{audio|en-au-boo.ogg|AU}}
== Interjection == {{interjection}} # '''Boo''' is a word that is sometimes shouted to [[scare]] a person. #: ''He jumped up from behind the box and yelled "'''boo'''!" I was frightened.'' #: ''Ghosts say "'''boo'''".'' # If someone in an [[audience]] says "'''boo'''", that means that they do not like the [[show]]. #: '''''Boo''', get off the stage.''
== Noun == {{noun}} # A [[loud]] and sometimes frightening [[yell]] or [[shout]].
== Verb == {{verb}} # To '''boo''' someone is to shout or yell at them. #: ''When it was my turn to sing a song, the crowd '''booed''' at me.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|bouns}}, {{IPA|/baʊns/}} * {{SAMPA|/baUns/}} * {{audio|en-us-bounce.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb|bounc|e}} [[File:Bouncywikilogo.gif|thumb|This Wikipedia logo is '''bouncing''']] # To '''bounce''' is to change the direction of motion after hitting an object. #: ''The tennis ball '''bounced''' off the wall.'' # To '''bounce''' is to make something move quickly up and down, or down and up. #: ''He '''bounced''' the child on his knee.'' # To '''bounce''' a check, is to be refused by a bank.
=== Synonyms === * [[rebound]] * [[bob]]
== Noun == {{noun}} # A '''bounce''' is a change of direction of [[motion]], often after hitting an object. #: ''The poor bird made a big '''bounce''' off my car when we hit each other.'' # A '''bounce''' can also mean movement that is up and down, up and down ([[repeat]]ed).

=== Pronunciation === ;noun * {{UK}} {{enPR|kŏn'strŭkt}}, {{IPA|/ˈkɒnstrʌkt/}}, {{SAMPA|/"kQnstrVkt/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|kän'strŭkt}}, {{IPA|/ˈkɑnstrʌkt/}}, {{SAMPA|/"kAnstrVkt/}} * {{audio|en-us-construct-noun.ogg|US}} ;verb * {{enPR|kənstrŭkt'}} * {{IPA|/kənˈstrʌkt/}} * {{SAMPA|/k@n"strVkt/}} * {{audio|en-us-construct-verb.ogg|US}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # Something made from parts. #: ''That artwork is a '''construct''' of wires and tubes.'' # A [[concept]] or [[model]]. #: The '''construct''' of the world being [[flat]] was changed due to Copernicus' telescope.
=== Synonyms === * {{a|something constructed from parts}} [[construction]] * {{a|concept, model}} [[concept]], [[idea]], [[model]], [[notion]], [[representation]]
== Verb == {{verb}} {{AVL}} # {{transitive}} To [[make]], [[build]], or [[form]] (something) by putting the [[part]]s together. #: ''We '''constructed''' the radio from parts.'' # {{transitive}} Similarly, to build (a [[sentence]] or an [[argument]]) by arranging [[word]]s or [[idea]]s. #: ''A sentence may be '''constructed''' with a subject, verb and object.'' # {{transitive}}; {{geometry}} To [[draw]] a [[figure]] by following a method. #: '''''Construct''' a circle that touches each [[point]] of the given [[triangle]].''
=== Synonyms === * {{a|build or form by assembling parts}} [[assemble]], [[build]], [[form]], [[make]], [[put together]] * {{a|build (a sentence or argument)}} [[form]]
=== Antonyms === * {{a|build or form by assembling parts}} [[destroy]], [[disassemble]], [[dismantle]], [[take apart]]
=== Related words === * [[reconstruct]] * [[construction]] * [[constructive]]
[[Category:Construction]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/tʃiːt/}} * {{audio|en-us-cheat.ogg|US}}
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} To [[break]] the [[rules]] for your own [[gain]]. #: ''Don't play cards with her, she '''cheats'''.'' # {{intransitive}} To have a [[relationship]] with someone not one's [[spouse]] or [[partner]] or someone who is married to someone else. #: ''He is '''cheating''' on his wife with his secretary.'' # {{transitive}} To [[avoid]] something that seemed likely. #: ''To '''cheat''' death.'' #: ''To '''cheat''' fate.''
== Noun == {{noun}} # Someone who cheats (informal: [[cheater]]). # A card game where the goal is to have no cards remaining in a hand, often by telling [[lies]]. # A hidden means of gaining an unfair advantage in a computer game, often by entering a [[cheat code]].
=== Related words and phrases === * [[cheat code]] * [[cheater]] * [[cheating]]<!--noun, adjective--> * [[cheat on]] * [[windcheater]]

=== Pronunciation === ;noun 1, verb 1 * {{UK}} {{enPR|bō}}, {{IPA|/bəʊ/}}, {{SAMPA|/b@U/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|bō}}, {{IPA|/boʊ/}}, {{SAMPA|/boU/}} * {{audio|en-uk-bow-1.ogg|UK}} * {{audio|en-us-bow-1.ogg|US}} * {{hmp|beau}}
;noun 2, verb 2, noun 3 * {{enPR|bou}}, {{IPA|/baʊ/}} * {{audio|en-uk-bow-2.ogg|UK}} * {{audio|en-us-bow-2.ogg|US}} * {{hmp|bough}}
== Noun 1 == {{noun}} # A '''bow''' is a [[weapon]] whose ends are connected by a [[string]], used for [[shoot]]ing [[arrow]]s. # A '''bow''' is a [[curve]]d bend. Such as in a river or road. # A '''bow''' is a long stick-like object with horsehair, used for [[play]]ing [[stringed]] [[musical]] [[instrument]]s. # A '''bow''' is a type of [[knot]] with two loops, such as used to [[tie]] [[shoe]]s or strings on a dress, or to make something pretty, such as in [[gift]]s.
<gallery> File:Hun bow.jpg|A bow File:Bow Cello.jpg|A [[musical]] bow File:BOWTIE red velvet pretied clipon.JPG|A [[bowtie]] </gallery>
=== Synonyms === * {{a|bow-shaped bend}} [[arc]], [[bend]], [[curve]] * {{a|tool for playing stringed instruments}} [[fiddlestick]]
=== Related word and phrases === * [[bow and arrow]] * [[bowman]] * [[crossbow]] * [[longbow]] * [[oxbow]] * [[rainbow]]<!--(noun sense "bow-shaped bend")--> * [[shortbow]] * [[bow tie]]<!--(noun sense "knot with two loops")-->
== Verb 1 == {{verb}} # To [[play]] music on (a stringed instrument) using a bow. #: ''The musician '''bowed''' his violin expertly.'' # {{intransitive}} To become bent or curved. #: ''The shelf '''bowed''' under the weight of the books.'' # {{transitive}} To make something bend or curve.
== Noun 2 == {{noun}} # To [[bend]] the [[waist]] or [[head]] forward toward someone, usually showing [[respect]]. #: ''He '''bowed''' politely as he entered the room.''
== Verb 2 == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} To bend oneself as a sign of respect.
=== Related words and phrases === * [[bow down]] * [[bow out]] * [[bow and scrape]] * [[bow to someone's better judgement]] * [[take a bow]] * [[curtsy]] * [[kowtow]]
== Noun 3 == {{noun}} [[File:Bow (PSF).png|thumb|The '''bow''' of a ship]] # {{nautical}} The [[front]] of a [[boat]] or [[ship]].
[[Category:Ship parts]] [[Category:Body language]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈdʒuːnɪə/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈdʒunjər/|/ˈdʒunjɚ/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-junior.wav|Audio (UK)}} * {{hyph|ju|nior}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # {{lc|Young}}er. # The third academic year in a [[high school]] or [[university]]. #: ''I'm hoping that my '''junior''' year will be better than my [[sophomore]] year.'' # In some cases, used to show less [[experience]], not age. #: ''He is the '''Junior''' Senator from that state.''
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A younger person. #: ''Steve is four years his brother's '''junior'''.'' # {{countable}} A third-year student at a high school or university. #: ''I'm a '''junior''', but a lot of my friends are seniors.'' # {{countable}} A name ending used after a son's name when his father has the same name. It is often shortened to ''[[Jr.]]'' #: ''Which President Bush do you mean, '''junior''' or senior?''
=== Antonyms === * [[senior]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/iːz/}} * {{audio|en-us-ease.ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Noun == {{noun|ease|none}} {{uncountable}} # The state of being [[comfortable]] or [[relax]]ed. #: ''She enjoyed the '''ease''' of living in a house where the servants did all the work.'' # {{lc|Free}} from [[pain]], [[worry]], etc. #: ''His mind was at '''ease''' when he took the test. He knew he had studied well.'' # Free from [[effort]], [[difficulty]] or [[hardship]]. #: ''He passed all the exams with '''ease'''.'' # Doing something without much effort. #: ''He played the piano with '''ease'''.'' # To be [[free]] from [[money]] [[problem]]s. #: ''After winning the lottery, she lived a life of '''ease'''.'' # {{lc|Relaxation}}, [[rest]] and [[leisure]]. #: ''We took our '''ease''' on the patio.''
=== Synonyms === * [[comfort]] * [[peace]] * [[peace of mind]] * [[dexterity]] * [[skill]] * [[leisure]] * to [[relax]] * to [[rest]]
=== Related words === * [[at ease]] * [[easy]]
== Verb == {{verb|eas|e}} # {{transitive}} To free or lessen (something) from [[pain]], [[worry]], agitation, etc. #: ''He '''eased''' his conscience telling her what he had done wrong.'' #: ''He loosened his shoe to '''ease''' the pain.'' # {{transitive}} To [[loosen]] or [[relax]] the [[tension]] on (something). #: ''We '''eased''' the rope, then lowered the [[sail]].'' # {{transitive}} To [[reduce]] the [[difficulty]] of (something). #: ''We had to '''ease''' the entry requirements.'' # {{transitive}} To move (something) [[slowly]] and [[carefully]]. #: ''He '''eased''' the car into the parking space.''
=== Synonyms === * [[alleviate]], [[lessen]], [[reduce]] * {{a|informal}} [[give someone a break]], [[lay off]] * {{a|loosen or slacken the tension on (something)}} [[loosen]], [[relax]], [[slacken]]

===Pronunciation=== * {{UK}} {{enPR|îr'ə}}, {{IPA|/ˈiə(r).ə/}}, {{SAMPA|/"I@(r).@/}} * {{US}} {{enPR|ĕr'ə}}, {{IPA|/ˈɛrə/}}, {{SAMPA|/"Er@/}} * {{audio|En-us-era.ogg|Audio (US)}} * {{audio|En-uk-era.ogg|Audio (UK)}}
==Noun== {{noun}} # A [[time]] [[period]], generally more than one [[year]]. Often used to show a time when something important was happening. #: ''The Elizabethan '''era''' is when Queen Elizabeth was the Queen of England.'' #: ''During the World War II '''era''', jazz music was popular.'' #A [[geology|geological]] series of rocks laid down over several hundred [[million]] years. #: ''[[dinosaur|Dinosaur]]s lived during the Mesozoic era''.
===Synonyms=== * [[age]] * [[epoch]] * [[period]]
[[Category:Time]]

===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|/ɪgˈzɔst/}} * {{audio|en-us-exhaust.ogg|Audio (US)}}
==Verb== {{verb}} # To use up completely. #: ''So many people came to dinner that we had '''exhausted''' the supply of silverware. I had to use my fingers.'' # To [[empty]] by using. #: The well was '''exhausted'''. # To wear out; use up one's [[strength]], [[patience]], or [[resource]]s. #: ''You look '''exhausted''', have you had any sleep?'' # To [[complete]]ly develop or discuss some topic or idea. #: ''We '''exhausted''' our money saving topic, there was nothing else to talk about on it.''
===Synonyms=== * [[consume]] * [[spend]] * [[tire out]] * [[weary]]
===Related words=== * [[exhaustion]]
==Noun== {{noun}} [[File:Tubo Escape.jpg|thumb|Exhaust pipe]] # The part of an [[engine]] or [[motor]] where burned [[gas]]es or [[steam]] comes out. # A [[pipe]] or [[vent]] used to take bad air out of a room or closed space.
===Related words and phrases=== * [[exhaust fan]] * [[exhaustless]] * [[exhaust nozzle]] * [[exhaust pipe]] * [[exhaust port]] * [[exhaust purifier]] * [[exhaust steam]] * [[exhaust system]] * [[exhaust valve]]

=== Synonyms === * {{a|influenza}} [[grippe]], [[grip]]
=== Related words === * [[avian flu]] * [[bird flu]] * [[blue flu]] * [[diplomatic flu]] * [[Spanish flu]] * [[stomach flu]] * [[swine flu]]

===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|/fʌs/}} * {{audio|en-us-fuss.ogg|Audio (US)}}
==Noun== {{noun|fuss|fusses}} # {{cu noun}} Too much [[activity]], [[worry]], [[bother]], or [[talk]] about something. #: ''They made a big '''fuss''' about the wedding plans.'' #: ''What's all the '''fuss''' about?'' # A [[complaint]] or [[noise]]. #: ''If you make enough of a '''fuss''' about the [[problem]], maybe they'll fix it for you.'' # A show of [[affection]] or about [[like|liking]] something. #: ''They made a great '''fuss''' over the new baby.''
==Verb== {{verb|fuss|es}} # {{intransitive}} To be very worried or excited about something, often too much. #: ''His grandmother will never quit '''fussing''' over his [[cigarette]] [[smoke|smoking]].'' # {{intransitive}} To [[fiddle]]; to [[move]] about, or [[adjust]]; to [[worry]] something #: ''Quit '''fussing''' with your hair. It looks fine.''
===Usage notes=== * to fuss [[with]] * to fuss [[over]] * to fuss [[about]]
===Related words and phrases=== * [[fussy]] * [[fidget]] * [[fuss and bother]] * [[no muss, no fuss]]

revision.text:
{{Wiktionary:Simple talk/Archives}} == Feedback == Does anyone support the idea of enabling [[:en:WT:Feedback|this]] on this simple.wikt? In my opinion it is not only a way of getting feedback, but also a way of getting to see how many visitors are come to this wiki. --'''''[[User:The New Mikemoral|The New]]''''' [[User talk:The New Mikemoral|Mikemoral]] [[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 06:43, 18 January 2010 (UTC) : Sure, but I think "anonymous" is a bit misleading since the user's IP address gets publicly logged in the page history... — '''[[User:Wenli|Wenli]]''' ([[User talk:Wenli|reply here]]) 04:55, 20 January 2010 (UTC) : I would have to agree here. This might enable us to gather more anonymous users and potentially, more new users for this site, which I think would be a good thing. [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 07:16, 20 January 2010 (UTC) ::I was revering to the JavaScript [[w:User:Conrad.Irwin/feedback.js|here]]. --'''''[[User:The New Mikemoral|The New]]''''' [[User talk:The New Mikemoral|Mikemoral]] [[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 02:03, 21 January 2010 (UTC) Is there anyone still supporting this idea? --[[User:The New Mikemoral|Mike]][[User talk:The New Mikemoral|moral]][[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 04:14, 17 February 2010 (UTC) :Fix the link? [[User:Griffinofwales|Griffinofwales]] ([[User talk:Griffinofwales|talk]]) 00:37, 18 February 2010 (UTC) ::What about the link? --[[User:The New Mikemoral|Mike]][[User talk:The New Mikemoral|moral]][[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 01:48, 18 February 2010 (UTC) :::It's a redlink. [[User:Griffinofwales|Griffinofwales]] ([[User talk:Griffinofwales|talk]]) 03:26, 18 February 2010 (UTC) ::::Weird. [http://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/User:Conrad.Irwin/feedback.js I'll try the full URL]. --[[User:The New Mikemoral|Mike]][[User talk:The New Mikemoral|moral]][[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 05:39, 18 February 2010 (UTC) :::::Sounds like a great idea to me. [[User:Griffinofwales|Griffinofwales]] ([[User talk:Griffinofwales|talk]]) 14:22, 18 February 2010 (UTC) ::::::Agreed, go for it. [[User:Tempodivalse|'''Tempodivalse''']] [[User talk:Tempodivalse#top|[talk]]] 20:33, 18 February 2010 (UTC) {{outdent}} Yup, good idea. [[user:Pmlineditor|'''Pmlineditor''']] [[user talk:Pmlineditor|'''∞''']] 07:58, 19 February 2010 (UTC) :I asked [[:en:User:Conrad.Irwin|User:Conrad.Irwin]] at en.wikt to see how it should be set up for simple.wikt. --[[User:The New Mikemoral|Mike]][[User talk:The New Mikemoral|moral]][[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 00:39, 20 February 2010 (UTC) ::{{done|Enabled}}. [[user:Pmlineditor|'''Pmlineditor''']] [[user talk:Pmlineditor|'''∞''']] 09:50, 27 February 2010 (UTC) :::I set up [[WT:FEED]]. --[[User:The New Mikemoral|Mike]][[User talk:The New Mikemoral|moral]][[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 18:57, 27 February 2010 (UTC) == Internet memes == Hi there all. Instead of writing individual entries for every Internet meme, I think that we should write one central list of Internet memes, and redirect all of the individual memes to the centralized list of memes. That is the way that the English Wiktionary does it. Any thoughts on this? [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 16:19, 20 January 2010 (UTC) :Individuals entries on listed on a single appendix perhaps? --'''''[[User:The New Mikemoral|The New]]''''' [[User talk:The New Mikemoral|Mikemoral]] [[Special:Contributions/The New Mikemoral|♪♫]] 02:06, 21 January 2010 (UTC) == Most wanted pages. == I've made an experimental list of most wanted pages at [[User:Wenli/Most wanted]]. This list is intended to combine [[User:Creol/Most wanted]] with [[User:Tygrrr/Pages Simple English Wikipedia says we have]], using updated data from database dumps. I think that using link data from the Simple Wikipedia more acurately reflects which pages are "most wanted", rather than using local link data. — '''[[User:Wenli|Wenli]]''' ([[User talk:Wenli|reply here]]) 07:46, 22 January 2010 (UTC) :Seems to be a good idea. -[[User:Barras|'''Barras''']] [[User Talk:Barras|'''talk''']] 14:00, 22 January 2010 (UTC) :I like the inclusion of this page. It will help our cause more :). Cheers, [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 22:05, 22 January 2010 (UTC) :Very good idea. Thanks for creating the list. [[User:Griffinofwales|Griffinofwales]] ([[User talk:Griffinofwales|talk]]) 22:07, 22 January 2010 (UTC) ::Sounds good, better than a popular list based on local links. [[User:Tempodivalse|'''Tempodivalse''']] [[User talk:Tempodivalse#top|[talk]]] 14:59, 4 February 2010 (UTC) ==Plural== how can the word favorite be pluralized :Favorites? [[user:Pmlineditor|'''Pmlineditor''']] [[user talk:Pmlineditor|'''∞''']] 11:18, 4 February 2010 (UTC) == Audio bot == I'm running my audio bot [[User:DerbethBot|DerbethBot]] now. If you have time, please take a look at its edits and let me know if anything is not ok. --[[User:Derbeth|Derbeth]] [[User talk:Derbeth|talk]] 23:23, 31 January 2010 (UTC) :If it is already flagged, then chances are that its' edits were approved already, but I'll take a further look at them to determine if they are good for this site or not. Cheers, [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 00:34, 1 February 2010 (UTC) :Finished looking at about 10 of its' edits, and there is just one very small detail that would help: Could you have your bot add a space in between the asterisk and the start of the audio template? :Example: *_{{audio Thanks, [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 00:37, 1 February 2010 (UTC) :: As far as I can see, in 'Pronunciation' section usually there is no space after asterisk, see [[always]]. --[[User:Derbeth|Derbeth]] [[User talk:Derbeth|talk]] 23:30, 1 February 2010 (UTC) :::Gah! That needs to be fixed, then :) Hmm...I need to go figure out how to fix that. Cheers, [[User:Razorflame|Razor]][[User talk:Razorflame|flame]] 09:40, 2 February 2010 (UTC) :: I can set my bot to do some simple cosmetic work at the same time it adds audio files - so it can add correctly indented audio entries and fix indentation in 'Pronunciation' section. I only need to know for sure, it should be done according to current rules. :) --[[User:Derbeth|Derbeth]] [[User talk:Derbeth|talk]] 13:28, 2 February 2010 (UTC) :::At least I do normally add an underscore between the asterisk and the coming thing. I think it would be fine this way. Please do some test edits with the new settings and give me (or any other crat) a hint to approve the bot for this task as well. Regards, -[[User:Barras|'''Barras''']] [[User Talk:Barras|'''talk''']] 20:41, 2 February 2010 (UTC) : Please review the latest edits of my bot. --[[User:Derbeth|Derbeth]] [[User talk:Derbeth|talk]] 23:48, 3 February 2010 (UTC) :: Think they are fine, but I'm not one of the godly crats. ;) [[user:Pmlineditor|'''Pmlineditor''']] [[user talk:Pmlineditor|'''∞''']] 11:18, 4 February 2010 (UTC) *Looks all fine. I'm going to say that this bot is for the new task '''approved'''. The bot is already flagged by Brett last year. Regards, -[[User:Barras (de)|Barras (de)]] ([[User talk:Barras (de)|talk]]) 11:41, 4 February 2010 (UTC) == Emergency sysops == Hi there! Well, last night we had an incident with crosswiki socks and troll (all blocked last night). The problem is that we only have fairly inactive administrators here on this wiki. I talked last night to [[w:User:Fr33kman|Fr33kman]], a crat/cu on simpleWP, to give out the sysop tool for Wiktionary to some of the regulars on WP who are also often around on IRC especially in the cvn-simplewikis countervandalism channel. The people I'm thinking about are [[w:User:Juliancolton|Juliancolton]] (admin@multiple projects including enwiki, meta and crat@simpleWP), [[w:User:Jamesofur|Jamesofur]] (cu@simpleWP, sysop@meta), [[w:User:PeterSymonds|PeterSymonds]] (sysop@multiple projects including enwiki, simpleWP), [[w:User:User:Bsadowski1|Bsadowski1]] (sysop@simpleWP) and [[w:User:Fr33kman|Fr33kman]] (crat/cu@simpleWP). To some of them I've talked already about this on IRC and to some others will do this soon to ensure they agree with having the flag here. They all will only be allowed to use the tools if clearly '''no''' regular sysop is around to handle this and also only if it is urgent. This means they shouldn't do regular deletion when there is no rush to do it. I think I'll give out the flags this evening even if no one agrees or opposes in this short time here. I think this is beneficial for our project to ensure that it keeps clean. If someone strongest disagrees with one of the mentioned user, so please say it here and give a reason why he shouldn't have the tools even if the comment is after I granted the tools. It is not a problem to remove the tools after they were granted (Just in this case, I would take care of it). I hope you understand my reasoning. Kindly -[[User:Barras|'''Barras''']] [[User Talk:Barras|'''talk''']] 12:28, 14 February 2010 (UTC) :I support this proposal since in SimpleWikt, (like many other small wikis) vandals get full freedom to vandalize/troll at the times when no admin is available. If we hand out sysop to some trusted members of the SimpleWP community, it will surely help Wikt. [[user:Pmlineditor|'''Pmlineditor''']] [[user talk:Pmlineditor|'''∞''']] 12:39, 14 February 2010 (UTC) ::I'd be honored to help. :) –'''[[User:Juliancolton|Juliancolton]]''' | [[User_talk:Juliancolton|''Talk'']] 15:01, 14 February 2010 (UTC) :::Looks like I misunderstood what Barras meant to say... fwiw, I support emergency admins; however, I think that there should be a short discussion at RfA before the crat grants the right, even if it be for 24 hours. I don't want a crat granting admin to users citing "trust" as is done in the case of rollback. Some of these users may not have the community's trust. I don't want sysoppings and running in search of stewards to desysop X/Y/Z since they distrust the user. [[user:Pmlineditor|'''Pmlineditor''']] [[user talk:Pmlineditor|'''∞''']] 15:19, 14 February 2010 (UTC) {{outdent}} Striking per private discussion with the user who proposed this. [[user:Pmlineditor|'''Pmlineditor''']] [[user talk:Pmlineditor|'''∞''']] 15:30, 14 February 2010 (UTC) The threat is overblown. The simple English Wiktionary has never had a big problem with vandalism and though stewards have stepped in upon occasion, the vandalism would have lasted only a few hour without their intervention. That doesn't seem to be a big deal. On the other hand, giving other people the ability to stop vandalism doesn't seem a big deal either.--[[User:Brett|Brett]] ([[User talk:Brett|talk]]) 15:57, 14 February 2010 (UTC) :Yes, it is true that we don't get many vandals here, but if they come here, so do their best to do as many damage as possible and it is much easier to when we get them when they start instead of doing a "one-hour-cleaning-up" afterwards. When vandals discover a wiki is kinda empty and no one seems to be around to stop them, they vandalize even more. [[User:Barras|'''Barras''']] [[User Talk:Barras|'''talk''']] 16:04, 14 February 2010 (UTC) :Btw, if the Global sysop proposal passes, they will have the same ability as sysops on this wiki. So we "appoint" people we want instead of having unknown people using the sysop tool here. -[[User:Barras|'''Barras''']] [[User Talk:Barras|'''talk''']] 16:34, 14 February 2010 (UTC) ::GS likely is going to fail. –'''[[User:Juliancolton|Juliancolton]]''' | [[User_talk:Juliancolton|''Talk'']] 16:37, 14 February 2010 (UTC) :::Possibly, I don't think it's done yet but it will depend on a coupel things. [[regulateeing]]? *What should I have done differently? *What do I need to know so that I could have fixed the error I created? :do this: {{verb|regulat|e}}--[[User:Brett|Brett]] ([[User talk:Brett|talk]]) 21:20, 1 April 2010 (UTC) :By the way, ''regulated'' is a verb, not an adjective. I had two purposes: (a) to use the word in a real sentence and (b) to provide an opportunity for open-ended constructive feedback like you have now offered. I did check a few dictionaries which only show "regulated" as a verb -- not an adjective. Is it relevant that these related words function like an adjective in the sample sentences? == Noun == {{noun4}} # {{uncountable}} '''Criminality''' is the state of being [[criminal]]. #: ''If things do not change, we will descend into an unending darkness of corruption, '''criminality''', murder, and reprisal.'' <ref>Date 2009 Publication information New York : Henry Holt and Company, Edition: 1st ed. revision.text:
=== Other spellings === * {{UK}} [[mould]]
=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|mŏld|mōld}} * {{UK}} {{IPA|/məʊld/|/mɔʊld/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/moʊld/}} * {{audio|en-us-mould.ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Noun 1 == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''mold''' is a [[hollow]] [[form]] in which a [[liquid]] or [[plastic]] object is made. #: ''The metal sword was made using a '''mold'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''mold''' is a [[frame]] or [[model]] around which an [[object]] is made. #: ''The gel dummy was made using a '''mold'''.'' # {{countable}} A '''mold''' is the [[shape]] or [[pattern]] of a mold. # {{countable}} A '''mold''' is a [[general]] shape or form of something. # {{countable}} A '''mold''' is a particular [[character]] or [[type]] of something.
=== Related words === * [[molding]]
== Noun 2 == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''mold''' is a natural [[furry]] [[growth]] of small [[fungi|fungus]] that appears when living [[material]] is left out in the open. #: ''Because the bread was left out overnight, '''mold''' grew on it.''
=== Related words === * [[moldy]] * [[moldiness]] * [[moldily]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If you '''mold''' something, you make it in a mold. # {{transitive}} If you '''mold''' something, you shape it into a [[particular]] form or shape. #: ''The molten metal was '''molded''' into a sword.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''mold''' something, you [[guide]] the growth or [[development]] of someone. #: ''A teacher '''molds''' their students into educated adults.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''mold''' something, you [[decorate]] it with [[molding]]s. #: ''The interior of the house was '''molded''' today.''
=== Related words === * [[molder]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === ; adjective * {{IPA|/ˈdɛsələt/}} * {{audio|en-us-desolate.ogg|Audio (US)}} ; verb * {{IPA|/ˈdɛsəleɪt/}}
== Adjective == {{adj|more=true}} # If a place is '''desolate''', it is [[deserted]]; nobody [[live]]s in that place. #: ''The area around the cave is '''desolate''' and filled with jagged rocks.'' # If a place is '''desolate''', it is [[barren]]; nothing lives there; it is [[lifeless]]. #: ''The tundra is a '''desolate''' place.'' # If a place is '''desolate''', it is not [[fit]] to [[use]] or live in; it is [[unfit]] for use. # If something is '''desolate''', it is [[dismal]] or [[dreary]]. #: ''The abandoned house looks very '''desolate'''.'' # If something or someone is '''desolate''', they are [[sad]], [[forlorn]], or [[hopeless]].
== Verb == {{verb|desolat|e}} # {{transitive}} If you '''desolate''' a place, you [[devastate]] it; you [[lay waste]] to it. #: ''The city was '''desolated''' during the war.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''desolate''' something, you [[abandon]] it; you [[forsake]] it. # {{transitive}} If you '''desolate''' a place, you take away any [[life]] living there. # {{transitive}} If you '''desolate''' someone, you make them [[sad]], [[forlorn]], or [[hopeless]].
=== Related words === * [[desolation]]

==Adjective== {{adjective}} # If something is '''nonobscene''', it is not [[obscene]]; it is not [[vulgar]], [[lewd]], [[disgusting]], [[lustful]], or [[revolting]]. #: ''The video was '''nonobscene'''.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/krʊk/}} * {{audio|EN-AU ck1 crook.ogg|Audio (AU)}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''crook''' is a person who [[steal]]s things, [[lie]]s, [[cheat]]s, or does other things which are against the [[law]]; they are a [[criminal]]. # {{countable}} A '''crook''' is a [[bend]].
=== Synonyms === * {{sense|criminal}} [[criminal]] * {{sense|bend}} [[bend]], [[curve]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{transitive}} If someone '''crook'''s something, they [[bend]] it; they [[curve]] it.
=== Synonyms === * [[bend]] * [[curve]]
=== Related words === * [[crooked]] * [[crookedness]] * [[crookedly]]
{{exstub}}

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ɪkˈspɛl/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-expel.wav|UK}} * {{hyph|ex|pel}}
== Verb == {{verb|expel|l}} # {{transitive}} If someone is '''expelled''', they are no longer a [[member]] of a [[group]] or [[organization]]. #: ''He was '''expelled''' from school.'' # {{transitive}} If someone '''expels''' a person, they force them to leave a [[country]]; they [[deport]] them. # {{transitive}} If someone or something is '''expelled''', they are thrown out; they are [[ejected]]; it [[erupted]].
=== Synonyms === * {{sense|forced to leave a country}} [[deport]] * {{sense|thrown out}} [[eject]]ed, [[erupt]]ed
=== Antonyms === * [[impel]]
=== Related words === * [[expulsion]]

===Pronunciation=== * {{audio|en-us-spontaneous.ogg|Audio (US)}} * {{hyphenation|spon|ta|ne|ous}}
==Adjective== {{adjective|more=true}} # If something is '''spontaneous''', it happens without any [[outside]] [[cause]]; nothing else [[make]]s it happen. #: ''He made a '''spontaneous''' offer to help the old lady cross the street.'' # If something is '''spontaneous''', it is [[random]]. # If something is '''spontaneous''', it happens [[suddenly]]; it happens without any [[warning]]. # If someone does something in a '''spontaneous''' way, it is done of their own [[free]] [[will]] or without making any [[plan]] to do so. # If something is '''spontaneous''', it was [[made]] without being [[plant]]ed by [[human]]s; it is [[indigenous]].
===Synonyms=== * {{sense|done of their own free will}} [[unplanned]] * {{sense|random}} [[random]] * {{sense|made without human work}} [[indigenous]]
===Related words=== * [[spontaneity]] * [[spontaneously]] * [[spontaneousness]]

=== Pronunciation === * {{IPA|/ˈbreɪkdaʊn/}} * {{audio|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-breakdown.wav|UK}} * {{hyph|break|down}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''breakdown''' is when something has [[fail]]ed, usually having to do with a [[machine]] of some sort. #: ''The car they were driving had a '''breakdown''' when the engine stopped working.'' # {{countable}} A '''breakdown''' is when someone's [[state]] of [[mind]] has fallen apart or [[lapse]]d. # {{countable}} A '''breakdown''' of something is a [[list]] or a breaking up of something into {{r|categor|ies}} in great [[detail]].
=== Related words === * [[nervous breakdown]] <!-- This link can stay a redlink for a good period of time. It isn't important to make it now, but it can be made later, once we've made a bunch of the more common words. -->
=== Related words === * [[break down]]

revision.text:
== Verb == {{verb|break down|breaks down|broke down|broke down|breaking down}} {{verb|break down|breaks down|broken down|broken down|breaking down}} # {{transitive}} If something '''breaks down''', it [[fail]]s, usually having to do with a [[machine]] of some kind. #: ''As Betty was driving, her car '''broke down''' in the middle of the road.'' # {{transitive}} If something living '''breaks down''', it [[decay]]s; it [[decomposes]]. # {{transitive}} If someone '''breaks down''', they become [[unstable]], either in their [[mind]] or some other way. # {{transitive}} If information or something else is '''broken down''', it is [[given]] in great [[detail]].
===Synonyms=== * {{sense|fails, usually about machines}} [[fail]] * {{sense|decomposes}} [[decompose]], [[decay]]
=== Related words === * [[breakdown]]

revision.text:
=== Pronunciation === * {{enPR|bŭmp}}, {{IPA|/bʌmp/}} * {{audio|en-au-bump.ogg|AU}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''bump''' is a small [[impact]] between two things. #: ''I felt a slight '''bump''' as the plane touched the landing strip.'' # {{countable}} A '''bump''' is a [[sound]] that might be made when two things [[hit]] each other. #: ''I looked up when I heard the '''bump''' of a car as it drove into another one parked outside my house.'' # {{countable}} A '''bump''' is a small [[lump]] or [[swelling]] on something that is [[smooth]]. #: ''Try to drive round the big '''bump''' in the road.'' # {{countable}} {{medicine}} A '''bump''' is a small [[lump]] or [[swelling]] on the [[skin]] or anywhere else on your body. #: ''I rubbed the small '''bump''' on my nose, and wondered if it was going to get any bigger.''
=== Related words === * [[bumper]]
== Verb == {{verb}} # {{intransitive}} If something '''bumps''', it [[knocks]] gently against something else, usually making a small noise. #: ''I could hear the open door '''bumping''' in the breeze.'' # {{transitive}} If you '''bump''' something, you [[knock]] it slightly. #: ''He '''bumped''' the chair as he walked past, so I put it back in place again.''

=== Pronunciation === * {{UK}} {{IPA|/ˈjəʊ.jəʊ/}} * {{US}} {{IPA|/ˈjoʊ.joʊ/}} * {{audio|en-us-yo-yo.ogg|Audio (US)}}
== Noun == {{noun}} # {{countable}} A '''yo-yo''' is a toy that spins and goes up and down, hanging from a string. #: ''Let's go play with my '''yo-yo'''.''
<gallery> File:Wooden yo-yo.jpg File:Us yoyo national 1a.jpg File:Bundesarchiv Bild 146-1985-101-36A, Berlin, Jo Jo-Spiel.jpg File:Butterfly design yoyo 0655.jpg </gallery>
[[Category:Toys]]

=== Other spellings === * [[tin foil]]
== Noun == {{noun4}} # {{uncountable}} '''Tinfoil''' is a piece of [[tin]] which is flat and thin like [[paper]]. Sometimes people say "tinfoil" when they really mean "aluminium foil", which is made of a different metal, [[aluminium]], instead of tin. [[File:ManInaTinfoilHat.jpg|thumb|A tinfoil hat]]
==Noun== {{noun}} # A '''red-light district''' is the part of [[town]] where [[prostitute]]s are found. #: ''His wife was upset when she found out he had been to the '''red-light district'''.''

revision.text:
===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|/dæʃ/}} * {{audio|en-us-dash.ogg|Audio (US)}}
==Noun== {{noun|dash|dashes}} [[File:Dashboard BX.jpg|thumb|The wheel and dash ([[dashboard]]) of a car.]] # On a computer [[keyboard]], a '''dash''' is a [[horizontal bar]] that looks like "-" or "—". #: ''There are many different types of '''dashes''' that you can type on a keyboard.'' # A '''dash''' can mean a short [[run]]. #: ''I got last place in the 100-meter '''dash''' because I tripped on a rock.'' # A '''dash''' is sometimes short for a [[dashboard]]. #: ''Someone dropped a brick through the car's windshield and onto the '''dash'''.'' # A '''dash''' is a very small amount in cooking. #: ''Put a '''dash''' of salt in the soup.''
===Related words=== * [[en dash]] * [[em dash]] * [[dashboard]]
==Verb== {{verb|dash|es}} # {{intransitive}} To '''dash''' is to [[run]] fast for a short [[distance]] #: ''When he heard there was ice cream he '''dashed''' off towards it.'' # {{transitive}} If your hopes, dreams, or expectations were [[ruin]]ed, [[disappoint]]ed, or [[destroy]]ed, they were '''dashed'''. #: ''Her hopes for a beautiful wedding day were '''dashed''' when dark clouds gathered in the sky.'' #: ''My dreams of a happy, quiet home were '''dashed''' when my mother in law moved in with us.'' # {{transitive}} To '''dash''' can be to [[sprinkle]] or [[spray]]. #: ''She '''dashed''' her soup with too much pepper.''

{{#tag:imagemap| File:{{{image|Image-missing.svg}}}{{!}}{{{width|310}}}x{{{height|{{{width|310}}}}}}px100px{{!}}{{{text|{{PAGENAME}}}}}{{!}}alt={{{text|{{PAGENAME}}}}} {{#if:{{{imagemap|}}}| {{{imagemap}}} | rect 0 0 1 1 [[{{PAGENAME}}]] }}}} {{#if:{{{labels|}}}|{{{labels}}}}}
|- |{{#if:{{{scrollable|}}}|

}} |} Use this template to add a [[picture dictionary]] to an entry. '''Parameters''' for this template: ;image :Image that describes the entry. ;detail1 : Any content, in most cases clickable image(s) describing a [[hypernym]]. : A clickable image can be inserted by adding a line with [[template:picdicimg]] for each image. '''Optional parameters''' ;detail2 ;detail3 ;detail4 : Any content, in most cases clickable images describing the [[hyponym]]s. : A clickable image can be inserted by adding a line with [[template:picdicimg]] for each image. : detail2, detail3 and detail4 are optional, in that case [[hyponym]]s should be described elsewhere. : Within parameters detail1, detail2, detail3 and detail4 the full wiki syntax can be used. The only restriction is the use of the | character in tables (and complex templates). That character should be replaced by the template {{!}}. For tables {|, |-, |, ||, |} etc. should be replaced by {{{!}}, {{!}}-, {{!}}, {{!}}{{!}}, {{!}}} etc. Alternatively the [[w:Help:Table#Other_table_syntax|(X)HTML syntax for tables]] can be used like <table><tr><td> </td></tr></table>. ;scrollable : Fill scrollable=yes to have a scroll bar at the bottom of the details ;text :The name of the entry. The default value is the page name of the entry. ;width :Maximum width of the image. :This parameter is optional, the default width is 310. ;height :Maximum height of the image. :This parameter is optional, the default height is 310. ;imagemap : This parameter is optional, and only to be used in case of an image map instead of other visual content describing the [[hyponym]]s. : The parameter imagemap cannot be used in combination with the parameter labels : To use image maps this parameter should be filled with a valid defintion of the imagemap areas. : The coordinates are the number of pixels from the upper-left-hand corner of the default size of the image, so are '''independent''' of the size shown on screen. : Example of this parameter:
::imagemap= ::circle 1035 572 13 [[Mercury]] ::circle 860 483 234 [[Sun]]
: A tutorial to use image maps can be found at [[:w:en:Wikipedia:Wikipedia Signpost/2008-03-03/Tutorial|Wikipedia:Wikipedia Signpost/2008-03-03]]. ;labels : This parameter is optional, and only to be used in case of text labels to be inserted on the main image instead of other visual content describing the [[hyponym]]s. : The parameter labels cannot be used in combination with the parameter imagemap : The labels itself should be inserted by adding a line with [[template:picdiclabel]] for each label. : The coordinates are the number of pixels from the upper-left-hand corner of the visable size of the image, so are '''dependent''' of the size shown on screen. See the template for further info. : Examples of this parameter:
::labels= ::{{ picdiclabel | posx=181 | posy= 86 | link=Sun }} ::{{ picdiclabel | posx=214 | posy=119 | link=Mercury | align=right }}

'''Parameters''' for this template: ;image :Image that describes the entry. ;link :The name of the entry, used for linking to the wiktionary entry (the caption, as well as the image!).
'''Optional parameters''' <!-- ;lang :The ISO code of the language of the entry, used for linking within the wiktionary entry :This parameter is optional, the default is "en", resulting in an anchor #English (as this is used througout wiktionary) --> ;anchor :A section within the entry, used for linking to a section within the wiktionary entry :This parameter is optional<!--, the default is the language name of the ISO language specified by the lang parameter (#English) --> ;altlink :The alternate text shown for the entry. :This parameter is optional, the default is the text of the link parameter. ;width :Maximum width of the image. :This parameter is optional, the default width is 150. The actual with is probably less as the default height is 75. ;height :Maximum height of the image. The height of the image is crucial for an appealing alignment of a series of images. :This parameter is optional, the default height is 75. This value is used to make the height parameter the limiting factor for many images.
</noinclude>
